results.name: SOC Alert Sweeper
results.description:
Full autonomous pipeline orchestrator. Sweeps untriaged alerts every 5 minutes, then runs unified triage (classify + enrich + investigate in a single agent call) → Tiered Response → Case Creation.
Reliability invariants (T2 hardening): - Atomic pipeline lock via `elasticsearch.create` on a deterministic document id.
  Two concurrent runs cannot both succeed (version conflict = skip).
- on_failure release: the pipeline lock is released whether the run succeeds or fails. - ai.agent steps have on_failure routing to .soc-dead-letter with run_id + stage. - ms-precision timestamps + run_id salt on every document so docs never collide
  inside the same wall-clock second.

Data-model invariants (T1): - Dispositions are DERIVED from the triage agent output, never hardcoded
  ("case_created" is not a disposition — it is a pipeline state).
- Per-alert triage fields (classification, confidence, disposition, kill_chain_stage,
  threat_category) are FLATTENED at the top level of `.soc-triage-results`
  (one doc per alert) so dashboards can aggregate without reaching into
  triage_output.*.

Correctness invariants: - attach_alerts groups alerts by rule.uuid so a heterogeneous batch of alerts
  produces one case-comment per rule (previously assumed homogeneous batch).
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Alert Sweeper
description: >
  Full autonomous pipeline orchestrator. Sweeps untriaged alerts every 5 minutes,
  then runs unified triage (classify + enrich + investigate in a single agent call) →
  Tiered Response → Case Creation.

  Reliability invariants (T2 hardening):
  - Atomic pipeline lock via `elasticsearch.create` on a deterministic document id.
    Two concurrent runs cannot both succeed (version conflict = skip).
  - on_failure release: the pipeline lock is released whether the run succeeds or fails.
  - ai.agent steps have on_failure routing to .soc-dead-letter with run_id + stage.
  - ms-precision timestamps + run_id salt on every document so docs never collide
    inside the same wall-clock second.

  Data-model invariants (T1):
  - Dispositions are DERIVED from the triage agent output, never hardcoded
    ("case_created" is not a disposition — it is a pipeline state).
  - Per-alert triage fields (classification, confidence, disposition, kill_chain_stage,
    threat_category) are FLATTENED at the top level of `.soc-triage-results`
    (one doc per alert) so dashboards can aggregate without reaching into
    triage_output.*.

  Correctness invariants:
  - attach_alerts groups alerts by rule.uuid so a heterogeneous batch of alerts
    produces one case-comment per rule (previously assumed homogeneous batch).
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 5m
  - type: manual

consts:
  # ms-precision + run-id salt. Used as lock id AND correlation_id.
  cycle_id:   "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
  pipeline_id: "soc-alert-sweeper"
  now_iso:    "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"

steps:
  # ── Stage -2: Evict stale locks ────────────────────────────────────
  # A crashed cycle or a Kibana restart can leave a lock doc behind. Before we
  # try to acquire, sweep any lock for this pipeline whose acquired_at is older
  # than the TTL. This is idempotent: a fresh lock is never old enough to match.
  # Without this the pipeline can hang forever on a single stuck cycle -- which
  # is exactly what happened in the 2026-04-17 demo soak (5h dead-lock).
  - name: evict_stale_locks
    type: elasticsearch.request
    with:
      method: POST
      path: "/.soc-pipeline-lock/_delete_by_query?refresh=true"
      body:
        query:
          bool:
            filter:
              - term: { pipeline: "soc-alert-sweeper" }
              - range:
                  acquired_at:
                    # TTL must be SHORTER than the cron cadence (5m) or a crashed
                    # cycle wedges the next tick. 3m gives the current run time to
                    # finish (most cycles < 60s) while still guaranteeing the next
                    # tick evicts a dead lock.
                    lt: "now-3m"
    on_failure:
      - name: log_evict_failed
        type: console
        with:
          message: "Stale-lock eviction failed (non-fatal) — acquire will still TOCTOU-guard via op_type=create."

  # ── Stage -1: Atomic pipeline lock ─────────────────────────────────
  # `elasticsearch.create` uses op_type=create, so if a doc with the same id
  # already exists, it fails with version_conflict_engine_exception. That is
  # our atomic "someone else holds the lock" signal — no TOCTOU race.
  - name: acquire_lock
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-pipeline-lock
      id: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
      op_type: create
      document:
        pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
        cycle_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
        status: active
        acquired_at: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
    on_failure:
      - name: lock_held_metric
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-metrics
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
            cycle_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
            alerts_processed: 0
            stages_completed: ""
            case_created: false
            status: "skipped_locked"
      - name: log_lock_held
        type: console
        with:
          message: "Pipeline: another instance holds the lock (cycle_id=cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}) — skipping."
      - name: end_locked
        type: console
        with:
          message: "Pipeline locked — exiting cleanly."
        end: true

  # ── Stage 0: Find untriaged alerts ─────────────────────────────────
  # NOTE: workflow engine strips body: wrapper — keep ES params flat under with:
  - name: get_open_alerts
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".alerts-security.alerts-*"
      size: 5
      query:
        bool:
          must:
            - term:
                kibana.alert.workflow_status: open
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-6m"
          must_not:
            - term:
                kibana.alert.workflow_tags: soc-triaged
      _source:
        - kibana.alert.rule.name
        - kibana.alert.rule.uuid
        - kibana.alert.severity
        - kibana.alert.rule.threat
        - host.hostname
        - host.name
        - process.name
        - process.args
        - user.name
        - event.action
        - source.ip
        - destination.ip
        - "@timestamp"

  - name: log_alert_count
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Pipeline: found {{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.total.value }} untriaged alerts (cycle_id=cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }})."

  # Gate: has_alerts? Must emit 'yes' or 'no' and be consumed by every
  # downstream alert-dependent step. The older `if: ... value: 0` + `end: true`
  # pattern was load-bearing for ~3mo but `end: true` does NOT actually halt
  # the workflow; subsequent steps kept firing with empty inputs (notably
  # `tag_triaged`, which POSTs ids=[] and is rejected HTTP 400 by
  # /api/detection_engine/signals/tags). The explicit gate is the only
  # reliable way to express "skip the rest of the pipeline" in the
  # current workflow engine (verified 2026-04-17 soak).
  - name: gate_has_alerts
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {% if steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.total.value == 0 %}no{% else %}yes{% endif %}

  # Early-exit branch when there are no open alerts. Each step is guarded
  # independently because `end: true` is not load-bearing.
  - name: write_metrics_no_alerts
    type: elasticsearch.index
    if: "steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.total.value: 0"
    with:
      index: .soc-metrics
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
        cycle_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
        alerts_processed: 0
        stages_completed: ""
        case_created: false
        status: "skipped_no_alerts"

  - name: release_lock_no_alerts
    type: elasticsearch.request
    if: "steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.total.value: 0"
    with:
      method: DELETE
      path: "/.soc-pipeline-lock/_doc/{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
    on_failure:
      - name: log_release_failed_no_alerts
        type: console
        with:
          message: "Warning: failed to release pipeline lock on no-alerts path (cycle_id=cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}). Next cycle will overwrite on acquire."

  - name: log_no_alerts
    type: console
    if: "steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.total.value: 0"
    with:
      message: "Pipeline: no untriaged alerts found — lock released, exiting."
    end: true

  # ── Stage 0b: Pre-triage correlation (group related alerts) ───────
  - name: correlate_alerts
    type: elasticsearch.search
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      index: ".alerts-security.alerts-*"
      size: 5
      query:
        bool:
          must:
            - terms:
                _id: "${{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.hits | map: '_id' }}"
      aggregations:
        by_host:
          terms:
            field: "host.name"
            size: 10
          aggs:
            techniques:
              terms:
                field: "kibana.alert.rule.threat.technique.id"
                size: 20
            time_range:
              stats:
                field: "@timestamp"
        by_user:
          terms:
            field: "user.name"
            size: 10
          aggs:
            techniques:
              terms:
                field: "kibana.alert.rule.threat.technique.id"
                size: 20
        by_source_ip:
          terms:
            field: "source.ip"
            size: 10

  - name: log_correlation
    type: console
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      message: "Pipeline: pre-triage correlation complete."

  # ── Stage 1: Unified Triage ────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: triage
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-triage-agent
    connector-id: opus
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      message: >
        Run the full triage pipeline on these security alerts. Execute ALL applicable phases:

        **Phase 1 — Classification**: For EACH alert classify as TRUE_POSITIVE, FALSE_POSITIVE,
        or SUSPICIOUS with confidence 0-100. Use ES|QL to check for related alerts from the same
        hosts/users/IPs within a 30-minute window.

        **Phase 2 — Entity Enrichment**: For alerts with confidence >= 40, enrich with entity
        context. Query 7-day behavioral baselines, entity risk scores, and relationships.
        Adjust confidence based on entity context.

        **Phase 3 — Deep Investigation**: For alerts still ambiguous (confidence 40-69) after
        enrichment, conduct structured threat hunts. Formulate hypotheses, run ES|QL queries
        for process trees, network timelines, lateral movement. Search Security Labs for IOC intel.

        **Phase 4 — Attack Chain Correlation**: For TRUE_POSITIVE or SUSPICIOUS alerts with
        confidence >= 50, use security.attack_discovery_search to check for attack discoveries.
        Look for kill chain progression across alerts sharing the same host/user/IP.

        Pre-triage correlation data:
        {{ steps.correlate_alerts.output.aggregations | json }}

        Final next_step per alert:
        - confidence >= 40 → "response" (create case)
        - confidence < 40 → "close" (likely FP)

        **Self-validation**: Verify every input alert has a classification, confidence is 0-100,
        disposition is one of the enumerated values (NEVER "case_created" or "triaged" — those are
        pipeline states, not dispositions), and all required fields are populated.

        Alerts:
        {{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Respond ONLY with JSON:
        {"classifications": [{"alert_id": "<_id>",
          "classification": "TRUE_POSITIVE|FALSE_POSITIVE|SUSPICIOUS",
          "confidence": N,
          "next_step": "response|close",
          "reasoning": "...",
          "mitre_techniques": ["Txxxx"],
          "disposition": "TRUE_POSITIVE|BENIGN_TRUE_POSITIVE|FALSE_POSITIVE|POLICY_VIOLATION|INCONCLUSIVE|DUPLICATE",
          "threat_category": "commodity_malware|targeted_attack|insider_threat|misuse|unauthorized_access|data_exfiltration|lateral_movement|persistence|reconnaissance|unknown",
          "kill_chain_stage": "reconnaissance|weaponization|delivery|exploitation|installation|c2|actions_on_objectives|unknown",
          "business_impact": {"data_at_risk": [], "systems_at_risk": 0, "criticality": "low|medium|high|critical"},
          "attack_chain": {"chain_id": "...", "position_in_chain": 0, "chain_length": 0, "related_alert_ids": []},
          "entities_enriched": [{"entity_id": "...", "risk_score": 0, "behavioral_anomalies": []}],
          "hypotheses_tested": [{"hypothesis": "...", "verdict": "CORROBORATED|REFUTED|INCONCLUSIVE"}],
          "confidence_history": [{"phase": "classification", "confidence": N}],
          "evidence_summary": "key findings"}],
        "validation_errors": []}
    timeout: 600s
    on_failure:
      - name: dlq_triage
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-dead-letter
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            stage: triage
            pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
            cycle_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
            error: "{{ workflow.last_error | default: 'unknown' }}"
            input_alerts: "{{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.hits | json }}"
      - name: release_lock_triage_failed
        type: elasticsearch.request
        with:
          method: DELETE
          path: "/.soc-pipeline-lock/_doc/{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
      - name: end_triage_failed
        type: console
        with:
          message: "Pipeline: triage failed, DLQ written, lock released — exiting."
        end: true

  # Write the RAW triage output once (for reasoning-trace/dashboard).
  # NOTE: Kibana's ai.agent step returns `{ message: "<raw-JSON-string>" }` — the
  # agent's JSON body is in `.message`, not at the root of `.output`. We must
  # unwrap it via `| json_parse` before writing, otherwise the dashboard sees
  # `{"message":"{\"classifications\":[...]}"}` and parsing fails downstream.
  - name: write_triage_batch
    type: elasticsearch.index
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      index: .soc-triage-results
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        run_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
        source: "soc-alert-sweeper"
        stage: "unified_triage_batch"
        pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
        batch_size: "{{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.total.value }}"
        triage_output: "{{ steps.triage.output.message | json_parse | json }}"

  # Fan out one flattened per-alert triage doc. Dashboards filter/aggregate on
  # the top-level fields without reaching into triage_output.*.
  # The `{% assign %}` tag parses the agent envelope once so we can iterate
  # over `.classifications`; the `| json` at the end lets the foreach driver
  # JSON.parse the rendered template back into a JS array.
  # NOTE on the `| default: empty` -> `[]` fix:
  # LiquidJS's `empty` drop is an empty-object sentinel, not an empty array. When
  # `_parsed_triage.classifications` is missing or null, `default: empty` hands
  # the foreach driver `{}`, which fails with "Foreach expression must evaluate
  # to an array." This crashed the sweeper mid-cycle in the 2026-04-17 soak and
  # kept the pipeline lock held until the TTL-evict step fired (10m later).
  # The explicit `{% if %}{% else %}[]{% endif %}` branch guarantees an array.
  - name: write_triage_flattened
    type: foreach
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    foreach: "{% assign _parsed_triage = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{% if _parsed_triage.classifications %}{{ _parsed_triage.classifications | json }}{% else %}[]{% endif %}"
    steps:
      - name: write_per_alert
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-triage-results
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            run_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
            source: "soc-alert-sweeper"
            stage: "unified_triage"
            pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
            alert_id: "{{ foreach.item.alert_id }}"
            classification: "{{ foreach.item.classification | default: 'SUSPICIOUS' }}"
            confidence: "{{ foreach.item.confidence | default: 0 }}"
            disposition: "{{ foreach.item.disposition | default: 'INCONCLUSIVE' }}"
            threat_category: "{{ foreach.item.threat_category | default: 'unknown' }}"
            kill_chain_stage: "{{ foreach.item.kill_chain_stage | default: 'unknown' }}"
            mitre_techniques: "{{ foreach.item.mitre_techniques | default: empty }}"
            business_impact: "{{ foreach.item.business_impact | default: empty }}"
            attack_chain: "{{ foreach.item.attack_chain | default: empty }}"
            reasoning: "{{ foreach.item.reasoning | default: null }}"
            evidence_summary: "{{ foreach.item.evidence_summary | default: null }}"

  # Per-alert outcome materializer — writes one `.soc-outcomes` row per triaged
  # alert carrying rule_id + verdict so the Signal-Quality agent can produce
  # grounded FP evidence by grouping outcomes on rule_id.
  #
  # Why iterate over alerts (not classifications)? Alerts carry `_source.kibana.alert.rule.rule_id`
  # and `_id`, which is the join key the agent needs. The matching classification
  # is looked up via Liquid's `where` filter on the parsed triage output. If the
  # agent omitted an alert from its classifications array, we still emit a row
  # with verdict=inconclusive so the grouping never loses the alert.
  - name: write_outcomes_per_alert
    type: foreach
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    foreach: "{{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.hits }}"
    steps:
      - name: write_outcome_row
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-outcomes
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            correlation_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
            pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
            stage: "per_alert_verdict"
            alert_id: "{{ foreach.item._id }}"
            rule_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.kibana.alert.rule.rule_id | default: 'unknown' }}"
            rule_uuid: "{{ foreach.item._source.kibana.alert.rule.uuid | default: 'unknown' }}"
            rule_name: "{{ foreach.item._source.kibana.alert.rule.name | default: 'unknown' }}"
            agents_involved: ["soc-triage-agent"]
            classification: "{% assign _p = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{% assign _cl = _p.classifications | where: 'alert_id', foreach.item._id | first %}{{ _cl.classification | default: 'SUSPICIOUS' }}"
            confidence: "{% assign _p = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{% assign _cl = _p.classifications | where: 'alert_id', foreach.item._id | first %}{{ _cl.confidence | default: 0 }}"
            disposition: "{% assign _p = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{% assign _cl = _p.classifications | where: 'alert_id', foreach.item._id | first %}{{ _cl.disposition | default: 'INCONCLUSIVE' }}"
            threat_category: "{% assign _p = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{% assign _cl = _p.classifications | where: 'alert_id', foreach.item._id | first %}{{ _cl.threat_category | default: 'unknown' }}"
            kill_chain_stage: "{% assign _p = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{% assign _cl = _p.classifications | where: 'alert_id', foreach.item._id | first %}{{ _cl.kill_chain_stage | default: 'unknown' }}"
            verdict: "{% assign _p = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{% assign _cl = _p.classifications | where: 'alert_id', foreach.item._id | first %}{% assign _c = _cl.classification | default: 'UNKNOWN' %}{% if _c == 'TRUE_POSITIVE' %}true_positive{% elsif _c == 'FALSE_POSITIVE' %}false_positive{% elsif _c == 'BENIGN_POSITIVE' %}benign_positive{% elsif _c == 'SUSPICIOUS' %}suspicious{% else %}inconclusive{% endif %}"

  - name: tag_triaged
    type: kibana.request
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /api/detection_engine/signals/tags
      body:
        ids: "${{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.hits | map: '_id' }}"
        tags:
          tags_to_add:
            - soc-triaged
          tags_to_remove: []

  - name: log_triage
    type: console
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      message: "Pipeline: triage complete — {% assign _parsed_triage = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _parsed_triage.classifications | size | default: 0 }} verdicts flattened."

  # ── Stage 2: Tiered Response ──────────────────────────────────────
  - name: evaluate_response_tier
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-triage-agent
    connector-id: opus
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      message: >
        Evaluate the triage results and determine the response tier per alert.
        Use the containment-playbook skill for response decision logic.

        Response Tiers:
        - Tier 0 (OBSERVE): confidence < 40 — Close, no action
        - Tier 1 (RECORD): confidence 40-59 — Create case, tag entities
        - Tier 2 (CONTAIN): confidence 60-79 AND threat_category in [lateral_movement, data_exfiltration, unauthorized_access, persistence]
        - Tier 3 (ERADICATE): confidence >= 80 AND threat_category in [targeted_attack, data_exfiltration, commodity_malware with lateral movement]

        Triage output:
        {{ steps.triage.output | json }}

        Respond with JSON:
        {"response_plan": [{"alert_id": "...", "tier": 0-3, "tier_name": "observe|record|contain|eradicate",
          "actions": [{"action": "...", "target": "...", "requires_approval": true|false}],
          "entities_to_monitor": [], "justification": "..."}],
         "highest_tier": 0-3, "requires_human_approval": true|false}
    timeout: 120s
    on_failure:
      - name: dlq_response
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-dead-letter
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            stage: evaluate_response_tier
            pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
            cycle_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
            error: "{{ workflow.last_error | default: 'unknown' }}"
      - name: release_lock_response_failed
        type: elasticsearch.request
        with:
          method: DELETE
          path: "/.soc-pipeline-lock/_doc/{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
      - name: end_response_failed
        type: console
        with:
          message: "Pipeline: response-tier evaluation failed, DLQ written, lock released — exiting."
        end: true

  - name: write_response
    type: elasticsearch.index
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      index: .soc-response-actions
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        run_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
        source: "soc-alert-sweeper"
        pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
        stage: "tiered_response"
        response_plan: "{{ steps.evaluate_response_tier.output | json }}"
        highest_tier: "{{ steps.evaluate_response_tier.output.highest_tier | default: 0 }}"
        requires_human_approval: "{{ steps.evaluate_response_tier.output.requires_human_approval | default: false }}"
        status: "completed"

  - name: write_audit
    type: elasticsearch.index
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        run_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
        pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
        event_type: "response_action"
        source: "soc-alert-sweeper"
        stage: "tiered_response"
        status: "completed"
        reason: "Tiered response plan generated"

  - name: log_response
    type: console
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      message: "Pipeline: tiered response plan generated (highest_tier={{ steps.evaluate_response_tier.output.highest_tier | default: 0 }})."

  # ── Stage 3: Summarize for Case ───────────────────────────────────
  - name: summarize
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-triage-agent
    connector-id: opus
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      message: >
        You are a SOC report writer. Given the unified triage output below, produce a clean **Markdown**
        case description. Do NOT output any JSON. Use headings, bullet lists, and tables.

        Structure your output EXACTLY like this:

        ## Executive Summary
        One-paragraph overview of what happened, how many alerts, top findings.

        ## Triage Results
        A markdown table: | Alert | Disposition | Threat Type | Kill Chain | Confidence | MITRE | Reasoning |

        ## Entity Enrichment
        ## Investigation Findings
        ## Confidence Timeline
        ## Attack Chain Analysis
        ## Business Impact Assessment
        ## Response Plan
        ## Recommended Follow-up Actions

        ---

        **Unified triage output:**
        {{ steps.triage.output | json }}

        **Tiered response plan:**
        {{ steps.evaluate_response_tier.output | json }}

        **Alert count:** {{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.total.value }}
    timeout: 120s
    on_failure:
      - name: dlq_summarize
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-dead-letter
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            stage: summarize
            pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
            cycle_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
            error: "{{ workflow.last_error | default: 'unknown' }}"
      - name: release_lock_summarize_failed
        type: elasticsearch.request
        with:
          method: DELETE
          path: "/.soc-pipeline-lock/_doc/{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
      - name: end_summarize_failed
        type: console
        with:
          message: "Pipeline: summarize failed, DLQ written, lock released — exiting."
        end: true

  # ── Stage 3b: Case Creation ───────────────────────────────────────
  - name: create_case
    type: kibana.request
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /api/cases
      body:
        title: "[SOC-AUTO] cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
        description: "{{ steps.summarize.output.message }}"
        tags:
          - soc-simulation
          - auto-generated
        severity: medium
        connector:
          id: none
          name: none
          type: ".none"
          fields: null
        settings:
          syncAlerts: true
        owner: securitySolution

  # ── Stage 3c: Attach alerts — GROUPED BY rule.uuid ────────────────
  # Previously assumed the whole batch shared one rule (first-hit uuid).
  # For heterogeneous batches this dropped alerts. We now fan out per rule.
  - name: group_alerts_by_rule
    type: elasticsearch.search
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      index: ".alerts-security.alerts-*"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          must:
            - terms:
                _id: "${{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.hits | map: '_id' }}"
      aggregations:
        by_rule:
          terms:
            field: "kibana.alert.rule.uuid"
            size: 50
          aggs:
            alert_ids:
              top_hits:
                size: 20
                _source:
                  includes:
                    - kibana.alert.rule.uuid
                    - kibana.alert.rule.name
                    - _index

  - name: attach_alerts_per_rule
    type: foreach
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    foreach: "{{ steps.group_alerts_by_rule.output.aggregations.by_rule.buckets }}"
    steps:
      - name: attach_alerts
        type: kibana.request
        with:
          method: POST
          path: "/api/cases/{{ steps.create_case.output.id }}/comments"
          body:
            type: alert
            alertId: "${{ foreach.item.alert_ids.hits.hits | map: '_id' }}"
            index: "${{ foreach.item.alert_ids.hits.hits | map: '_index' }}"
            rule:
              id: "{{ foreach.item.key }}"
              name: "{{ foreach.item.alert_ids.hits.hits.first._source.kibana.alert.rule.name | default: 'unknown' }}"
            owner: securitySolution

  - name: log_case
    type: console
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      message: "Pipeline: case created ({{ steps.create_case.output.id }}) — alerts attached across {{ steps.group_alerts_by_rule.output.aggregations.by_rule.buckets | size | default: 0 }} rule(s)."

  # ── Stage 4: Cycle Metrics ─────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: write_metrics
    type: elasticsearch.index
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      index: .soc-metrics
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
        cycle_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
        alerts_processed: "{{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.total.value }}"
        stages_completed: "unified_triage,response,case_creation"
        case_created: true
        case_id: "{{ steps.create_case.output.id | default: null }}"
        status: "success"

  # ── Stage 5: Final Outcome + Release Lock ──────────────────────────
  # The outcome is DERIVED from the triage agent's highest-severity disposition —
  # never hardcoded to "case_created" (that is a pipeline state, not a disposition).
  - name: write_final_outcome
    type: elasticsearch.index
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      index: .soc-outcomes
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        correlation_id: "cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}"
        pipeline: "{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
        stage: "pipeline_complete"
        agents_involved: ["soc-triage-agent"]
        alerts_processed: "{{ steps.get_open_alerts.output.hits.total.value }}"
        case_created: true
        case_id: "{{ steps.create_case.output.id | default: null }}"
        # `disposition`, `classification`, `confidence` here are the pipeline-level
        # aggregate — first classification is used as an anchor; per-alert dispositions
        # live on per-alert docs in .soc-triage-results.
        # ai.agent returns `{ message: "<JSON>" }`; unwrap it the same way the
        # write_triage_batch / foreach paths do.
        classification: "{% assign _parsed_triage = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _parsed_triage.classifications.first.classification | default: 'SUSPICIOUS' }}"
        confidence: "{% assign _parsed_triage = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _parsed_triage.classifications.first.confidence | default: 0 }}"
        disposition: "{% assign _parsed_triage = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _parsed_triage.classifications.first.disposition | default: 'INCONCLUSIVE' }}"
        threat_category: "{% assign _parsed_triage = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _parsed_triage.classifications.first.threat_category | default: 'unknown' }}"
        kill_chain_stage: "{% assign _parsed_triage = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _parsed_triage.classifications.first.kill_chain_stage | default: 'unknown' }}"
        verdict: "{% assign _parsed_triage = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{% assign _c = _parsed_triage.classifications.first.classification | default: 'UNKNOWN' %}{% if _c == 'TRUE_POSITIVE' %}true_positive{% elsif _c == 'FALSE_POSITIVE' %}false_positive{% elsif _c == 'BENIGN_POSITIVE' %}benign_positive{% elsif _c == 'SUSPICIOUS' %}suspicious{% else %}inconclusive{% endif %}"
        highest_tier: "{{ steps.evaluate_response_tier.output.highest_tier | default: 0 }}"
        pipeline_complete: true

  # Final release_lock is ONLY for the has-alerts branch.
  # The no-alerts branch releases the lock earlier via `release_lock_no_alerts`.
  # Running this unconditionally produces a 404 (lock already deleted) which the
  # workflow engine marks as step=failed -> execution=failed, even though the
  # on_failure handler fires. Guard it with the same gate that fanout the rest
  # of the has-alerts pipeline.
  - name: release_lock
    type: elasticsearch.request
    if: "steps.gate_has_alerts.output: yes"
    with:
      method: DELETE
      path: "/.soc-pipeline-lock/_doc/{{ consts.pipeline_id }}"
    on_failure:
      - name: log_release_failed
        type: console
        with:
          message: "Warning: failed to release pipeline lock (cycle_id=cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}). Next cycle will overwrite on acquire."

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Pipeline: COMPLETE (cycle_id=cycle-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}). Lock released."

definition.name: SOC Alert Sweeper
definition.description:
Full autonomous pipeline orchestrator. Sweeps untriaged alerts every 5 minutes, then runs unified triage (classify + enrich + investigate in a single agent call) → Tiered Response → Case Creation.
Reliability invariants (T2 hardening): - Atomic pipeline lock via `elasticsearch.create` on a deterministic document id.
  Two concurrent runs cannot both succeed (version conflict = skip).
- on_failure release: the pipeline lock is released whether the run succeeds or fails. - ai.agent steps have on_failure routing to .soc-dead-letter with run_id + stage. - ms-precision timestamps + run_id salt on every document so docs never collide
  inside the same wall-clock second.

Data-model invariants (T1): - Dispositions are DERIVED from the triage agent output, never hardcoded
  ("case_created" is not a disposition — it is a pipeline state).
- Per-alert triage fields (classification, confidence, disposition, kill_chain_stage,
  threat_category) are FLATTENED at the top level of `.soc-triage-results`
  (one doc per alert) so dashboards can aggregate without reaching into
  triage_output.*.

Correctness invariants: - attach_alerts groups alerts by rule.uuid so a heterogeneous batch of alerts
  produces one case-comment per rule (previously assumed homogeneous batch).

**Phase 1 — Classification**: For EACH alert classify as TRUE_POSITIVE, FALSE_POSITIVE, or SUSPICIOUS with confidence 0-100. Use ES|QL to check for related alerts from the same hosts/users/IPs within a 30-minute window.
**Phase 2 — Entity Enrichment**: For alerts with confidence >= 40, enrich with entity context. Query 7-day behavioral baselines, entity risk scores, and relationships. Adjust confidence based on entity context.
**Phase 3 — Deep Investigation**: For alerts still ambiguous (confidence 40-69) after enrichment, conduct structured threat hunts. Formulate hypotheses, run ES|QL queries for process trees, network timelines, lateral movement. Search Security Labs for IOC intel.
**Phase 4 — Attack Chain Correlation**: For TRUE_POSITIVE or SUSPICIOUS alerts with confidence >= 50, use security.attack_discovery_search to check for attack discoveries. Look for kill chain progression across alerts sharing the same host/user/IP.

**Self-validation**: Verify every input alert has a classification, confidence is 0-100, disposition is one of the enumerated values (NEVER "case_created" or "triaged" — those are pipeline states, not dispositions), and all required fields are populated.

results.name: SOC Autonomous Applier
results.description:
Pure Elastic-native applier for autonomous self-governance mutations.
AUTONOMY-FIRST LIFECYCLE (2026-04): ----------------------------------- The applier ONLY processes intents whose status is one of:
    auto_apply_ready, approved_by_human, pending (non-rule-update only)

Rule-update intents land as `pending`; the soc-rule-backtester workflow evaluates them and flips status to `auto_apply_ready` (projection safe) or `pending_review` (exception queue). The applier refuses to touch a rule-update intent that has not passed the backtester — the refusal is a deferral (no rejection), so the backtester's next tick can still claim it.
DETERMINISTIC GATE CASCADE: ---------------------------
   1. Kill-switch           (.soc-kill-switch autonomy_enabled=false)
   2. Freeze-window         (.soc-kill-switch docs with scope=freeze-*)
   3. Ownership             (must be auto-* prefix + owner=autosoc for update)
   4. Envelope validity     (runtime recheck of recommendation.schema.json)
   5. Backtest required     (rule-update + status=pending -> defer to backtester)
   6. Drift                 (patch.current_values vs live rule state)
   7. First-of-kind         (agent has never produced this kind of mutation
                             before -> exception queue)
   8. Trust-tier            (.soc-trust-scores agent_tier=probationary -> review)
   9. Budget                (24h global mutation budget)
  10. Cooldown              (same artifact in last 15 min)
  11. Loop                  (same artifact 3+ times in 24h)

Failures are logged to `.soc-autonomy-decisions` with the first failing gate. Successes are logged too (auto_applied: true). The activity-feed dashboard aggregates this index to compute the Autonomy KPI.
Pipeline (all steps are elasticsearch.*, kibana.request, ai.agent, foreach, if — NO external code):
  1. Read global kill-switch from .soc-kill-switch. If `autonomy_enabled: false`, exit without touching anything.
  2. Pull pending / auto_apply_ready / approved_by_human intents, oldest first.
  3. Pull last-24h evolution metrics used for budget / cooldown / loop gates.
  4. For each intent, run the gate cascade and hand-off or defer.
  5. Write a heartbeat row to .soc-audit-trail and a decision log to
     .soc-autonomy-decisions with counts.

PREFIX CONVENTION (critical):
  - canonical artifacts:       id head (first `-` segment) == `soc` or `caldera`
  - autonomously-created:      id head anything else — convention is `auto-*`
                               (e.g. `auto-lateral-hunter-agent`). Do NOT use
                               `autosoc-*`; a naive substring check against
                               `soc-` would falsely flag that as canonical.
The check uses Liquid `| split: '-' | first` so `auto-*`, `autosoc-*`, and any other head are correctly classified as non-canonical.
This workflow is the ONLY path by which AutoSOC can mutate its own artifacts.

    1. Read global kill-switch from .soc-kill-switch. If `autonomy_enabled: false`, exit without touching anything.
    2. Pull pending / auto_apply_ready / approved_by_human intents, oldest first.

  PREFIX CONVENTION (critical):
    - canonical artifacts:       id head (first `-` segment) == `soc` or `caldera`
    - autonomously-created:      id head anything else — convention is `auto-*`
                                 (e.g. `auto-lateral-hunter-agent`). Do NOT use
                                 `autosoc-*`; a naive substring check against

enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 2m
  - type: manual

consts:
  max_per_tick: 20
  daily_budget_all: 50
  cooldown_seconds: 900
  loop_window_seconds: 86400
  loop_threshold: 3

steps:
  # ── 1. Kill-switch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # NOTE: uses elasticsearch.request (not .search) because the workflow engine's
  # zod schema for top-level `sort` only accepts strings or the reserved keys
  # (_score/_doc/_geo_distance/_script). Sorting @timestamp desc requires an
  # object form that the raw request API passes through unchanged.
  - name: read_kill_switch
    type: elasticsearch.request
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /.soc-kill-switch/_search
      body:
        size: 1
        query:
          term:
            scope: "global"
        sort:
          - "@timestamp":
              order: desc
  # Pre-compute kill-switch gates into scalar "yes"/"no" so the if: conditions
  # can use KQL `steps.<gate>.output: yes` matching (the only reliable pattern —
  # bare Liquid `{{ ... == false }}` renders to "true"/"false" which KQL then
  # evaluates as `is(*, 'false')` and silently returns false).
  - name: gate_kill_switch_active
    type: console
    with:
      message: "{% if steps.read_kill_switch.output.hits.hits[0]._source.autonomy_enabled == false %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}"

  - name: gate_autonomy_ok
    type: console
    with:
      message: "{% if steps.read_kill_switch.output.hits.hits[0]._source.autonomy_enabled == false %}no{% else %}yes{% endif %}"

  - name: kill_switch_active_log
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        Kill-switch ACTIVE (autonomy_enabled=false) — aborting applier run.
        Reason: {{ steps.read_kill_switch.output.hits.hits[0]._source.reason | default: 'unset' }}
    if: "steps.gate_kill_switch_active.output: yes"

  - name: abort_if_kill_switch
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: autonomous_applier_abort
        reason: kill_switch_active
        kill_switch: "{{ steps.read_kill_switch.output.hits.hits[0]._source | json }}"
    if: "steps.gate_kill_switch_active.output: yes"

  # ── 2. Pending intents (skipped when kill-switch active / autonomy disabled) ─
  #
  # Status matrix:
  #   pending              -> new intent. Non-rule-update: eligible; rule-update: deferred to backtester
  #   auto_apply_ready     -> backtester said safe; apply immediately
  #   approved_by_human    -> exception queue -> operator approved; apply immediately
  #
  # Any other status (pending_backtest, pending_review, applying, applied, rolled_back,
  # failed, rejected_*) is ignored — that record is owned by another workflow.
  # NOTE: uses elasticsearch.request (not .search) — see read_kill_switch above
  # for the sort-schema rationale.
  - name: pending_intents
    type: elasticsearch.request
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /.soc-recommendations/_search
      body:
        size: 20
        query:
          bool:
            filter:
              - term: {type: "mutation_intent"}
              - terms: {status: ["pending", "auto_apply_ready", "approved_by_human"]}
        sort:
          - "@timestamp":
              order: asc
    if: "steps.gate_autonomy_ok.output: yes"

  # ── 3. Budget / cooldown / loop context ──────────────────────────────
  # Initial pre-foreach snapshot of the 24h applied counter. The live
  # recount inside the foreach is authoritative; this outer read is kept
  # only for the heartbeat/summary at the end of the tick.
  - name: recent_mutations
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-evolution-log"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term: {source: "soc-autonomous-applier"}
            - term: {result: "applied"}
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-24h"
      aggs:
        total_24h:
          value_count:
            field: "artifact_id"
    if: "steps.gate_autonomy_ok.output: yes"

  # ── 4. Dispatch each intent ──────────────────────────────────────────
  # Per-iteration, each gate re-queries .soc-evolution-log so the budget
  # / cooldown / loop counters see mutations applied earlier in the same
  # tick. A wait_for-refreshed serialization marker is written after
  # each successful apply so the subsequent iteration's search observes
  # the newly-written audit row (T2 applier-concurrency).
  - name: dispatch_intents
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.pending_intents.output.hits.hits }}"
    if: "steps.gate_autonomy_ok.output: yes"
    steps:
      # Live recount of 24h applied mutations — authoritative for the
      # global budget gate. Re-queried every iteration so intents later
      # in the batch correctly see earlier intra-batch applies.
      - name: recent_mutations_live
        type: elasticsearch.search
        with:
          index: ".soc-evolution-log"
          size: 0
          query:
            bool:
              filter:
                - term: {source: "soc-autonomous-applier"}
                - term: {result: "applied"}
                - range:
                    "@timestamp":
                      gte: "now-24h"
          aggs:
            total_24h:
              value_count:
                field: "artifact_id"

      # -- Ownership lookup ---------------------------------------------
      - name: ownership_row
        type: elasticsearch.search
        with:
          index: ".soc-artifact-registry"
          size: 1
          query:
            bool:
              filter:
                - term: {type: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type }}"}
                - term: {artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"}

      # ── GATE COMPUTATION ──────────────────────────────────────────────
      # All gates are pre-computed via console steps that emit "yes"/"no".
      # Each consumer step's `if:` then uses KQL `steps.<gate>.output: yes`.
      # Why: LiquidJS renders boolean expressions as the strings "true"/"false"
      # (or "1"/""), but KQL treats those as bare terms like `is(*, 'true')`
      # which silently evaluate to false. Compute-and-match is the only
      # reliable pattern empirically verified against the workflow engine.

      # Envelope validation — runtime enforcement of recommendation.schema.json.
      - name: gate_envelope_invalid
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign rec_id = foreach.item._source.rec_id -%}
            {%- assign sv = foreach.item._source.schema_version -%}
            {%- assign t = foreach.item._source.type -%}
            {%- assign src = foreach.item._source.source -%}
            {%- assign st = foreach.item._source.status -%}
            {%- assign ti = foreach.item._source.title -%}
            {%- assign su = foreach.item._source.summary -%}
            {%- assign cf = foreach.item._source.confidence -%}
            {%- assign de = foreach.item._source.details -%}
            {%- assign tr = foreach.item._source.track -%}
            {%- assign hk = foreach.item._source.housekeeping -%}
            {%- assign ev = foreach.item._source.evidence -%}
            {%- assign ei = foreach.item._source.expected_impact -%}
            {%- assign ev_size = ev | size | default: 0 -%}
            {%- assign track_bad = false -%}
            {%- if tr != 'deterministic' and tr != 'agentic' -%}{%- assign track_bad = true -%}{%- endif -%}
            {%- assign ev_bad = false -%}
            {%- if hk != true and ev_size == 0 -%}{%- assign ev_bad = true -%}{%- endif -%}
            {%- if hk != true and ei == nil -%}{%- assign ev_bad = true -%}{%- endif -%}
            {% if rec_id == nil or rec_id == empty or sv == nil or t != 'mutation_intent' or src == nil or src == empty or st == nil or st == empty or ti == nil or ti == empty or su == nil or su == empty or cf == nil or de == nil or track_bad == true or ev_bad == true %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      # Awaiting-backtest — rule-update intents at status=pending defer to backtester.
      - name: gate_awaiting_backtest
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign at = foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type -%}
            {%- assign op = foreach.item._source.details.op -%}
            {%- assign st = foreach.item._source.status -%}
            {% if at == 'rule' and op == 'update' and st == 'pending' %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      # Canonical artifact — block mutations where the registry explicitly says
      # `canonical` or `platform`, OR where no registry row exists AND the
      # artifact id is in a reserved prefix (`soc-*`, `caldera-*`). Retro-tagged
      # rules (where registry owner=autosoc but id is a UUID) are ALLOWED: the
      # registry is the source of truth for ownership; the id prefix is only a
      # fallback safety net when registry knows nothing about the artifact.
      - name: gate_canonical
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign owner = steps.ownership_row.output.hits.hits[0]._source.owner -%}
            {%- assign first_seg = foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id | split: '-' | first -%}
                        {%- assign block = false -%}
                        {%- if owner == 'canonical' -%}{%- assign block = true -%}{%- endif -%}
                        {%- if owner == 'platform' -%}{%- assign block = true -%}{%- endif -%}
                        {%- if owner == nil and first_seg == 'soc' -%}{%- assign block = true -%}{%- endif -%}
                        {%- if owner == nil and first_seg == 'caldera' -%}{%- assign block = true -%}{%- endif -%}
                        {% if block == true %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      # Unregistered-mutation — mutating op (update/delete/enable/disable) on an
      # artifact that does not have an autosoc-owned registry row. The applier
      # refuses to mutate anything it has not been given ownership over. This
      # now applies to ALL artifact id prefixes (not just auto-*), because
      # retro-tagged rules keep their UUID ids but are legitimately autosoc-owned.
      - name: gate_unregistered_mutation
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign op = foreach.item._source.details.op -%}
            {%- assign owner = steps.ownership_row.output.hits.hits[0]._source.owner -%}
            {%- assign is_mutating = false -%}
            {%- if op == 'update' or op == 'delete' or op == 'enable' or op == 'disable' -%}{%- assign is_mutating = true -%}{%- endif -%}
            {%- assign owner_bad = false -%}
            {%- if owner == nil or owner != 'autosoc' -%}{%- assign owner_bad = true -%}{%- endif -%}
            {% if is_mutating == true and owner_bad == true %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      - name: block_missing_envelope
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-evolution-log
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            source: "soc-autonomous-applier"
            intent_rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id | default: 'unknown' }}"
            artifact_type: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type | default: 'unknown' }}"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id | default: 'unknown' }}"
            op: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.op | default: 'unknown' }}"
            result: validation_failed
            reason: >-
              Envelope validation failed. Required fields per recommendation.schema.json:
              rec_id, schema_version, type, source, status, title, summary, confidence, details, track.
              track must be 'deterministic' or 'agentic'. confidence must be 0-100.
              Unless housekeeping=true, evidence[] must have ≥1 entry and expected_impact must be a non-empty object.
            tool_called: "none"
        if: "steps.gate_envelope_invalid.output: yes"

      - name: dead_letter_missing_envelope
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-dead-letter
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            source: "soc-autonomous-applier"
            reason: "envelope_validation_failed"
            rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id | default: 'unknown' }}"
            schema_ref: "recommendation.schema.json"
            doc: "{{ foreach.item._source | json }}"
        if: "steps.gate_envelope_invalid.output: yes"

      # ── GATE: Backtest required for rule updates ────────────────────
      # A rule-update intent with status=pending has NOT been backtested yet.
      # We defer — the backtester's next tick (every 1m) will compute a
      # projection and flip status to auto_apply_ready or pending_review.
      # Logging to .soc-autonomy-decisions is deliberate: even a "wait"
      # decision is a decision the activity-feed should show.
      - name: defer_awaiting_backtest
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-autonomy-decisions
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id | default: 'unknown' }}"
            artifact_type: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type }}"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"
            op: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.op }}"
            action: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.patch.action | default: 'none' }}"
            source_agent: "{{ foreach.item._source.source | default: 'unknown' }}"
            source_workflow: "soc-autonomous-applier"
            gates_evaluated: ["kill_switch", "envelope", "backtest_required"]
            gates_passed: ["kill_switch", "envelope"]
            first_failing_gate: "backtest_required"
            final_status: "deferred_awaiting_backtest"
            auto_applied: false
            required_human: false
            review_reason: "awaiting_backtest"
            confidence: "{{ foreach.item._source.confidence | default: 0 }}"
        if: "steps.gate_awaiting_backtest.output: yes"

      # Mark the intent as pending_backtest so the backtester sees it
      # in its next tick's primary query. Without this, the backtester
      # only sees truly-fresh intents and older pending rule-updates
      # stall forever.
      - name: mark_pending_backtest
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: .soc-recommendations
          id: "{{ foreach.item._id }}"
          doc:
            status: pending_backtest
            backtest_queued_at: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        if: "steps.gate_awaiting_backtest.output: yes"

      # Block canonical artifacts (registry says canonical OR first dash-segment
      # is `soc`/`caldera`) AND block non-`auto-*` ids for any op — this closes
      # the T5 registry-protection gap: even if the applier agent concocts a
      # plausible-looking artifact_id like `autosoc-thing`, it is rejected
      # unless the first dash-segment is literally `auto`.
      - name: block_canonical
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-evolution-log
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            source: "soc-autonomous-applier"
            intent_rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id }}"
            artifact_type: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type }}"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"
            op: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.op }}"
            result: blocked_canonical
            reason: "Artifact id is not in the protected `auto-*` namespace (registry owner=canonical, first dash-segment is 'soc'/'caldera', or does not start with 'auto-'). Autonomous mutation refused."
            tool_called: "none"
        if: "steps.gate_canonical.output: yes"

      # For update/delete/enable/disable ops, the artifact MUST already exist
      # in .soc-artifact-registry with owner=autosoc. This prevents the
      # applier agent from mutating anything it never created (e.g. an
      # artifact created manually by an operator, or by a sibling system).
      - name: block_unregistered_mutation
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-evolution-log
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            source: "soc-autonomous-applier"
            intent_rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id }}"
            artifact_type: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type }}"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"
            op: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.op }}"
            result: blocked_unregistered
            reason: "Non-create op requires an existing .soc-artifact-registry row with owner=autosoc. The applier refuses to mutate an artifact it does not own."
            tool_called: "none"
        if: "steps.gate_unregistered_mutation.output: yes"

      # Block on loop detection (>= loop_threshold attempts of same artifact in
      # window, counting both applied AND failed — so a persistently failing
      # intent does not retry forever).
      - name: artifact_recent_count
        type: elasticsearch.search
        with:
          index: ".soc-evolution-log"
          size: 0
          query:
            bool:
              filter:
                - term: {source: "soc-autonomous-applier"}
                - term: {artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"}
                - range:
                    "@timestamp":
                      gte: "now-{{ consts.loop_window_seconds }}s"
                - terms:
                    result: ["applied", "failure", "validation_failed"]
        # Only run the loop/cooldown counter query when the intent has passed
        # envelope + canonical + unregistered gates — skip noise from malformed
        # or out-of-scope intents.
        if: >-
          steps.gate_envelope_invalid.output: no and
          steps.gate_canonical.output: no and
          steps.gate_unregistered_mutation.output: no

      # Gate: loop threshold exceeded for this artifact in the window.
      - name: gate_loop_exceeded
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign cnt = steps.artifact_recent_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 -%}
            {%- assign th = consts.loop_threshold -%}
            {% if cnt >= th %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      - name: block_loop
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-evolution-log
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            source: "soc-autonomous-applier"
            intent_rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id }}"
            artifact_type: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type }}"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"
            op: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.op }}"
            result: blocked_loop
            reason: "Artifact was mutated {{ steps.artifact_recent_count.output.hits.total.value }} times in the last {{ consts.loop_window_seconds }}s (threshold: {{ consts.loop_threshold }}). Oscillation detected; refusing further mutations."
            tool_called: "none"
        if: "steps.gate_loop_exceeded.output: yes"

      # Cooldown: count applied mutations for this artifact in the cooldown window.
      # Zero means safe to proceed; >= 1 means defer.
      - name: artifact_cooldown_count
        type: elasticsearch.search
        with:
          index: ".soc-evolution-log"
          size: 0
          query:
            bool:
              filter:
                - term: {source: "soc-autonomous-applier"}
                - term: {result: "applied"}
                - term: {artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"}
                - range:
                    "@timestamp":
                      gte: "now-{{ consts.cooldown_seconds }}s"
        # Only check cooldown when earlier gates passed. Matches the original
        # compound condition: not canonical, loop not exceeded, envelope good.
        if: >-
          steps.gate_envelope_invalid.output: no and
          steps.gate_canonical.output: no and
          steps.gate_loop_exceeded.output: no

      # Gate: cooldown window active for this artifact.
      - name: gate_cooldown_active
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign cnt = steps.artifact_cooldown_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 -%}
            {% if cnt >= 1 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      - name: block_cooldown
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-evolution-log
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            source: "soc-autonomous-applier"
            intent_rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id }}"
            artifact_type: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type }}"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"
            op: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.op }}"
            result: blocked_cooldown
            reason: "Artifact was mutated within the last {{ consts.cooldown_seconds }}s cooldown window. Deferring."
            tool_called: "none"
        if: "steps.gate_cooldown_active.output: yes"

      # Defer on budget (global or per-type)
      - name: block_budget_global
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-evolution-log
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            source: "soc-autonomous-applier"
            intent_rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id }}"
            artifact_type: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type }}"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"
            op: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.op }}"
            result: blocked_budget
            reason: "Global 24h budget of {{ consts.daily_budget_all }} mutations reached ({{ steps.recent_mutations_live.output.aggregations.total_24h.value | default: 0 }}). Deferring."
            tool_called: "none"
        if: "steps.gate_budget_exceeded.output: yes"

      # Gate: global 24h budget exceeded AND earlier gates passed.
      - name: gate_budget_exceeded
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign cnt_24h = steps.recent_mutations_live.output.aggregations.total_24h.value | default: 0 -%}
            {%- assign budget = consts.daily_budget_all -%}
            {% if cnt_24h >= budget %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      # Gate: all checks passed — invoke applier agent.
      # Composite: not canonical, not unregistered, not loop, not cooldown, not budget,
      # not envelope-invalid, not awaiting-backtest, first_seg=='auto'.
      # We encode first_seg and op_allowed_for_owner here since they aren't in other gates.
      # All gates must pass. `op_allowed` encodes the positive-ownership rule:
      #   - op=create is always allowed (we're creating a new artifact)
      #   - OR owner=='autosoc' per the registry (covers both `auto-*` greenfield
      #     artifacts AND retro-tagged SOC-Sim UUID rules whose registry row was
      #     stamped by soc-registry-retro-tag).
      # The old implementation ALSO required `first_seg == 'auto'` which
      # silently blocked every autosoc-owned UUID rule — that was the root
      # cause of the 95% rejection rate in the 2026-04-17 demo soak (the
      # individual gates passed but the composite refused every UUID).
      - name: gate_all_pass
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign owner = steps.ownership_row.output.hits.hits[0]._source.owner -%}
            {%- assign op = foreach.item._source.details.op -%}
            {%- assign op_allowed = false -%}
            {%- if op == 'create' -%}{%- assign op_allowed = true -%}{%- endif -%}
            {%- if owner == 'autosoc' -%}{%- assign op_allowed = true -%}{%- endif -%}
            {%- assign env_invalid = steps.gate_envelope_invalid.output -%}
            {%- assign canonical = steps.gate_canonical.output -%}
            {%- assign unreg = steps.gate_unregistered_mutation.output -%}
            {%- assign loop_ex = steps.gate_loop_exceeded.output -%}
            {%- assign cool_ac = steps.gate_cooldown_active.output -%}
            {%- assign budg_ex = steps.gate_budget_exceeded.output -%}
            {%- assign await_bt = steps.gate_awaiting_backtest.output -%}
            {% if env_invalid == 'no' and canonical == 'no' and unreg == 'no' and loop_ex == 'no' and cool_ac == 'no' and budg_ex == 'no' and await_bt == 'no' and op_allowed == true %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      # Gate: permanent rejection — canonical, non-auto, loop-exceeded,
      # envelope invalid, or unregistered mutation.
      - name: gate_permanent_reject
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign env_invalid = steps.gate_envelope_invalid.output -%}
            {%- assign canonical = steps.gate_canonical.output -%}
            {%- assign unreg = steps.gate_unregistered_mutation.output -%}
            {%- assign loop_ex = steps.gate_loop_exceeded.output -%}
            {% if canonical == 'yes' or env_invalid == 'yes' or loop_ex == 'yes' or unreg == 'yes' %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      # -- All gates passed -> invoke the applier agent -----------------
      - name: apply_with_agent
        type: ai.agent
        agent-id: soc-autonomous-applier-agent
        connector-id: opus
        with:
          message: >
            You have been handed ONE validated mutation_intent. Apply it per your
            instructions. Snapshot first, then mutate, then audit, then close.

            intent = {{ foreach.item._source | json }}
            ownership_registry_row = {{ steps.ownership_row.output.hits.hits[0]._source | json }}
            recent_mutations_for_artifact = {{ steps.artifact_recent_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}

            Return the JSON result described in your instructions. Nothing else.
        timeout: 300s
        if: "steps.gate_all_pass.output: yes"

      # Serialization barrier — force .soc-evolution-log to be searchable
      # before the next iteration's live gates query it. The applier
      # agent writes its audit row via tool call; that write is not
      # refresh=wait_for by default, so without this barrier the next
      # iteration could miss the just-applied mutation and re-breach
      # budget/cooldown/loop thresholds (T2 applier-concurrency).
      - name: serialize_applied_intent
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-evolution-log
          refresh: "wait_for"
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            source: "soc-autonomous-applier"
            event_type: "applier_serialize_marker"
            intent_rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id }}"
            artifact_type: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type }}"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"
            op: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.op }}"
            result: "serialize_marker"
            tool_called: "none"
            note: "Synchronization barrier ensuring the next iteration's gate queries observe this apply."
        if: "steps.gate_all_pass.output: yes"

      # On a PERMANENT block (canonical or loop detection), mark the intent
      # `rejected` so it never retries. Cooldown and budget are DEFERS — the
      # intent stays `pending` and the next tick reconsiders it.
      - name: close_rejected_intent
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: .soc-recommendations
          id: "{{ foreach.item._id }}"
          doc:
            status: rejected
            applied_by: soc-autonomous-applier
            applied_at: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            rejection_reason: "gated_by_applier_workflow"
        # Permanent-rejection conditions (ANY one trips it):
        #   - canonical owner OR non-auto artifact prefix
        #   - loop threshold reached
        #   - envelope invalid (same check as block_missing_envelope)
        #   - mutating op on an artifact not owned by autosoc
        if: "steps.gate_permanent_reject.output: yes"

      # ── Close successfully applied intent ──────────────────────────
      # After a successful auto-apply, transition the recommendation's
      # status from `auto_apply_ready` / `approved_by_human` / `pending`
      # to `applied` so the next applier tick does not re-process the
      # same intent. Without this transition, the applier keeps re-running
      # the full gate cascade every tick and the 24h budget counter
      # inflates on each re-attempt.
      - name: close_applied_intent
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: .soc-recommendations
          id: "{{ foreach.item._id }}"
          refresh: "wait_for"
          doc:
            status: applied
            applied_by: soc-autonomous-applier
            applied_at: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            applied_exec_id: "{{ execution.id | default: 'unknown' }}"
        if: "steps.gate_all_pass.output: yes"

      # ── Decision log: successful auto-apply ────────────────────────
      # Records every auto-apply attempt so the Autonomy Activity Feed
      # can show "N decisions today, M auto-applied". The row is keyed
      # by rec_id — the post-apply-observer reconciles with the actual
      # artifact state later.
      - name: log_auto_apply_decision
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-autonomy-decisions
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id }}"
            artifact_type: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_type }}"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.artifact_id }}"
            op: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.op }}"

definition.name: SOC Autonomous Applier
definition.description:
Pure Elastic-native applier for autonomous self-governance mutations.
AUTONOMY-FIRST LIFECYCLE (2026-04): ----------------------------------- The applier ONLY processes intents whose status is one of:
    auto_apply_ready, approved_by_human, pending (non-rule-update only)

Rule-update intents land as `pending`; the soc-rule-backtester workflow evaluates them and flips status to `auto_apply_ready` (projection safe) or `pending_review` (exception queue). The applier refuses to touch a rule-update intent that has not passed the backtester — the refusal is a deferral (no rejection), so the backtester's next tick can still claim it.
DETERMINISTIC GATE CASCADE: ---------------------------
   1. Kill-switch           (.soc-kill-switch autonomy_enabled=false)
   2. Freeze-window         (.soc-kill-switch docs with scope=freeze-*)
   3. Ownership             (must be auto-* prefix + owner=autosoc for update)
   4. Envelope validity     (runtime recheck of recommendation.schema.json)
   5. Backtest required     (rule-update + status=pending -> defer to backtester)
   6. Drift                 (patch.current_values vs live rule state)
   7. First-of-kind         (agent has never produced this kind of mutation
                             before -> exception queue)
   8. Trust-tier            (.soc-trust-scores agent_tier=probationary -> review)
   9. Budget                (24h global mutation budget)
  10. Cooldown              (same artifact in last 15 min)
  11. Loop                  (same artifact 3+ times in 24h)

Failures are logged to `.soc-autonomy-decisions` with the first failing gate. Successes are logged too (auto_applied: true). The activity-feed dashboard aggregates this index to compute the Autonomy KPI.
Pipeline (all steps are elasticsearch.*, kibana.request, ai.agent, foreach, if — NO external code):
  1. Read global kill-switch from .soc-kill-switch. If `autonomy_enabled: false`, exit without touching anything.
  2. Pull pending / auto_apply_ready / approved_by_human intents, oldest first.
  3. Pull last-24h evolution metrics used for budget / cooldown / loop gates.
  4. For each intent, run the gate cascade and hand-off or defer.
  5. Write a heartbeat row to .soc-audit-trail and a decision log to
     .soc-autonomy-decisions with counts.

PREFIX CONVENTION (critical):
  - canonical artifacts:       id head (first `-` segment) == `soc` or `caldera`
  - autonomously-created:      id head anything else — convention is `auto-*`
                               (e.g. `auto-lateral-hunter-agent`). Do NOT use
                               `autosoc-*`; a naive substring check against
                               `soc-` would falsely flag that as canonical.
The check uses Liquid `| split: '-' | first` so `auto-*`, `autosoc-*`, and any other head are correctly classified as non-canonical.
This workflow is the ONLY path by which AutoSOC can mutate its own artifacts.
