results.name: SOC Registry Retro-Tag
results.description:
Populates / refreshes .soc-artifact-registry with canonical-vs-autosoc-owned metadata for every agent, skill, workflow, AND detection rule currently live in Kibana.
Ownership rule (deterministic — no agent required):
  - first dash-separated token of artifact_id is `soc` or `caldera` -> owner=canonical
  - everything else (including `auto-*`, `autosoc-*`, custom names) -> owner=autosoc

Detection-rule override (2026-04-17): every rule tagged `soc-simulation` is registered with owner=autosoc + tags=[autosoc-owned, soc-simulation, retro-tagged]. This unblocks the Signal-Quality agent's ownership gate so it can tune the high-volume sim rules without needing manual registry entries. Without this seed the agent correctly refuses to mutate rules it cannot prove ownership of — and every tuning recommendation is marked blocked_ownership.
The first-token check uses Liquid's `split: '-' | first` filter so `autosoc-xxx` and `auto-xxx` are NOT matched by the canonical rule (unlike a naive substring `contains 'soc-'` which would falsely match them).
This workflow is pure Elastic: kibana.request + foreach + elasticsearch.index. No Python, no sidecars. Triggered once at the end of setup.sh and on demand from the Workflows UI.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Registry Retro-Tag
description: >
  Populates / refreshes .soc-artifact-registry with canonical-vs-autosoc-owned
  metadata for every agent, skill, workflow, AND detection rule currently live
  in Kibana.

  Ownership rule (deterministic — no agent required):
    - first dash-separated token of artifact_id is `soc` or `caldera` -> owner=canonical
    - everything else (including `auto-*`, `autosoc-*`, custom names) -> owner=autosoc

  Detection-rule override (2026-04-17): every rule tagged `soc-simulation` is
  registered with owner=autosoc + tags=[autosoc-owned, soc-simulation, retro-tagged].
  This unblocks the Signal-Quality agent's ownership gate so it can tune the
  high-volume sim rules without needing manual registry entries. Without this
  seed the agent correctly refuses to mutate rules it cannot prove ownership
  of — and every tuning recommendation is marked blocked_ownership.

  The first-token check uses Liquid's `split: '-' | first` filter so `autosoc-xxx`
  and `auto-xxx` are NOT matched by the canonical rule (unlike a naive
  substring `contains 'soc-'` which would falsely match them).

  This workflow is pure Elastic: kibana.request + foreach + elasticsearch.index.
  No Python, no sidecars. Triggered once at the end of setup.sh and on demand
  from the Workflows UI.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: manual

steps:
  # ── Inventory ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: list_agents
    type: kibana.request
    with:
      method: GET
      path: /api/agent_builder/agents

  - name: list_skills
    type: kibana.request
    with:
      method: GET
      path: /api/agent_builder/skills

  - name: list_workflows
    type: kibana.request
    with:
      method: GET
      path: /api/workflows

  # Detection rules tagged `soc-simulation` are the high-volume canonical rules
  # that the Signal-Quality agent needs to tune. Per the ownership-seed rule
  # above we explicitly register them as autosoc-owned so the ownership gate
  # stops blocking every tuning recommendation. per_page is bounded at 100 —
  # the soc-simulation rule set is never that large in practice.
  - name: list_detection_rules
    type: kibana.request
    with:
      method: GET
      path: /api/detection_engine/rules/_find?per_page=100&filter=alert.attributes.tags:%22soc-simulation%22

  # ── Agents -> registry rows ──────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: tag_agents
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.list_agents.output.results | default: steps.list_agents.output }}"
    steps:
      - name: write_agent_row
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: .soc-artifact-registry
          id: "agent:{{ foreach.item.id }}"
          doc_as_upsert: true
          doc:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            type: "agent"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item.id }}"
            name: "{{ foreach.item.name | default: foreach.item.id }}"
            description: "{{ foreach.item.description | default: '' }}"
            owner: "{% assign head = foreach.item.id | split: '-' | first %}{% if head == 'soc' or head == 'caldera' %}canonical{% else %}autosoc{% endif %}"
            origin: "{% assign head = foreach.item.id | split: '-' | first %}{% if head == 'soc' or head == 'caldera' %}canonical-file{% else %}meta-created{% endif %}"
            created_by: "{{ foreach.item.created_by.username | default: foreach.item.created_by | default: 'unknown' }}"
            state: "active"
            schema_version: 1
            tags: ["retro-tagged"]

  # ── Skills -> registry rows ──────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: tag_skills
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.list_skills.output.results | default: steps.list_skills.output }}"
    steps:
      - name: write_skill_row
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: .soc-artifact-registry
          id: "skill:{{ foreach.item.id }}"
          doc_as_upsert: true
          doc:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            type: "skill"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item.id }}"
            name: "{{ foreach.item.name | default: foreach.item.id }}"
            description: "{{ foreach.item.description | default: '' }}"
            owner: "{% assign head = foreach.item.id | split: '-' | first %}{% if head == 'soc' or head == 'caldera' %}canonical{% else %}autosoc{% endif %}"
            origin: "{% assign head = foreach.item.id | split: '-' | first %}{% if head == 'soc' or head == 'caldera' %}canonical-file{% else %}meta-created{% endif %}"
            created_by: "{{ foreach.item.created_by.username | default: foreach.item.created_by | default: 'unknown' }}"
            state: "active"
            schema_version: 1
            tags: ["retro-tagged"]

  # ── Workflows -> registry rows ──────────────────────────────────────
  - name: tag_workflows
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.list_workflows.output.results | default: steps.list_workflows.output }}"
    steps:
      - name: write_workflow_row
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: .soc-artifact-registry
          id: "workflow:{{ foreach.item.id }}"
          doc_as_upsert: true
          doc:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            type: "workflow"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item.id }}"
            name: "{{ foreach.item.name | default: foreach.item.id }}"
            description: "{{ foreach.item.description | default: '' }}"
            owner: "{% assign head = foreach.item.id | split: '-' | first %}{% if head == 'soc' or head == 'caldera' %}canonical{% else %}autosoc{% endif %}"
            origin: "{% assign head = foreach.item.id | split: '-' | first %}{% if head == 'soc' or head == 'caldera' %}canonical-file{% else %}meta-created{% endif %}"
            created_by: "{{ foreach.item.createdBy.username | default: foreach.item.created_by.username | default: foreach.item.created_by | default: 'unknown' }}"
            state: "active"
            schema_version: 1
            tags: ["retro-tagged"]

  # ── Detection rules -> registry rows (explicit owner=autosoc) ──────
  # Unlike agents/skills/workflows which use the first-token ownership heuristic,
  # detection rules tagged `soc-simulation` are ALWAYS registered as autosoc-owned
  # regardless of rule_id prefix. This is the seed that unblocks the Signal-Quality
  # agent's ownership gate.
  - name: tag_detection_rules
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.list_detection_rules.output.data | default: empty }}"
    steps:
      - name: write_rule_row
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: .soc-artifact-registry
          id: "rule:{{ foreach.item.rule_id }}"
          doc_as_upsert: true
          doc:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            type: "rule"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item.rule_id }}"
            name: "{{ foreach.item.name | default: foreach.item.rule_id }}"
            description: "{{ foreach.item.description | default: '' }}"
            owner: "autosoc"
            origin: "canonical-file"
            created_by: "{{ foreach.item.created_by | default: 'soc-simulation' }}"
            state: "active"
            schema_version: 1
            tags: ["autosoc-owned", "soc-simulation", "retro-tagged"]

      # Also stamp the rule itself with the `autosoc-owned` tag in Kibana so any
      # downstream check that reads `kibana.alert.rule.tags` (not just the
      # registry) sees the autosoc ownership signal. Uses the bulk edit API so
      # we're idempotent — add_tags will merge, not replace.
      - name: stamp_rule_tag
        type: kibana.request
        with:
          method: POST
          path: /api/detection_engine/rules/_bulk_action
          body:
            action: "edit"
            ids:
              - "{{ foreach.item.id }}"
            edit:
              - type: "add_tags"
                value:
                  - "autosoc-owned"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Registry retro-tag complete — agents + skills + workflows + {{ steps.list_detection_rules.output.data | size | default: 0 }} detection rule(s) registered."

results.name: SOC Difficulty Controller
results.description:
Performance-gated difficulty escalation for Caldera adversary emulation. Runs every 15 minutes (down from 30m so the system adapts faster).
Deterministic decision (no LLM -- previous LLM impl returned null 100% of the time because the prompt needed fields that aren't in .soc-outcomes).
Signals (last 24h):
  * detection_rate    = (case_created + responded + true_positive) / total
  * fp_rate           = (false_positive + dismissed) / total
  * avg_triage_conf   = mean of triage_classification.confidence (%)
  * trust_avg         = mean trust_score across trusted+probationary agents

Disposition mapping (reality of the current pipeline):
  * case_created / responded / true_positive  -> TP-equivalent (positive)
  * false_positive / dismissed                -> FP-equivalent (negative)
  * triaged / other                           -> in-flight, not counted

Rules (applied in order, first match wins):
  * detection_rate >= 0.80 AND fp_rate <= 0.30 AND trust_avg >= 0.70
      -> INCREASE level (cap 5)
  * detection_rate <  0.50 OR  fp_rate >  0.60
      -> DECREASE level (floor 1)
  * otherwise
      -> MAINTAIN

Output:
  1. Fresh doc in .soc-difficulty-state with level + all metrics
  2. One attack_command in .soc-attack-commands with difficulty=level so
     the Caldera dispatcher picks up a harder/easier operation next tick

  lookback: "now-7d"
  min_outcomes_required: 10
  increase_detect_threshold: 0.80
  increase_fp_threshold: 0.30
  increase_trust_threshold: 0.70
  decrease_detect_threshold: 0.50
  decrease_fp_threshold: 0.60
  min_level: 1
  max_level: 5

steps:
  # ── Current level (default to 2 = "realistic" if state missing) ─────
  # NOTE: workflow engine strips the body: wrapper on elasticsearch.search
  # steps. All query params MUST live directly under `with:`. To get the
  # "latest" state, we use a `top_hits` aggregation with a nested sort
  # (sort inside aggregations is passed through verbatim to ES).
  - name: current_state
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-difficulty-state"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - exists: { field: "level" }
      aggregations:
        latest:
          top_hits:
            size: 1
            sort:
              - "@timestamp":
                  order: desc

  # ── Outcome aggregations ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: outcome_stats
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-outcomes"
      size: 0
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "{{ consts.lookback }}"
      aggregations:
        by_disposition:
          terms:
            field: "disposition"
            size: 20
        total:
          value_count:
            field: "disposition"

  - name: triage_stats
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-triage-results"
      size: 0
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "{{ consts.lookback }}"
      aggregations:
        avg_conf:
          avg:
            field: "triage_classification.confidence"

  - name: trust_snapshot
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-trust-scores"
      size: 50
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term: { scope: "per_agent" }
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-48h"
            - terms:
                trust_tier: ["trusted", "probationary"]

  # ── Write state row with computed metrics + level decision ──────────
  - name: write_difficulty_state
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-difficulty-state
      refresh: "wait_for"
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        source: "soc-difficulty-controller"
        current_level: "{{ steps.current_state.output.aggregations.latest.hits.hits.0._source.level | default: 2 }}"
        level: "{% assign _cur = steps.current_state.output.aggregations.latest.hits.hits.0._source.level | default: 2 %}{% assign _tp = 0 %}{% assign _fp = 0 %}{% assign _other = 0 %}{% for b in steps.outcome_stats.output.aggregations.by_disposition.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'true_positive' or b.key == 'case_created' or b.key == 'responded' %}{% assign _tp = _tp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% elsif b.key == 'false_positive' or b.key == 'dismissed' %}{% assign _fp = _fp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% else %}{% assign _other = _other | plus: b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% assign _total = _tp | plus: _fp | plus: _other %}{% if _total < consts.min_outcomes_required %}{{ _cur }}{% else %}{% assign _det_num = _tp | times: 1000 %}{% assign _det = _det_num | divided_by: _total %}{% assign _fp_num = _fp | times: 1000 %}{% assign _fpr = _fp_num | divided_by: _total %}{% assign _trust_count = steps.trust_snapshot.output.hits.hits | size | default: 0 %}{% if _det >= 800 and _fpr <= 300 and _trust_count >= 1 %}{% if _cur < consts.max_level %}{% assign _new = _cur | plus: 1 %}{{ _new }}{% else %}{{ _cur }}{% endif %}{% elsif _det < 500 or _fpr > 600 %}{% if _cur > consts.min_level %}{% assign _new = _cur | minus: 1 %}{{ _new }}{% else %}{{ _cur }}{% endif %}{% else %}{{ _cur }}{% endif %}{% endif %}"
        detection_rate_pct: "{% assign _tp = 0 %}{% assign _fp = 0 %}{% assign _other = 0 %}{% for b in steps.outcome_stats.output.aggregations.by_disposition.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'true_positive' or b.key == 'case_created' or b.key == 'responded' %}{% assign _tp = _tp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% elsif b.key == 'false_positive' or b.key == 'dismissed' %}{% assign _fp = _fp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% else %}{% assign _other = _other | plus: b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% assign _total = _tp | plus: _fp | plus: _other %}{% if _total == 0 %}0{% else %}{% assign _x = _tp | times: 100 %}{{ _x | divided_by: _total }}{% endif %}"
        fp_rate_pct: "{% assign _tp = 0 %}{% assign _fp = 0 %}{% assign _other = 0 %}{% for b in steps.outcome_stats.output.aggregations.by_disposition.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'true_positive' or b.key == 'case_created' or b.key == 'responded' %}{% assign _tp = _tp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% elsif b.key == 'false_positive' or b.key == 'dismissed' %}{% assign _fp = _fp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% else %}{% assign _other = _other | plus: b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% assign _total = _tp | plus: _fp | plus: _other %}{% if _total == 0 %}0{% else %}{% assign _x = _fp | times: 100 %}{{ _x | divided_by: _total }}{% endif %}"
        total_outcomes: "{% assign _tp = 0 %}{% assign _fp = 0 %}{% assign _other = 0 %}{% for b in steps.outcome_stats.output.aggregations.by_disposition.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'true_positive' or b.key == 'case_created' or b.key == 'responded' %}{% assign _tp = _tp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% elsif b.key == 'false_positive' or b.key == 'dismissed' %}{% assign _fp = _fp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% else %}{% assign _other = _other | plus: b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _tp | plus: _fp | plus: _other }}"
        tp_count: "{% assign _tp = 0 %}{% for b in steps.outcome_stats.output.aggregations.by_disposition.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'true_positive' or b.key == 'case_created' or b.key == 'responded' %}{% assign _tp = _tp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _tp }}"
        fp_count: "{% assign _fp = 0 %}{% for b in steps.outcome_stats.output.aggregations.by_disposition.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'false_positive' or b.key == 'dismissed' %}{% assign _fp = _fp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _fp }}"
        avg_triage_confidence: "{{ steps.triage_stats.output.aggregations.avg_conf.value | default: 0 }}"
        trusted_agent_count: "{{ steps.trust_snapshot.output.hits.hits | size | default: 0 }}"
        decision: "{% assign _cur = steps.current_state.output.aggregations.latest.hits.hits.0._source.level | default: 2 %}{% assign _tp = 0 %}{% assign _fp = 0 %}{% assign _other = 0 %}{% for b in steps.outcome_stats.output.aggregations.by_disposition.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'true_positive' or b.key == 'case_created' or b.key == 'responded' %}{% assign _tp = _tp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% elsif b.key == 'false_positive' or b.key == 'dismissed' %}{% assign _fp = _fp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% else %}{% assign _other = _other | plus: b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% assign _total = _tp | plus: _fp | plus: _other %}{% if _total < consts.min_outcomes_required %}maintain_insufficient_data{% else %}{% assign _det_num = _tp | times: 1000 %}{% assign _det = _det_num | divided_by: _total %}{% assign _fp_num = _fp | times: 1000 %}{% assign _fpr = _fp_num | divided_by: _total %}{% assign _tc = steps.trust_snapshot.output.hits.hits | size | default: 0 %}{% if _det >= 800 and _fpr <= 300 and _tc >= 1 %}increase{% elsif _det < 500 or _fpr > 600 %}decrease{% else %}maintain{% endif %}{% endif %}"
        reasoning: "{% assign _cur = steps.current_state.output.aggregations.latest.hits.hits.0._source.level | default: 2 %}detection/FP/trust-based escalation, current level={{ _cur }}"

  # ── Launch a difficulty-tagged attack command so Caldera operates at
  #    the CURRENT level. The Caldera dispatcher polls this index.
  - name: launch_attack
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-attack-commands
      refresh: "wait_for"
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        status: "pending"
        source: "soc-difficulty-controller"
        difficulty: "{% assign _cur = steps.current_state.output.aggregations.latest.hits.hits.0._source.level | default: 2 %}{% assign _tp = 0 %}{% assign _fp = 0 %}{% assign _other = 0 %}{% for b in steps.outcome_stats.output.aggregations.by_disposition.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'true_positive' or b.key == 'case_created' or b.key == 'responded' %}{% assign _tp = _tp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% elsif b.key == 'false_positive' or b.key == 'dismissed' %}{% assign _fp = _fp | plus: b.doc_count %}{% else %}{% assign _other = _other | plus: b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% assign _total = _tp | plus: _fp | plus: _other %}{% if _total < consts.min_outcomes_required %}{{ _cur }}{% else %}{% assign _det_num = _tp | times: 1000 %}{% assign _det = _det_num | divided_by: _total %}{% assign _fp_num = _fp | times: 1000 %}{% assign _fpr = _fp_num | divided_by: _total %}{% assign _tc = steps.trust_snapshot.output.hits.hits | size | default: 0 %}{% if _det >= 800 and _fpr <= 300 and _tc >= 1 %}{% if _cur < consts.max_level %}{% assign _new = _cur | plus: 1 %}{{ _new }}{% else %}{{ _cur }}{% endif %}{% elsif _det < 500 or _fpr > 600 %}{% if _cur > consts.min_level %}{% assign _new = _cur | minus: 1 %}{{ _new }}{% else %}{{ _cur }}{% endif %}{% else %}{{ _cur }}{% endif %}{% endif %}"
        operation_profile: "{% assign _raw = steps.current_state.output.aggregations.latest.hits.hits.0._source.level | default: 2 %}{% assign _cur = _raw | plus: 0 %}{% if _cur <= 1 %}basic_recon{% elsif _cur == 2 %}commodity_malware{% elsif _cur == 3 %}living_off_the_land{% elsif _cur == 4 %}targeted_apt{% else %}nation_state_simulation{% endif %}"

  - name: heartbeat
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: difficulty_controller_heartbeat
        source: "soc-difficulty-controller"
        version: "v2-deterministic"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Difficulty Controller v2 tick complete (deterministic, no-LLM)"

definition.name: SOC Difficulty Controller
definition.description:
Performance-gated difficulty escalation for Caldera adversary emulation. Runs every 15 minutes (down from 30m so the system adapts faster).
Deterministic decision (no LLM -- previous LLM impl returned null 100% of the time because the prompt needed fields that aren't in .soc-outcomes).
Signals (last 24h):
  * detection_rate    = (case_created + responded + true_positive) / total
  * fp_rate           = (false_positive + dismissed) / total
  * avg_triage_conf   = mean of triage_classification.confidence (%)
  * trust_avg         = mean trust_score across trusted+probationary agents

Disposition mapping (reality of the current pipeline):
  * case_created / responded / true_positive  -> TP-equivalent (positive)
  * false_positive / dismissed                -> FP-equivalent (negative)
  * triaged / other                           -> in-flight, not counted

Rules (applied in order, first match wins):
  * detection_rate >= 0.80 AND fp_rate <= 0.30 AND trust_avg >= 0.70
      -> INCREASE level (cap 5)
  * detection_rate <  0.50 OR  fp_rate >  0.60
      -> DECREASE level (floor 1)
  * otherwise
      -> MAINTAIN

Output:
  1. Fresh doc in .soc-difficulty-state with level + all metrics
  2. One attack_command in .soc-attack-commands with difficulty=level so
     the Caldera dispatcher picks up a harder/easier operation next tick

results.name: SOC Trust Scorer
results.description:
Periodically computes trust scores per evolution tier and per source agent based on recommendation approval/rejection history AND post-apply rollback outcomes. Enables graduated autonomy — tiers with high approval rates can auto-approve, and agents with repeated rollbacks can be automatically quarantined.
Feedback model (deterministic, per agent, last 7 days):
  applied successfully   -> +0.02 per applied intent (cap 1.0)
  rolled_back            -> -0.10 per rollback (floor 0.0)
  rejected_drift / loop  -> -0.02 per rejection
  rejected_backtest      -> -0.05 per rejection

Tiering (trust_score + recent_rollbacks):
  trust >= 0.90 AND rollbacks_24h == 0  -> tier=trusted (auto-apply default)
  trust >= 0.70 AND rollbacks_24h <= 1  -> tier=probationary (auto-apply with backtest)
  trust <  0.70 OR  rollbacks_24h >= 2  -> tier=observing (exception queue)
  rollbacks_24h >= 3                    -> tier=quarantined (all intents -> .soc-dead-letter)

The applier's trust-tier gate (future) reads these rows and routes intents accordingly. The observer writes rolled_back markers that feed back here, closing the trust loop.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Trust Scorer
description: >
  Periodically computes trust scores per evolution tier and per source agent
  based on recommendation approval/rejection history AND post-apply rollback
  outcomes. Enables graduated autonomy — tiers with high approval rates can
  auto-approve, and agents with repeated rollbacks can be automatically
  quarantined.

  Feedback model (deterministic, per agent, last 7 days):
    applied successfully   -> +0.02 per applied intent (cap 1.0)
    rolled_back            -> -0.10 per rollback (floor 0.0)
    rejected_drift / loop  -> -0.02 per rejection
    rejected_backtest      -> -0.05 per rejection

  Tiering (trust_score + recent_rollbacks):
    trust >= 0.90 AND rollbacks_24h == 0  -> tier=trusted (auto-apply default)
    trust >= 0.70 AND rollbacks_24h <= 1  -> tier=probationary (auto-apply with backtest)
    trust <  0.70 OR  rollbacks_24h >= 2  -> tier=observing (exception queue)
    rollbacks_24h >= 3                    -> tier=quarantined (all intents -> .soc-dead-letter)

  The applier's trust-tier gate (future) reads these rows and routes intents
  accordingly. The observer writes rolled_back markers that feed back here,
  closing the trust loop.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 30m
  - type: manual

steps:
  # ── Gather recommendation history (last 7 days) ───────────────────
  - name: get_rec_stats
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      size: 0
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-7d"
      aggs:
        by_type:
          terms:
            field: "type"
            size: 20
          aggs:
            statuses:
              terms:
                field: "status"
                size: 10

  # ── Compute and write trust scores per tier ────────────────────────
  - name: compute_trust
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-meta-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        Analyze the recommendation statistics below and compute trust scores per tier.

        Statistics:
        {{ steps.get_rec_stats.output.aggregations | json }}

        For each type (rule_tuning = Tier 1, agent_evolution = Tier 2/3), compute:
        1. total_proposals: total recommendations
        2. approved_count: approved + applied
        3. rejected_count: rejected
        4. approval_rate: approved_count / total_proposals (0-1.0)
        5. auto_approve_eligible: true if approval_rate >= 0.90 AND total_proposals >= 5

        Output ONLY JSON array:
        [{"tier": "tier_1_workflows", "total_proposals": N, "approved_count": N, "rejected_count": N,
          "applied_count": N, "failed_count": N, "approval_rate": 0.XX,
          "auto_approve_eligible": true/false, "confidence_threshold": 0.95, "window_days": 7}]
    timeout: 120s

  - name: write_trust_scores
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-trust-scores
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        source: "soc-trust-scorer"
        scores: "{{ steps.compute_trust.output | json }}"

  # ── Per-agent trust via deterministic aggregation ─────────────────────
  # This runs alongside the LLM scorer above but writes rows the applier
  # can query directly. No LLM, no interpretation — pure counting.
  - name: per_agent_outcomes
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term: { type: "mutation_intent" }
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-7d"
      aggs:
        by_source:
          terms:
            field: "source"
            size: 30
          aggs:
            by_status:
              terms:
                field: "status"
                size: 20

  - name: recent_rollbacks
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term: { status: "rolled_back" }
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-24h"
      aggs:
        by_source:
          terms:
            field: "source"
            size: 30

  # For every agent seen in the last 7 days, index one trust row with
  # computed score + tier. This is the row the applier's trust-tier gate
  # (future) reads to decide auto-apply vs exception queue.
  - name: gate_has_per_agent_buckets
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _n = steps.per_agent_outcomes.output.aggregations.by_source.buckets | size | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _n > 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

  - name: per_agent_trust_rows
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.per_agent_outcomes.output.aggregations.by_source.buckets }}"
    if: "steps.gate_has_per_agent_buckets.output: yes"
    steps:
      - name: write_row
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-trust-scores
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            source: "soc-trust-scorer"
            scope: "per_agent"
            agent_id: "{{ foreach.item.key }}"
            window_days: 7
            counts: "{{ foreach.item.by_status.buckets | json }}"
            total_intents: "{{ foreach.item.doc_count }}"
            rollbacks_24h: "{% assign _src = foreach.item.key %}{% assign _rb = 0 %}{% for b in steps.recent_rollbacks.output.aggregations.by_source.buckets %}{% if b.key == _src %}{% assign _rb = b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _rb }}"
            trust_tier: "{% assign _src = foreach.item.key %}{% assign _rb = 0 %}{% for b in steps.recent_rollbacks.output.aggregations.by_source.buckets %}{% if b.key == _src %}{% assign _rb = b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% assign _applied = 0 %}{% assign _rejected = 0 %}{% for b in foreach.item.by_status.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'applied' %}{% assign _applied = b.doc_count %}{% elsif b.key == 'rejected' or b.key == 'rejected_backtest' or b.key == 'rejected_drift' or b.key == 'rejected_loop' %}{% assign _rejected = b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% assign _score_num = _applied | times: 2 %}{% assign _score_denom = _applied | plus: _rejected | plus: 1 %}{% if _rb >= 3 %}quarantined{% elsif _applied >= 5 and _rb == 0 and _rejected == 0 %}trusted{% elsif _rb <= 1 and _rejected <= 2 %}probationary{% else %}observing{% endif %}"
            approval_rate: "{% assign _applied = 0 %}{% assign _rejected = 0 %}{% for b in foreach.item.by_status.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'applied' %}{% assign _applied = b.doc_count %}{% elsif b.key == 'rejected' or b.key == 'rejected_backtest' or b.key == 'rejected_drift' or b.key == 'rejected_loop' %}{% assign _rejected = b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% assign _total = _applied | plus: _rejected %}{% if _total == 0 %}0{% else %}{{ _applied | divided_by: _total }}{% endif %}"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Trust Scorer: computed and stored trust scores (legacy aggregate + per-agent rows)"

definition.name: SOC Trust Scorer
definition.description:
Periodically computes trust scores per evolution tier and per source agent based on recommendation approval/rejection history AND post-apply rollback outcomes. Enables graduated autonomy — tiers with high approval rates can auto-approve, and agents with repeated rollbacks can be automatically quarantined.
Feedback model (deterministic, per agent, last 7 days):
  applied successfully   -> +0.02 per applied intent (cap 1.0)
  rolled_back            -> -0.10 per rollback (floor 0.0)
  rejected_drift / loop  -> -0.02 per rejection
  rejected_backtest      -> -0.05 per rejection

Tiering (trust_score + recent_rollbacks):
  trust >= 0.90 AND rollbacks_24h == 0  -> tier=trusted (auto-apply default)
  trust >= 0.70 AND rollbacks_24h <= 1  -> tier=probationary (auto-apply with backtest)
  trust <  0.70 OR  rollbacks_24h >= 2  -> tier=observing (exception queue)
  rollbacks_24h >= 3                    -> tier=quarantined (all intents -> .soc-dead-letter)

The applier's trust-tier gate (future) reads these rows and routes intents accordingly. The observer writes rolled_back markers that feed back here, closing the trust loop.

with.message:
Analyze the recommendation statistics below and compute trust scores per tier.
Statistics: {{ steps.get_rec_stats.output.aggregations | json }}
For each type (rule_tuning = Tier 1, agent_evolution = Tier 2/3), compute: 1. total_proposals: total recommendations 2. approved_count: approved + applied 3. rejected_count: rejected 4. approval_rate: approved_count / total_proposals (0-1.0) 5. auto_approve_eligible: true if approval_rate >= 0.90 AND total_proposals >= 5
Output ONLY JSON array: [{"tier": "tier_1_workflows", "total_proposals": N, "approved_count": N, "rejected_count": N,
  "applied_count": N, "failed_count": N, "approval_rate": 0.XX,
  "auto_approve_eligible": true/false, "confidence_threshold": 0.95, "window_days": 7}]
{%- assign _n = steps.per_agent_outcomes.output.aggregations.by_source.buckets | size | default: 0 -%} {% if _n > 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

document.rollbacks_24h: {% assign _src = foreach.item.key %}{% assign _rb = 0 %}{% for b in steps.recent_rollbacks.output.aggregations.by_source.buckets %}{% if b.key == _src %}{% assign _rb = b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _rb }}
document.trust_tier: {% assign _src = foreach.item.key %}{% assign _rb = 0 %}{% for b in steps.recent_rollbacks.output.aggregations.by_source.buckets %}{% if b.key == _src %}{% assign _rb = b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% assign _applied = 0 %}{% assign _rejected = 0 %}{% for b in foreach.item.by_status.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'applied' %}{% assign _applied = b.doc_count %}{% elsif b.key == 'rejected' or b.key == 'rejected_backtest' or b.key == 'rejected_drift' or b.key == 'rejected_loop' %}{% assign _rejected = b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% assign _score_num = _applied | times: 2 %}{% assign _score_denom = _applied | plus: _rejected | plus: 1 %}{% if _rb >= 3 %}quarantined{% elsif _applied >= 5 and _rb == 0 and _rejected == 0 %}trusted{% elsif _rb <= 1 and _rejected <= 2 %}probationary{% else %}observing{% endif %}

results.name: SOC Recommendation Applier
results.description: Picks up recommendations with approved status or approved sub-items and executes them using the SOC Recommendation Applier Agent with self-management tools. Includes a validation step that confirms approved items exist before execution. Runs every 5 minutes to process approved items from the review queue.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Recommendation Applier
description: >
  Picks up recommendations with approved status or approved sub-items and executes them
  using the SOC Recommendation Applier Agent with self-management tools.
  Includes a validation step that confirms approved items exist before execution.
  Runs every 5 minutes to process approved items from the review queue.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 5m
  - type: manual

steps:
  - name: get_approved_recs
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      query:
        bool:
          must:
            - terms:
                status:
                  - approved
          must_not:
            - term:
                status: applied
            - term:
                status: failed
      size: 3
      _source:
        - rec_id
        - type
        - source
        - status
        - title
        - summary
        - details
        - sub_items
        - confidence

  - name: log_check
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Applier: found {{ steps.get_approved_recs.output.hits.total.value }} approved recommendations"

  # Early-exit when there are no approved recommendations. Runs only when
  # total.value == 0 and ends the workflow. If alerts > 0, this step is skipped
  # and the pipeline continues to apply_recommendations below.
  - name: log_nothing
    type: console
    if: "steps.get_approved_recs.output.hits.total.value: 0"
    with:
      message: "Applier: no approved recommendations to process"
    end: true

  - name: apply_recommendations
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-rec-applier-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        You are the SOC Recommendation Applier. Execute ONLY the approved items below.

        CANDIDATE RECOMMENDATIONS:
        {{ steps.get_approved_recs.output.hits.hits | json }}

        EXECUTION RULES:
        1. Check each document's sub_items field:
           - If sub_items exist: only execute sub-items where sub_items[N].status = "approved"
           - If NO sub_items but parent status = "approved": execute everything
           - If parent status = "pending" and no approved sub_items: SKIP entirely
        2. If sub_items[N].status = "applied": SKIP (already done)

        SELF-VALIDATION:
        Before executing any action, validate:
        - For rule operations: confirm the rule_id exists using manage_detection_rules
        - For workflow deployment: validate_workflow BEFORE deploy_workflow
        - For skill creation: verify tool_ids are valid
        - For agent patches: verify target agent exists
        If validation fails, mark the item as "failed" with the validation error and move on.

        FOR RULE TUNING RECOMMENDATIONS (type=rule_tuning):
        - add_exception / update_exception: Use platform.core.manage_detection_rules with operation='patch'
        - raise_threshold / lower_threshold: Use operation='patch' with the patch_fields
        - enable / disable: Use operation='enable' or 'disable'
        - create: Use operation='create' with enabled=false

        FOR AGENT EVOLUTION RECOMMENDATIONS (type=agent_evolution):
        - create_workflow: Use platform.workflows.deploy_workflow
        - create_skill: Use platform.core.manage_skills
        - enrich_agent / refine_agent: Use platform.core.update_agent
        - create_agent: Use platform.core.create_agent + deploy_workflow

        IMPORTANT:
        - Validate before executing. If validation fails, skip the item and report the error.
        - If nothing needs to be done, respond: {"applied": [], "skipped": [...], "nothing_to_do": true}
    timeout: 300s

  - name: log_application
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: "recommendation_applied"
        source: "soc-recommendation-applier"
        details: "{{ steps.apply_recommendations.output | json }}"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Applier: recommendation processing complete"

results.name: SOC Forensic Summarizer
results.description:
Polls Kibana Cases every 15 minutes for closed cases that do not yet have a forensic summary. For each, aggregates IOCs, YARA rules, attribution, and exceptions produced during the investigation, then emits ONE immutable document to .soc-forensic-summary (op_type=create, case_id as doc_id).
This replaces the PM vision's "forensic post-investigation panel": the dashboard row reads this index directly, producing a consolidated view of every durable artifact captured for each investigation.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Forensic Summarizer
description: >
  Polls Kibana Cases every 15 minutes for closed cases that do not yet have a
  forensic summary. For each, aggregates IOCs, YARA rules, attribution, and
  exceptions produced during the investigation, then emits ONE immutable
  document to .soc-forensic-summary (op_type=create, case_id as doc_id).

  This replaces the PM vision's "forensic post-investigation panel": the
  dashboard row reads this index directly, producing a consolidated view of
  every durable artifact captured for each investigation.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 15m
  - type: manual

steps:
  - name: poll_closed_cases
    type: kibana.request
    with:
      method: GET
      path: /api/cases/_find?status=closed&perPage=50&sortField=updatedAt&sortOrder=desc

  - name: existing_summaries
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-forensic-summary"
      size: 500
      _source: ["case_id"]
      query:
        match_all: {}

  - name: emit_summaries
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.poll_closed_cases.output.cases }}"
    steps:
      # Pull investigation artefacts for this case from the hunt/outcome indices.
      - name: hunt_findings
        type: elasticsearch.search
        with:
          index: ".soc-hunt-findings"
          size: 100
          query:
            bool:
              filter:
                - term: {case_id.keyword: "{{ foreach.item.id }}"}

      # Compute-and-match: has this case already been summarized?
      - name: gate_needs_summary
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign seen_ids = '' -%}
            {%- for d in steps.existing_summaries.output.hits.hits -%}
              {%- assign seen_ids = seen_ids | append: ',' | append: d._source.case_id -%}
            {%- endfor -%}
            {%- assign needle = ',' | append: foreach.item.id -%}
            {% if seen_ids contains needle %}no{% else %}yes{% endif %}

      - name: compose_summary
        type: ai.agent
        agent-id: soc-triage-agent
        connector-id: opus
        with:
          message: >
            The following Kibana case has just been closed. Produce a durable
            forensic summary (JSON only) consolidating every meaningful artefact
            from the investigation. Cite only data that appears in the inputs
            below — DO NOT invent IOCs.

            case = {{ foreach.item | json }}
            hunt_findings = {{ steps.hunt_findings.output.hits.hits | json }}

            Return ONLY:
            {
              "verdict": "true_positive|false_positive|benign_true_positive|inconclusive",
              "iocs":              [ {"type":"...","value":"...","confidence":0.0} ],
              "yara_rules":        [ {"name":"...","body":"...","added_to_rules_index": false } ],
              "attribution":       { "actor": null, "campaign": null, "ttps": [] },
              "exceptions_created":[ {"rule_id":"...","exception_id":"..."} ],
              "summary_markdown":  "<markdown string, <= 2000 chars>"
            }
        timeout: 120s
        if: "steps.gate_needs_summary.output: yes"

      # Compute-and-match: did compose_summary actually produce output?
      - name: gate_summary_produced
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {% if steps.compose_summary.output.verdict %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      - name: write_summary
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-forensic-summary
          id: "{{ foreach.item.id }}"
          op_type: create
          document:
            case_id: "{{ foreach.item.id }}"
            closed_at: "{{ foreach.item.closedAt | default: foreach.item.updatedAt }}"
            verdict: "{{ steps.compose_summary.output.verdict | default: 'inconclusive' }}"
            iocs: "{{ steps.compose_summary.output.iocs | default: [] }}"
            yara_rules: "{{ steps.compose_summary.output.yara_rules | default: [] }}"
            attribution: "{{ steps.compose_summary.output.attribution }}"
            exceptions_created: "{{ steps.compose_summary.output.exceptions_created | default: [] }}"
            summary_markdown: "{{ steps.compose_summary.output.summary_markdown | default: 'No summary available.' }}"
        if: "steps.gate_summary_produced.output: yes"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Forensic summarizer tick complete ({{ steps.poll_closed_cases.output.cases | size | default: 0 }} closed case(s) inspected)."

results.name: SOC Skill Metrics Roller
results.description: Hourly rollup: for every skill observed in .soc-evolution-log (source of the last 7 days), upsert one document into .soc-skill-metrics with invocation counts, success rate, and ROI estimates (hours_saved, cost_saved). This is the source-of-truth for the "Skills ROI" dashboard row.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Skill Metrics Roller
description: >
  Hourly rollup: for every skill observed in .soc-evolution-log (source
  of the last 7 days), upsert one document into .soc-skill-metrics with
  invocation counts, success rate, and ROI estimates (hours_saved, cost_saved).
  This is the source-of-truth for the "Skills ROI" dashboard row.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 1h
  - type: manual

consts:
  baseline_minutes_saved_per_success: 25
  analyst_hourly_rate_usd: 90

steps:
  - name: rollup
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-evolution-log"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-7d"
            - exists:
                field: "source"
      aggs:
        by_skill:
          terms:
            field: "source"
            size: 500
          aggs:
            invocations_24h:
              filter:
                range:
                  "@timestamp":
                    gte: "now-24h"
            invocations_7d:
              filter:
                range:
                  "@timestamp":
                    gte: "now-7d"
            success_24h:
              filter:
                bool:
                  must:
                    - range:
                        "@timestamp":
                          gte: "now-24h"
                    - term: {result: "applied"}
            failure_24h:
              filter:
                bool:
                  must:
                    - range:
                        "@timestamp":
                          gte: "now-24h"
                    - terms:
                        result: ["failure", "validation_failed", "blocked_canonical", "blocked_loop", "blocked_budget", "blocked_cooldown"]
            success_7d:
              filter:
                bool:
                  must:
                    - range:
                        "@timestamp":
                          gte: "now-7d"
                    - term: {result: "applied"}
            failure_7d:
              filter:
                bool:
                  must:
                    - range:
                        "@timestamp":
                          gte: "now-7d"
                    - terms:
                        result: ["failure", "validation_failed", "blocked_canonical", "blocked_loop", "blocked_budget", "blocked_cooldown"]
            last_run:
              max:
                field: "@timestamp"

  - name: gate_has_skill_buckets
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _n = steps.rollup.output.aggregations.by_skill.buckets | size | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _n > 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

  - name: upsert_metrics
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.rollup.output.aggregations.by_skill.buckets }}"
    if: "steps.gate_has_skill_buckets.output: yes"
    steps:
      - name: write_doc
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-skill-metrics
          id: "{{ foreach.item.key }}"
          document:
            skill_id: "{{ foreach.item.key }}"
            invocations_24h: "{{ foreach.item.invocations_24h.doc_count | default: 0 }}"
            invocations_7d: "{{ foreach.item.invocations_7d.doc_count  | default: 0 }}"
            success_count_24h: "{{ foreach.item.success_24h.doc_count | default: 0 }}"
            failure_count_24h: "{{ foreach.item.failure_24h.doc_count | default: 0 }}"
            success_count_7d: "{{ foreach.item.success_7d.doc_count  | default: 0 }}"
            failure_count_7d: "{{ foreach.item.failure_7d.doc_count  | default: 0 }}"
            success_rate_7d: >-
              {% assign s = foreach.item.success_7d.doc_count | default: 0 %}
              {% assign f = foreach.item.failure_7d.doc_count | default: 0 %}
              {% assign total = s | plus: f %}
              {% if total > 0 %}{{ s | times: 1.0 | divided_by: total }}{% else %}0{% endif %}
            hours_saved_est_7d: >-
              {% assign s = foreach.item.success_7d.doc_count | default: 0 %}
              {{ s | times: consts.baseline_minutes_saved_per_success | divided_by: 60.0 }}
            cost_saved_usd_est_7d: >-
              {% assign s = foreach.item.success_7d.doc_count | default: 0 %}
              {% assign hrs = s | times: consts.baseline_minutes_saved_per_success | divided_by: 60.0 %}
              {{ hrs | times: consts.analyst_hourly_rate_usd }}
            baseline_minutes_saved: "{{ consts.baseline_minutes_saved_per_success }}"
            analyst_hourly_rate_usd: "{{ consts.analyst_hourly_rate_usd }}"
            estimate: true
            last_run_ts: "{{ foreach.item.last_run.value_as_string | default: null }}"

  - name: log_done

results.name: SOC Capability Gap Analyzer
results.description: Proactive capability gap detection. Inventories all available tools, data sources, detection rules, and SOC metrics, then uses the meta-agent with the capability-gap-analyzer skill to discover opportunities the system isn't exploiting. Writes findings to .soc-recommendations with type capability_gap for human review.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Capability Gap Analyzer
description: >
  Proactive capability gap detection. Inventories all available tools, data sources,
  detection rules, and SOC metrics, then uses the meta-agent with the capability-gap-analyzer
  skill to discover opportunities the system isn't exploiting. Writes findings to
  .soc-recommendations with type capability_gap for human review.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 4h
  - type: manual

steps:
  # ── Inventory available data sources (lightweight queries) ────────
  - name: get_soc_indices
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-*"
      size: 0
      aggs:
        indices:
          terms:
            field: "_index"
            size: 50

  - name: get_log_indices
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: "logs-*"
      size: 0
      aggs:
        indices:
          terms:
            field: "_index"
            size: 20

  # ── Gather SOC performance data ──────────────────────────────────
  - name: get_triage_results
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-triage-results"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-7d"
      size: 50
  - name: get_outcomes
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-outcomes"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-7d"
      size: 50
  - name: get_response_actions
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-response-actions"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-7d"
      size: 50
  - name: get_recommendations_stats
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-7d"
      size: 0
      aggs:
        by_type:
          terms:
            field: "type"
            size: 20
          aggs:
            statuses:
              terms:
                field: "status"
                size: 10
        rejected_reasons:
          filter:
            term:
              status: rejected
          aggs:
            by_source:
              terms:
                field: "source"
                size: 10

  - name: get_coverage_gaps
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-coverage-gaps"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-7d"
      size: 20
  - name: log_start
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Gap Analyzer: starting proactive capability gap analysis"

  # ── Run gap analysis ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: analyze_gaps
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-meta-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        Perform a proactive capability gap analysis using your capability-gap-analyzer skill.

        Your task is to discover things the AutoSOC COULD do but DOESN'T. Analyze unused tools,
        untapped data sources, kill chain coverage gaps, response gaps, confidence calibration
        drift, and stale baselines.

        AVAILABLE DATA (summaries only — use your tools to query details):

        SOC indices (aggregated doc counts):
        {{ steps.get_soc_indices.output.aggregations | json }}

        Log indices (aggregated doc counts):
        {{ steps.get_log_indices.output.aggregations | json }}

        Triage results count (7d): {{ steps.get_triage_results.output.hits.total.value }}
        Outcomes count (7d): {{ steps.get_outcomes.output.hits.total.value }}
        Response actions count (7d): {{ steps.get_response_actions.output.hits.total.value }}

        Recommendation statistics (7d):
        {{ steps.get_recommendations_stats.output.aggregations | json }}

        Coverage gaps count: {{ steps.get_coverage_gaps.output.hits.total.value }}

        KNOWN REGISTERED TOOLS (from Agent Builder allow list):
        security: alerts, entity_risk_score, attack_discovery_search, security_labs_search,
          get_entity, search_entities, create_detection_rule
        platform.core: execute_esql, generate_esql, search, list_indices, get_index_mapping,
          get_document_by_id, create_visualization, product_documentation, integration_knowledge,
          cases, sml_search, sml_attach, index_explorer
        management: create_agent, update_agent, manage_skills, manage_detection_rules
        workflows: deploy_workflow, validate_workflow, get_step_definitions, list_workflows

        CURRENT SOC AGENTS: soc-triage-agent, soc-meta-agent, soc-deteng-agent (Principal DetEng — rule authoring),
          soc-signal-quality-agent (FP/TP tuning), soc-rec-applier-agent, soc-autonomous-applier-agent
        CURRENT SOC SKILLS: soc-health-check, soc-difficulty-evaluation, soc-architecture-review,
          soc-capability-gap-analyzer, soc-attack-chain-analysis, soc-proactive-hunt, soc-containment-playbook

        Use your tools (search, execute_esql, list_indices) to query specific details as needed.
        Compare which registered tools are used by agents vs which are available but unused.
        Identify the highest-impact gaps and produce structured findings AND concrete mutation intents.

        Self-validate: every finding must include metrics-based justification.

        Respond with JSON:
        {
          "findings":        [ { "gap": "...", "severity": "low|med|high", "evidence": [...] } ],
          "summary":         "...",
          "top_3_priorities": [ ... ],
          "intents":         [ /* ZERO or more mutation_intent objects — SAME envelope as soc-meta (title, summary, reasoning, confidence, track, housekeeping, expected_impact, evidence, details{artifact_type, artifact_id (auto-*), op, expected_ownership, reason, new_definition?, patch?, dependencies:[]}) */ ]
        }
    timeout: 600s

  # ── Write results ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: write_evolution_log
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-evolution-log
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        source: "soc-gap-analyzer"
        event_type: "capability_gap_analysis"
        analysis_output: "{{ steps.analyze_gaps.output | json }}"

  - name: write_recommendation
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-recommendations
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        rec_id: "gap-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M%S' }}"
        type: "capability_gap"
        source: "soc-gap-analyzer"
        source_doc_id: "{{ steps.write_evolution_log.output._id }}"
        status: "pending"
        title: "Capability Gap Analysis - {{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M' }}"
        summary: "{{ steps.analyze_gaps.output.message }}"
        details: "{{ steps.analyze_gaps.output | json }}"
        reasoning: "Proactive capability gap detection"
        confidence: 75
        track: "deterministic"
        expected_impact: "{{ steps.analyze_gaps.output.expected_impact }}"
        evidence: "{{ steps.analyze_gaps.output.evidence | default: [] }}"

  # ── Fan out concrete mutation intents (if any) ───────────────────
  # The aggregate `capability_gap` doc above is analyst-facing. Any concrete
  # intents the meta-agent proposed are materialized here as individual
  # mutation_intent recommendations for soc-autonomous-applier.
  - name: gate_has_gap_intents
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _n = steps.analyze_gaps.output.intents | size | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _n > 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

  - name: write_mutation_intents
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.analyze_gaps.output.intents }}"
    if: "steps.gate_has_gap_intents.output: yes"
    steps:
      - name: write_intent
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-recommendations
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            rec_id: "gap-mi-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M%S' }}-{{ foreach.index }}"
            schema_version: 2
            type: "mutation_intent"
            source: "soc-gap-analyzer"
            source_doc_id: "{{ steps.write_evolution_log.output._id }}"
            status: "pending"
            title: "{{ foreach.item.title }}"
            summary: "{{ foreach.item.summary }}"
            reasoning: "{{ foreach.item.reasoning | default: 'Capability gap auto-remediation' }}"
            confidence: "{{ foreach.item.confidence | default: 75 }}"
            track: "{{ foreach.item.track | default: 'agentic' }}"
            housekeeping: "{{ foreach.item.housekeeping | default: false }}"
            expected_impact: "{{ foreach.item.expected_impact | default: empty }}"
            evidence: "{{ foreach.item.evidence | default: empty }}"
            details: "{{ foreach.item.details }}"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        Gap Analyzer: analysis complete — findings written and
        {{ steps.analyze_gaps.output.intents | size | default: 0 }} mutation intent(s) dispatched.

results.name: SOC Detection Engineering
results.description:
Scheduled rule health review. Runs in two phases so that tactical tuning and strategic authoring have clear ownership and blast radius:
Phase 1 — Signal Quality: tunes existing rules (exceptions, thresholds)
          based on triage outcomes. Emits `redesign_required` for rules that
          are structurally noisy.

Phase 2 — Principal Detection Engineering: closes coverage gaps with new
          rules (always DISABLED) and redesigns rules flagged in Phase 1.

Both phases write recommendations into .soc-recommendations with distinct `source` values so the human reviewer and the soc-autonomous-applier can route them correctly.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Detection Engineering
description: >
  Scheduled rule health review. Runs in two phases so that tactical tuning and
  strategic authoring have clear ownership and blast radius:

  Phase 1 — Signal Quality: tunes existing rules (exceptions, thresholds)
            based on triage outcomes. Emits `redesign_required` for rules that
            are structurally noisy.

  Phase 2 — Principal Detection Engineering: closes coverage gaps with new
            rules (always DISABLED) and redesigns rules flagged in Phase 1.

  Both phases write recommendations into .soc-recommendations with distinct
  `source` values so the human reviewer and the soc-autonomous-applier can
  route them correctly.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 30m
  - type: manual

steps:
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shared inputs
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  - name: get_recent_outcomes
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-outcomes"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-6h"
      size: 50
  - name: get_coverage_gaps
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-coverage-gaps"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-24h"
      size: 20
  - name: get_rejected_recs
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - terms:
                source: ["soc-deteng", "soc-deteng-agent", "soc-signal-quality-agent"]
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-7d"
          should:
            - term:
                status: rejected
            - exists:
                field: sub_items
          minimum_should_match: 1
      size: 20
      _source:
        - title
        - summary
        - rejection_reason
        - reviewed_at
        - sub_items
        - source

  - name: get_open_redesign_flags
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-evolution-log"
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term: {source: "soc-signal-quality-agent"}
            - term: {event_type: "redesign_required"}
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-24h"
      size: 20
      _source:
        - "@timestamp"
        - rule_id
        - analysis_output

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Phase 1 — Signal Quality Agent (tactical FP/TP tuning)
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  - name: analyze_signal_quality
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-signal-quality-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        Tune existing detection rules using recent triage outcomes as ground truth.

        Follow the tuning matrix in your instructions. DO NOT create new rules.
        If a rule is structurally noisy, emit `redesign_required` and let the
        Principal Detection Engineer rewrite it in Phase 2.

        IMPORTANT — structured patch envelope is mandatory for rule updates:
        every `intents[]` entry where `details.artifact_type="rule"` AND
        `details.op="update"` MUST carry `details.patch` with fields
        rule_id, action, patch_fields, current_values, impact_prediction —
        see the Structured Patch Envelope section of your instructions.
        Prose-only intents are dead-lettered at ingest. ALWAYS call
        `platform.core.manage_detection_rules` with `operation='read'` (or
        `find`) first so `current_values` reflects the live rule state —
        the backtester and drift gate both depend on it.

        Previously rejected recommendations (learn from these — do NOT repeat):
        {{ steps.get_rejected_recs.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Recent outcomes (last 6h):
        {{ steps.get_recent_outcomes.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Respond with JSON:
        {
          "findings": [ /* per-rule tuning observations */ ],
          "summary":  "...",
          "intents":  [ /* one mutation_intent per exception / threshold / disable.
                           Envelope: {
                             title, summary, confidence, track:"agentic",
                             evidence[], expected_impact{},
                             details: {
                               artifact_type: "rule" | "exception",
                               artifact_id: "auto-*",   // must be autosoc-owned
                               op: "update" | "enable" | "disable",
                               expected_ownership: "autosoc",
                               reason: "<>=20 chars>",
                               // For artifact_type="rule" AND op="update", patch MUST
                               // be a structured rule_patch (see agent instructions).
                               patch: { rule_id, action, patch_fields, current_values,
                                        impact_prediction }
                             }
                           } */ ]
        }
    timeout: 300s

  - name: write_signal_quality_evolution_log
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-evolution-log
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        source: "soc-signal-quality-agent"
        event_type: "signal_quality_tuning"
        analysis_output: "{{ steps.analyze_signal_quality.output | json }}"

  - name: write_signal_quality_recommendation
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-recommendations
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        rec_id: "signal-quality-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M%S' }}"
        type: "rule_tuning"
        source: "soc-signal-quality-agent"
        source_doc_id: "{{ steps.write_signal_quality_evolution_log.output._id }}"
        status: "pending"
        title: "Signal Quality tuning - {{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M' }}"
        summary: "{{ steps.analyze_signal_quality.output.message }}"
        details: "{{ steps.analyze_signal_quality.output | json }}"
        reasoning: "Tactical FP/TP tuning based on .soc-outcomes"
        confidence: 75
        track: "agentic"
        expected_impact: "{{ steps.analyze_signal_quality.output.expected_impact }}"
        evidence: "{{ steps.analyze_signal_quality.output.evidence | default: [] }}"

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Phase 2 — Principal Detection Engineering (strategic authoring)
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  - name: analyze_principal_deteng
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-deteng-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        Close coverage gaps with NEW rules (DISABLED), redesign rules flagged
        by the Signal Quality agent, and deprecate stale rules. Do NOT tune
        existing rules for FP/TP — that is Phase 1's job.

        Apply your instructions' validation rules on every new/redesigned rule:
        - execute the query against a 24h window
        - reject if >10k hits or catch-all
        - confirm fields exist in the target mapping
        - require a concrete MITRE tactic + technique

        Open redesign flags from Phase 1 (prioritize these):
        {{ steps.get_open_redesign_flags.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Coverage gaps (last 24h):
        {{ steps.get_coverage_gaps.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Signal Quality output from Phase 1 (for context):
        {{ steps.analyze_signal_quality.output | json }}

        Previously rejected recommendations (learn from these — do NOT repeat):
        {{ steps.get_rejected_recs.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Respond with JSON:
        {
          "findings": [ /* per-rule authoring/redesign observations */ ],
          "summary":  "...",
          "intents":  [ /* mutation_intent objects for each new/redesigned/retired rule
                           — details.artifact_type="rule", artifact_id="auto-*",
                           op="create|update|delete", expected_ownership="autosoc",
                           new_definition (full rule payload with enabled:false for new rules),
                           evidence[] (must cite coverage gap or redesign flag),
                           expected_impact{} with coverage_delta_pct or fp_reduction_pct */ ]
        }
    timeout: 300s

  - name: write_principal_evolution_log
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-evolution-log
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        source: "soc-deteng-agent"
        event_type: "principal_deteng_cycle"
        analysis_output: "{{ steps.analyze_principal_deteng.output | json }}"

  - name: write_principal_recommendation
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-recommendations
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        rec_id: "deteng-principal-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M%S' }}"
        type: "rule_authoring"
        source: "soc-deteng-agent"
        source_doc_id: "{{ steps.write_principal_evolution_log.output._id }}"
        status: "pending"
        title: "Principal DetEng cycle - {{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M' }}"
        summary: "{{ steps.analyze_principal_deteng.output.message }}"
        details: "{{ steps.analyze_principal_deteng.output | json }}"
        reasoning: "Strategic rule authoring driven by coverage gaps + Signal Quality redesign flags"
        confidence: 75
        track: "agentic"
        expected_impact: "{{ steps.analyze_principal_deteng.output.expected_impact }}"
        evidence: "{{ steps.analyze_principal_deteng.output.evidence | default: [] }}"

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Fan-out: materialize concrete mutation intents from BOTH phases
  # Each concrete intent becomes its own .soc-recommendations doc with
  # type=mutation_intent, which soc-autonomous-applier picks up under
  # governance gates.
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  - name: gate_has_signal_quality_intents
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _n = steps.analyze_signal_quality.output.intents | size | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _n > 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

  - name: write_signal_quality_intents
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.analyze_signal_quality.output.intents }}"
    if: "steps.gate_has_signal_quality_intents.output: yes"
    steps:
      - name: write_intent
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-recommendations
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            rec_id: "sq-mi-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M%S' }}-{{ foreach.index }}"
            schema_version: 2
            type: "mutation_intent"
            source: "soc-signal-quality-agent"
            source_doc_id: "{{ steps.write_signal_quality_evolution_log.output._id }}"
            status: "pending"
            title: "{{ foreach.item.title }}"
            summary: "{{ foreach.item.summary }}"
            reasoning: "{{ foreach.item.reasoning | default: 'Signal-quality tuning' }}"
            confidence: "{{ foreach.item.confidence | default: 75 }}"
            track: "{{ foreach.item.track | default: 'agentic' }}"
            housekeeping: "{{ foreach.item.housekeeping | default: false }}"
            expected_impact: "{{ foreach.item.expected_impact | default: empty }}"
            evidence: "{{ foreach.item.evidence | default: empty }}"
            details: "{{ foreach.item.details }}"

  - name: gate_has_principal_intents
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _n = steps.analyze_principal_deteng.output.intents | size | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _n > 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

  - name: write_principal_intents
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.analyze_principal_deteng.output.intents }}"
    if: "steps.gate_has_principal_intents.output: yes"
    steps:
      - name: write_principal_intent
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-recommendations
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            rec_id: "deteng-mi-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M%S' }}-{{ foreach.index }}"
            schema_version: 2
            type: "mutation_intent"
            source: "soc-deteng-agent"
            source_doc_id: "{{ steps.write_principal_evolution_log.output._id }}"
            status: "pending"
            title: "{{ foreach.item.title }}"
            summary: "{{ foreach.item.summary }}"
            reasoning: "{{ foreach.item.reasoning | default: 'Principal DetEng authoring' }}"
            confidence: "{{ foreach.item.confidence | default: 75 }}"
            track: "{{ foreach.item.track | default: 'agentic' }}"
            housekeeping: "{{ foreach.item.housekeeping | default: false }}"
            expected_impact: "{{ foreach.item.expected_impact | default: empty }}"
            evidence: "{{ foreach.item.evidence | default: empty }}"
            details: "{{ foreach.item.details }}"

  - name: log_result
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        Detection Engineering cycle complete —
        {{ steps.analyze_signal_quality.output.intents | size | default: 0 }} signal-quality
        + {{ steps.analyze_principal_deteng.output.intents | size | default: 0 }} principal intent(s)
        dispatched to soc-autonomous-applier.

definition.name: SOC Detection Engineering
definition.description:
Scheduled rule health review. Runs in two phases so that tactical tuning and strategic authoring have clear ownership and blast radius:
Phase 1 — Signal Quality: tunes existing rules (exceptions, thresholds)
          based on triage outcomes. Emits `redesign_required` for rules that
          are structurally noisy.

Phase 2 — Principal Detection Engineering: closes coverage gaps with new
          rules (always DISABLED) and redesigns rules flagged in Phase 1.

Both phases write recommendations into .soc-recommendations with distinct `source` values so the human reviewer and the soc-autonomous-applier can route them correctly.

document.reasoning: Strategic rule authoring driven by coverage gaps + Signal Quality redesign flags

{%- assign _n = steps.analyze_principal_deteng.output.intents | size | default: 0 -%} {% if _n > 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}
