results.name: SOC Meta Agent
results.description:
Autonomous evolution planner. The meta-agent ANALYZES system state and emits structured `mutation_intent` recommendations into .soc-recommendations. It does NOT mutate the platform directly — the soc-autonomous-applier workflow performs all execution under governance gates (kill-switch, ownership, budget, cooldown, loop-detection). This enforces a single control plane for self-governance: every change flows through the applier, every change is audited, every change can be rolled back.
Signal gate: the cycle short-circuits when there is nothing new to evolve on (no fresh outcomes, no new coverage gaps, no agent errors since the previous cycle). This is the T3 cost optimization — an expensive Opus call is only made when there is actual SOC signal to reason about.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Meta Agent
description: >
  Autonomous evolution planner. The meta-agent ANALYZES system state and emits
  structured `mutation_intent` recommendations into .soc-recommendations. It does
  NOT mutate the platform directly — the soc-autonomous-applier workflow
  performs all execution under governance gates (kill-switch, ownership, budget,
  cooldown, loop-detection). This enforces a single control plane for
  self-governance: every change flows through the applier, every change is
  audited, every change can be rolled back.

  Signal gate: the cycle short-circuits when there is nothing new to evolve on
  (no fresh outcomes, no new coverage gaps, no agent errors since the previous
  cycle). This is the T3 cost optimization — an expensive Opus call is only
  made when there is actual SOC signal to reason about.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 30m
  - type: manual

consts:
  signal_window: "now-35m"
  cycle_window: "now-24h"

steps:
  # ── Signal gate ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Short-circuit when there is no fresh SOC signal since the previous cycle.
  # Cheaper than paying for an Opus call just to conclude "no_action".
  - name: new_outcomes_count
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-outcomes"
      size: 0
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "{{ consts.signal_window }}"

  - name: new_gaps_count
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-coverage-gaps"
      size: 0
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "{{ consts.signal_window }}"

  - name: new_evolution_count
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-evolution-log"
      size: 0
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "{{ consts.signal_window }}"

  - name: signal_gate_log
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        Meta cycle signals — outcomes={{ steps.new_outcomes_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}
        gaps={{ steps.new_gaps_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}
        evolution={{ steps.new_evolution_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}

  # Compute-and-match gate: did the cycle see any new signals?
  - name: gate_no_new_signals
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _o = steps.new_outcomes_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 -%}
        {%- assign _g = steps.new_gaps_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 -%}
        {%- assign _e = steps.new_evolution_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _o == 0 and _g == 0 and _e == 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

  - name: signal_gate_heartbeat
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        event_type: meta_cycle_skipped
        source: soc-meta
        reason: no_new_signal
        recent_outcomes: "{{ steps.new_outcomes_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
        recent_gaps: "{{ steps.new_gaps_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
        recent_evolution: "{{ steps.new_evolution_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
    if: "steps.gate_no_new_signals.output: yes"

  - name: signal_gate_skip
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Meta cycle: no new signals in last 35m — skipping (cost optimization)."
    end: true
    if: "steps.gate_no_new_signals.output: yes"

  # ── 1. Context gather ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: get_outcomes
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-outcomes"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "{{ consts.cycle_window }}"
      size: 50
  - name: get_evolution_log
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-evolution-log"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "{{ consts.cycle_window }}"
      size: 30
  - name: get_coverage_gaps
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-coverage-gaps"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "{{ consts.cycle_window }}"
      size: 20
  - name: get_agent_registry
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-agent-registry"
      query:
        bool:
          must_not:
            - term:
                agent_id: seed
      size: 50
  - name: get_artifact_registry
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-artifact-registry"
      size: 200
  - name: get_rejected_recs
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term:
                source: soc-meta
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-7d"
          should:
            - term:
                status: rejected
            - term:
                status: failed
          minimum_should_match: 1
      size: 20
      _source:
        - rec_id
        - title
        - summary
        - rejection_reason
        - reviewed_at
        - type
        - details

  - name: get_existing_skills
    type: kibana.request
    with:
      method: GET
      path: /api/agent_builder/skills

  - name: log_start
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Meta Agent: starting tiered evolution planning (read-only analysis)"

  # ── 2. Plan mutations (LLM plan, NO direct writes) ──────────────────
  - name: plan
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-meta-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        You are the Meta Agent. Analyze SOC state and PROPOSE mutations as
        structured `mutation_intent` objects. You MUST NOT call any write tool
        in this turn — the soc-autonomous-applier workflow performs every
        platform mutation under governance gates. Your job is planning only.

        TIERED PLANNING (in preference order):
        - Tier 1: deterministic workflow  → emit `{artifact_type:"workflow", op:"create"}` with full `new_definition.yaml`
        - Tier 2a: new/updated skill      → emit `{artifact_type:"skill",    op:"create"|"update"}`
        - Tier 2b: agent instruction patch → emit `{artifact_type:"agent",   op:"update", patch:{instruction_patch:"..."}}`
        - Tier 3 (last resort): new agent → emit `{artifact_type:"agent",    op:"create"}`

        RESPONSE SHAPE (respond with ONLY this JSON — no prose):
        {
          "intents": [
            {
              "title":   "<<=200 char title>",
              "summary": "<10-2000 char explanation>",
              "reasoning": "<why now, what signal drives this>",
              "confidence": 0-100,
              "track": "deterministic" | "agentic",
              "housekeeping": false,
              "expected_impact": {
                "fp_reduction_pct": 0,
                "tp_gain_pct": 0,
                "mttr_reduction_minutes": 0,
                "hours_saved_per_week": 0,
                "coverage_delta_pct": 0
              },
              "evidence": [
                { "summary": "<500 char observation>",
                  "source_ref": "<ES|QL query or .soc-* doc id>",
                  "confidence": 0.0-1.0 }
              ],
              "details": {
                "artifact_type": "workflow" | "skill" | "agent" | "rule" | "exception",
                "artifact_id":   "auto-<kebab-id>",
                "op":            "create" | "update" | "delete" | "enable" | "disable",
                "expected_ownership": "autosoc",
                "reason": "<20+ char rationale stored in intent>",
                "new_definition": { ... optional for create/update ... },
                "patch":          { ... optional for update ... },
                "parent_recommendation_id": null,
                "dependencies": []
              }
            }
          ]
        }

        RULES:
        - Artifact id MUST start with `auto-` (e.g. `auto-lateral-hunter-workflow`). NEVER `soc-*` or `caldera-*` — those prefixes are reserved for canonical artifacts and the applier will reject mutations on them (result=blocked_canonical).
        - At least one `evidence[]` entry is REQUIRED unless `housekeeping: true`.
        - `expected_impact` must be populated with realistic numbers for the proposed change — it is used by the review UI to rank and by trust-scoring to grade outcomes. Zero-padding is fine; placeholders like `null` or `{}` are rejected unless housekeeping=true.
        - If you have nothing to propose this cycle, respond `{"intents": []}`.
        - Rejected/failed prior proposals are listed below — DO NOT repeat them.

        Existing core agents (enrich these before creating new ones):
        - soc-triage-agent, soc-deteng-agent, soc-signal-quality-agent,
          soc-autonomous-applier-agent

        Existing skills (avoid duplicating):
        {{ steps.get_existing_skills.output | json }}

        Recent outcomes (24h):
        {{ steps.get_outcomes.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Evolution log (recent decisions — avoid oscillation):
        {{ steps.get_evolution_log.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Coverage gaps:
        {{ steps.get_coverage_gaps.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Artifact registry (for ownership/dependency awareness):
        {{ steps.get_artifact_registry.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Previously rejected recommendations (learn from these):
        {{ steps.get_rejected_recs.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Respond with JSON only.
    timeout: 600s

  # ── 3. Persist evolution-decision audit row ─────────────────────────
  - name: write_evolution_decision
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-evolution-log
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        source: "soc-meta"
        event_type: "meta_cycle_plan"
        result: "planned"
        reason: "Meta agent produced planning output; intents dispatched to soc-autonomous-applier."
        evolution_output: "{{ steps.plan.output | json }}"

  # ── 4. Fan out: one mutation_intent per plan entry ──────────────────
  #     These are the documents soc-autonomous-applier picks up (type=mutation_intent,
  #     status=pending). The applier runs deterministic gates, then dispatches
  #     validated intents to soc-autonomous-applier-agent.
  #
  #     The AI agent may return no intents this cycle (steady-state). Guard the
  #     foreach with a compute-and-match gate so the workflow doesn't fail the
  #     tick with "foreach expression must evaluate to an array".
  - name: gate_has_intents
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _n = steps.plan.output.intents | size | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _n > 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

  - name: write_mutation_intents
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.plan.output.intents }}"
    if: "steps.gate_has_intents.output: yes"
    steps:
      - name: write_intent
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-recommendations
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            rec_id: "meta-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M%S' }}-{{ foreach.index }}"
            schema_version: 2
            type: "mutation_intent"
            source: "soc-meta"
            source_doc_id: "{{ steps.write_evolution_decision.output._id }}"
            status: "pending"
            title: "{{ foreach.item.title }}"
            summary: "{{ foreach.item.summary }}"
            reasoning: "{{ foreach.item.reasoning | default: 'Autonomous evolution proposal' }}"
            confidence: "{{ foreach.item.confidence | default: 80 }}"
            track: "{{ foreach.item.track | default: 'agentic' }}"
            housekeeping: "{{ foreach.item.housekeeping | default: false }}"
            expected_impact: "{{ foreach.item.expected_impact | default: empty }}"
            evidence: "{{ foreach.item.evidence | default: empty }}"
            details: "{{ foreach.item.details }}"

  # ── 5. If nothing was proposed, log a no_action audit row ───────────
  - name: gate_no_intents
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _n = steps.plan.output.intents | size | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _n == 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

  - name: log_no_intents
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        event_type: meta_cycle_no_action
        source: soc-meta
        reason: "Meta agent produced zero intents — nothing new to evolve this cycle."
    if: "steps.gate_no_intents.output: yes"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        Meta cycle complete — intents={{ steps.plan.output.intents | size | default: 0 }}
        (dispatched to soc-autonomous-applier for governance-gated execution).

results.name: SOC Outcomes Latency Field Presence Snapshot
results.description: Deterministically measure whether outcome latency fields (time_to_detect/time_to_respond) are present in .soc-outcomes* and write a trendable snapshot to .soc-audit-trail. This supports KPI enablement work without LLM reasoning.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Outcomes Latency Field Presence Snapshot
description: Deterministically measure whether outcome latency fields (time_to_detect/time_to_respond) are present in .soc-outcomes* and write a trendable snapshot to .soc-audit-trail. This supports KPI enablement work without LLM reasoning.
enabled: true
triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 15m
steps:
  - name: sample_outcomes
    type: elasticsearch.request
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /.soc-outcomes*/_search
      body:
        size: 200
        sort:
          - "@timestamp":
              order: desc
        _source:
          - "@timestamp"
          - "correlation_id"
          - "disposition"
          - "pipeline_complete"
          - "time_to_detect"
          - "time_to_respond"
        query:
          match_all: {}

  - name: write_snapshot
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: soc_outcomes_latency_field_presence_snapshot
        window: "now-15m"
        outcomes:
          index: ".soc-outcomes*"
          sampled: "{{ steps.sample_outcomes.output.hits.hits | size | default: 0 }}"
          has_time_to_detect_count: "{{ steps.sample_outcomes.output.hits.hits | where_exp: 'h', 'h._source.time_to_detect != null' | size | default: 0 }}"
          has_time_to_respond_count: "{{ steps.sample_outcomes.output.hits.hits | where_exp: 'h', 'h._source.time_to_respond != null' | size | default: 0 }}"
          dispositions_sample: "{{ steps.sample_outcomes.output.hits.hits | map: '_source' | map: 'disposition' | uniq | slice: 0, 20 }}"
        notes:
          - "Latest 24h outcomes aggregation shows time_to_detect/time_to_respond are not present (PRESENT()=false), blocking latency KPIs."
          - "This workflow only measures and trends field presence; it does not change agent behavior or detection rules."

results.name: SOC No-Outcomes-in-6h Health Alert
results.description: Deterministically detect silent stoppages where .soc-outcomes* has zero documents in the last 6 hours (as reported by soc-watchdog) and write a health signal to .soc-audit-trail.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC No-Outcomes-in-6h Health Alert
description: Deterministically detect silent stoppages where .soc-outcomes* has zero documents in the last 6 hours (as reported by soc-watchdog) and write a health signal to .soc-audit-trail.
enabled: true
triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 15m
steps:
  - name: count_outcomes_last_6h
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-outcomes*"
      size: 0
      track_total_hits: true
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-6h"

  - name: gate_has_outcomes
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _n = steps.count_outcomes_last_6h.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _n > 0 %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

  - name: write_ok
    if: "steps.gate_has_outcomes.output: yes"
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: soc_no_outcomes_6h_check
        status: OK
        window: "now-6h"
        outcomes:
          index: ".soc-outcomes*"
          total_hits: "{{ steps.count_outcomes_last_6h.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"

  - name: write_alert
    if: "steps.gate_has_outcomes.output: no"
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: soc_no_outcomes_6h_check
        status: ALERT
        window: "now-6h"
        outcomes:
          index: ".soc-outcomes*"
          total_hits: 0
        notes:
          - "soc-watchdog reported outcomes_total=0 over last 6h while pipeline runs continued; this alert makes the condition trendable and actionable."

results.name: SOC Outcomes Timestamp Skew Monitor
results.description: Deterministically detect clock/timestamp skew in .soc-outcomes* (docs with @timestamp > now+5m) and write a trendable health signal to .soc-audit-trail. This addresses watchdog-reported KPI window failures caused by future timestamps.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Outcomes Timestamp Skew Monitor
description: Deterministically detect clock/timestamp skew in .soc-outcomes* (docs with @timestamp > now+5m) and write a trendable health signal to .soc-audit-trail. This addresses watchdog-reported KPI window failures caused by future timestamps.
enabled: true
triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 15m
steps:
  - name: check_outcomes_timestamp_skew
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-outcomes*"
      size: 0
      track_total_hits: true
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gt: "now+5m"

  - name: gate_skew_ok
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _n = steps.check_outcomes_timestamp_skew.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _n > 0 %}no{% else %}yes{% endif %}

  - name: write_ok
    if: "steps.gate_skew_ok.output: yes"
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: soc_outcomes_timestamp_skew_check
        status: OK

results.name: SOC Outcomes vs Pipeline Telemetry Divergence Monitor
results.description: Deterministically detect when SOC pipeline executions are occurring but .soc-outcomes* has zero documents in the last 6h (a recurring watchdog condition). Writes a trendable health signal to .soc-audit-trail.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Outcomes vs Pipeline Telemetry Divergence Monitor
description: Deterministically detect when SOC pipeline executions are occurring but .soc-outcomes* has zero documents in the last 6h (a recurring watchdog condition). Writes a trendable health signal to .soc-audit-trail.
enabled: true
triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 15m
steps:
  - name: count_pipeline_runs_last_1h
    type: elasticsearch.request
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /.kibana-event-log-*/_search
      body:
        size: 0
        track_total_hits: true
        query:
          bool:
            filter:
              - range:
                  "@timestamp":
                    gte: "now-1h"
              - term:
                  event.provider: "alerting"
              - prefix:
                  rule.name: "SOC"
              - term:
                  event.action: "execute"

  - name: count_outcomes_last_6h
    type: elasticsearch.request
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /.soc-outcomes*/_search
      body:
        size: 0
        track_total_hits: true
        query:
          range:
            "@timestamp":
              gte: "now-6h"

  - name: gate_divergence
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        {%- assign _runs = steps.count_pipeline_runs_last_1h.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 -%}
        {%- assign _outs = steps.count_outcomes_last_6h.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 -%}
        {% if _runs > 0 and _outs == 0 %}alert{% else %}ok{% endif %}

  - name: write_ok
    if: "steps.gate_divergence.output: ok"
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: soc_outcomes_pipeline_divergence_check
        status: OK
        windows:
          pipeline: "now-1h"
          outcomes: "now-6h"
        observed:
          pipeline_runs_last_1h: "{{ steps.count_pipeline_runs_last_1h.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
          outcomes_last_6h: "{{ steps.count_outcomes_last_6h.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"

  - name: write_alert
    if: "steps.gate_divergence.output: alert"
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: soc_outcomes_pipeline_divergence_check
        status: ALERT
        windows:
          pipeline: "now-1h"
          outcomes: "now-6h"
        observed:
          pipeline_runs_last_1h: "{{ steps.count_pipeline_runs_last_1h.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
          outcomes_last_6h: 0
        notes:
          - "soc-watchdog repeatedly reports outcomes_total=0 over last 6h while pipeline runs are observed. This makes the divergence explicit and trendable for remediation of the outcomes write path/time-windowing."

results.name: SOC Caldera Dispatcher
results.description:
Claims the oldest pending attack command from .soc-attack-commands, looks up the matching adversary profile from .soc-attack-profiles, and POSTs a new operation to the Caldera REST API.
Replaces the former caldera-bridge Python sidecar — this workflow runs on a scheduled trigger every 1 minute (minimum allowed by the workflow engine) and is purely Elastic-native: elasticsearch.*, http, and foreach/if steps only.
Pairs with soc-caldera-poller, which watches running operations and writes back techniques_executed once Caldera reports state=finished|cleanup|paused.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Caldera Dispatcher
description: >
  Claims the oldest pending attack command from .soc-attack-commands, looks up
  the matching adversary profile from .soc-attack-profiles, and POSTs a new
  operation to the Caldera REST API.

  Replaces the former caldera-bridge Python sidecar — this workflow runs on a
  scheduled trigger every 1 minute (minimum allowed by the workflow engine) and
  is purely Elastic-native: elasticsearch.*, http, and foreach/if steps only.

  Pairs with soc-caldera-poller, which watches running operations and writes
  back techniques_executed once Caldera reports state=finished|cleanup|paused.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 1m
  - type: manual

consts:
  # Caldera URL — when Kibana runs inside docker-compose, use "http://caldera:8888".
  # When Kibana runs natively on the host (yarn start), Caldera is exposed at
  # localhost:${CALDERA_PORT:-18888}. This const is templated and can be updated
  # by setup scripts depending on deployment topology.
  caldera_url: "http://localhost:18888"
  caldera_api_key: "ADMIN123"
  batch_size: 3

steps:
  # ── Pull pending commands, oldest first ──────────────────────────────
  - name: pending_commands
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-attack-commands"
      size: 3
      seq_no_primary_term: true
      query:
        term:
          status: "pending"

  - name: dispatch
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.pending_commands.output.hits.hits }}"
    steps:
      # Optimistic-concurrency claim: only takes the doc if seq_no/primary_term
      # still match what we saw on the search. Another dispatcher run (or
      # another replica) that beats us will 409; we simply skip.
      # NOTE: elasticsearch.update takes `doc` at the top level — no `body:`
      # wrapper. `if_seq_no` / `if_primary_term` are URL params.
      - name: claim_command
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: ".soc-attack-commands"
          id: "{{ foreach.item._id }}"
          if_seq_no: "{{ foreach.item._seq_no }}"
          if_primary_term: "{{ foreach.item._primary_term }}"
          doc:
            status: "running"
            claimed_at: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            claimed_by: "soc-caldera-dispatcher"

      # Lookup the adversary profile for this difficulty level.
      # NOTE: the workflow engine has no elasticsearch.get connector, so we use
      # elasticsearch.request (raw pass-through) with method=GET.
      - name: profile_lookup
        type: elasticsearch.request
        with:
          method: GET
          path: "/.soc-attack-profiles/_doc/level-{{ foreach.item._source.difficulty }}"

      # Gate: profile must be present to proceed. Pre-compute a scalar "yes"/"no"
      # that KQL can match against via `steps.<name>.output: yes`.
      - name: gate_profile_found
        type: console
        with:
          message: "{% if steps.profile_lookup.output.found == true %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}"

      # Fail-fast when the profile is missing (seeded from caldera_profiles/ at setup time)
      - name: missing_profile
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: ".soc-attack-commands"
          id: "{{ foreach.item._id }}"
          doc:
            status: "failed"
            completed_at: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            error: "No adversary profile found for difficulty level {{ foreach.item._source.difficulty }}. Reseed caldera_profiles via setup.sh."
        if: "steps.gate_profile_found.output: no"

      # POST the Caldera operation.
      # NOTE: the http connector requires `body` to be a string — we build the
      # JSON payload with Liquid interpolation here. Watch for unescaped quotes
      # in interpolated values.
      - name: create_operation
        type: http
        with:
          url: "{{ consts.caldera_url }}/api/v2/operations"
          method: POST
          headers:
            KEY: "{{ consts.caldera_api_key }}"
            Content-Type: application/json
          body: >-
            {"name":"soc-sim-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d-%H%M%S' }}-{{ foreach.item._id }}","adversary":{"adversary_id":"{{ steps.profile_lookup.output._source.adversary_id }}"},"group":"{{ steps.profile_lookup.output._source.group | default: 'all-endpoints' }}"}
        if: "steps.gate_profile_found.output: yes"

      # Gate: did the Caldera POST succeed? Emit yes/no based on op_id presence.
      # IMPORTANT: the http connector returns { status, statusText, headers, data }
      # so the Caldera operation id lives at steps.create_operation.output.data.id
      - name: gate_op_created
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign op_id = steps.create_operation.output.data.id -%}
            {%- assign http_status = steps.create_operation.output.status -%}
            {% if steps.profile_lookup.output.found == true and http_status == 200 and op_id != nil and op_id != '' %}yes{% else %}no{% endif %}

      # Stash the operation id on the command doc for the poller to pick up.
      - name: record_operation_id
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: ".soc-attack-commands"
          id: "{{ foreach.item._id }}"
          doc:
            caldera_operation_id: "{{ steps.create_operation.output.data.id }}"
            caldera_adversary_id: "{{ steps.profile_lookup.output._source.adversary_id }}"
            dispatched_at: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        if: "steps.gate_op_created.output: yes"

      # Operation creation failed — mark the command failed so it doesn't re-claim forever
      - name: gate_op_failed
        type: console
        with:
          message: >-
            {%- assign op_id = steps.create_operation.output.data.id -%}
            {%- assign http_status = steps.create_operation.output.status -%}
            {%- assign profile_ok = steps.profile_lookup.output.found -%}
            {% if profile_ok == true and http_status != 200 %}yes
            {%- elsif profile_ok == true and op_id == nil %}yes
            {%- elsif profile_ok == true and op_id == '' %}yes
            {%- else %}no{% endif %}

      - name: mark_operation_failed
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: ".soc-attack-commands"
          id: "{{ foreach.item._id }}"
          doc:
            status: "failed"
            completed_at: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            error: "Caldera operation creation failed (HTTP {{ steps.create_operation.output.status | default: 'unknown' }})"
        if: "steps.gate_op_failed.output: yes"

  - name: heartbeat
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: caldera_dispatcher_tick
        pending_batch_size: "{{ steps.pending_commands.output.hits.hits | size | default: 0 }}"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Caldera dispatcher tick complete — dispatched {{ steps.pending_commands.output.hits.hits | size | default: 0 }} commands"

results.name: SOC Watchdog
results.description: Health monitoring and coverage gap detection. Uses deterministic ES queries for KPI checks and writes structured health reports. The meta-agent's health-check skill handles the analysis if anomalies are detected.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Watchdog
description: >
  Health monitoring and coverage gap detection. Uses deterministic ES queries for
  KPI checks and writes structured health reports. The meta-agent's health-check
  skill handles the analysis if anomalies are detected.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 15m
  - type: manual

steps:
  # ── Gather aggregated signals (NOT raw docs — avoids LLM token overrun) ──
  - name: outcomes_agg
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-outcomes"
      size: 0
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-6h"
      aggs:
        total: { value_count: { field: "@timestamp" } }
        by_disposition:
          terms: { field: "disposition", size: 20 }
        avg_confidence:
          avg: { field: "confidence" }
        by_technique:
          terms: { field: "techniques_observed", size: 10 }
          aggs:
            avg_conf: { avg: { field: "confidence" } }
            fp_count:
              filter: { term: { disposition: "auto_closed_fp" } }

  - name: triage_agg
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-triage-results"
      size: 0
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-6h"
      aggs:
        total: { value_count: { field: "@timestamp" } }
        by_disposition:
          terms: { field: "disposition", size: 20 }

  - name: pipeline_agg
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-metrics"
      size: 0
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-1h"
      aggs:
        total: { value_count: { field: "@timestamp" } }
        by_status:
          terms: { field: "status", size: 10 }

  - name: dead_letter_count
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-dead-letter"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          must:
            - term: { status: "failed" }
            - range: { "@timestamp": { gte: "now-1h" } }

  # ── Analyze with meta-agent's health-check skill ─────────────────
  - name: health_check
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-meta-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        Perform SOC health monitoring using your health-check skill.

        KPI summary (aggregated, last 6h):
          Outcomes total: {{ steps.outcomes_agg.output.aggregations.total.value }}
          Outcomes by disposition: {{ steps.outcomes_agg.output.aggregations.by_disposition.buckets | json }}
          Avg confidence: {{ steps.outcomes_agg.output.aggregations.avg_confidence.value }}
          By technique (top 10): {{ steps.outcomes_agg.output.aggregations.by_technique.buckets | json }}

          Triage total: {{ steps.triage_agg.output.aggregations.total.value }}
          Triage by disposition: {{ steps.triage_agg.output.aggregations.by_disposition.buckets | json }}

          Pipeline (1h): {{ steps.pipeline_agg.output.aggregations.total.value }} runs,
          by status: {{ steps.pipeline_agg.output.aggregations.by_status.buckets | json }}

          Dead-letter failed (1h): {{ steps.dead_letter_count.output.hits.total.value }}

        Thresholds:
          - Dead-letter failed > 10 → FAILING
          - Pipeline runs == 0 in last hour → STALLED
          - FP ratio > 0.7 across outcomes → REVIEW_DETECTIONS

        Compute:
          1) FP ratio = fp_count / total
          2) Which techniques have low confidence (< 0.6) and non-FP disposition?
          3) Dead-letter status
          4) Pipeline status
          5) Recommendations (1-3 concrete, actionable items)

        Use your search tools only if you need per-document details for a specific technique.
        Output a structured health report. Self-validate: every numeric field must be finite.
    timeout: 300s

  # ── Write results ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: write_coverage_gaps
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-coverage-gaps
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        source: "soc-watchdog"
        health_report: "{{ steps.health_check.output | json }}"

  - name: write_audit
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: "health_check"
        source: "soc-watchdog"
        details: "{{ steps.health_check.output | json }}"

  - name: log_result
    type: console
    with:
      message: "SOC Watchdog health check complete"

definition.name: SOC Watchdog
definition.description: Health monitoring and coverage gap detection. Uses deterministic ES queries for KPI checks and writes structured health reports. The meta-agent's health-check skill handles the analysis if anomalies are detected.

with.message: SOC Watchdog health check complete

results.name: SOC Triage
results.description: Unified triage workflow (alert-triggered). Runs classification, entity enrichment, and deep investigation in a single agent call. Writes the flattened triage verdict to `.soc-triage-results` and a derived outcome to `.soc-outcomes`. The disposition is derived from the agent output — it is NOT hardcoded.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Triage
description: >
  Unified triage workflow (alert-triggered). Runs classification, entity enrichment,
  and deep investigation in a single agent call. Writes the flattened triage verdict
  to `.soc-triage-results` and a derived outcome to `.soc-outcomes`. The disposition
  is derived from the agent output — it is NOT hardcoded.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: manual
  - type: alert

consts:
  run_id: "triage-{{ workflow.run_id | default: 'run' }}-{{ 'now' | date: '%s%3N' }}"
  now_iso: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"

steps:
  - name: log_alert
    type: console
    with:
      message: "SOC Triage received alert: {{ event | json }}"

  - name: triage
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-triage-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        Run the full triage pipeline on this security alert:
        Phase 1 — Classify as TRUE_POSITIVE, FALSE_POSITIVE, or SUSPICIOUS with confidence 0-100.
        Phase 2 — If confidence >= 40, enrich with entity context (risk scores, baselines, relationships).
        Phase 3 — If still ambiguous (confidence 40-69), conduct structured threat hunt.
        Phase 4 — If TRUE_POSITIVE or SUSPICIOUS with confidence >= 50, check for attack chain correlation
                   using security.attack_discovery_search.

        Produce multi-dimensional classification. Respond with STRICT JSON (no prose):

        {
          "classification":     "TRUE_POSITIVE" | "FALSE_POSITIVE" | "SUSPICIOUS",
          "confidence":         0-100,
          "disposition":        "TRUE_POSITIVE" | "BENIGN_TRUE_POSITIVE" | "FALSE_POSITIVE"
                               | "POLICY_VIOLATION" | "INCONCLUSIVE" | "DUPLICATE",
          "threat_category":    "commodity_malware" | "targeted_attack" | "insider_threat" | "misuse"
                               | "unauthorized_access" | "data_exfiltration" | "lateral_movement"
                               | "persistence" | "reconnaissance" | "unknown",
          "kill_chain_stage":   "reconnaissance" | "weaponization" | "delivery" | "exploitation"
                               | "installation" | "c2" | "actions_on_objectives" | "unknown",
          "business_impact":    { "data_at_risk": [...], "systems_at_risk": [...], "criticality": "low|medium|high|critical" },
          "recommended_action": "close_fp" | "open_case" | "enrich_only" | "escalate",
          "reasoning":          "<concise rationale>",
          "evidence":           [ { "summary": "...", "source_ref": "<doc id|query>", "confidence": 0.0-1.0 } ]
        }

        Self-validate: every field above MUST be populated. `disposition` MUST be one of the enumerated values
        (never "triaged" or other placeholders). `confidence` MUST be an integer 0-100.

        Alert data:
        {{ event | json }}
    timeout: 600s

  # Flatten the triage output at the top of the doc so dashboards and
  # aggregations don't have to reach into triage_output.* to get the verdict.
  # NOTE: Kibana's ai.agent step returns `{ message: "<raw-JSON-string>" }`; the
  # fields below live inside that string, not on `.output` directly. Every
  # reference uses `{% assign parsed = ... | json_parse %}` so the flat fields
  # are populated correctly instead of silently falling back to defaults.
  - name: write_triage_result
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-triage-results
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ consts.now_iso }}"
        run_id: "{{ consts.run_id }}"
        source: "soc-triage"
        stage: "unified_triage"
        pipeline: "soc-triage"
        alert_id: "{{ event.id | default: event._id | default: 'unknown' }}"
        rule_id: "{{ event['kibana.alert.rule.uuid'] | default: event.rule.id | default: null }}"
        rule_name: "{{ event['kibana.alert.rule.name'] | default: event.rule.name | default: null }}"
        classification: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.classification | default: 'SUSPICIOUS' }}"
        confidence: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.confidence | default: 0 }}"
        disposition: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.disposition | default: 'INCONCLUSIVE' }}"
        threat_category: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.threat_category | default: 'unknown' }}"
        kill_chain_stage: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.kill_chain_stage | default: 'unknown' }}"
        recommended_action: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.recommended_action | default: null }}"
        reasoning: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.reasoning | default: null }}"
        business_impact: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.business_impact | default: empty }}"
        evidence: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.evidence | default: empty }}"
        triage_output: "{{ steps.triage.output.message | json_parse | json }}"

  # Outcomes are the single source of truth for SLO/rollup dashboards. The
  # `disposition` on this doc is the agent's disposition — never "triaged".
  - name: write_outcome
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-outcomes
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ consts.now_iso }}"
        correlation_id: "{{ consts.run_id }}"
        pipeline: "soc-triage"
        stage: "unified_triage"
        agents_involved: ["soc-triage-agent"]
        classification: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.classification | default: 'SUSPICIOUS' }}"
        confidence: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.confidence | default: 0 }}"
        disposition: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.disposition | default: 'INCONCLUSIVE' }}"
        threat_category: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.threat_category | default: 'unknown' }}"
        kill_chain_stage: "{% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}{{ _pt.kill_chain_stage | default: 'unknown' }}"
        triage_result_ref: "{{ steps.write_triage_result.output._id | default: null }}"

  - name: write_reasoning_trace
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-reasoning-trace
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ consts.now_iso }}"
        run_id: "{{ consts.run_id }}"
        agent_id: "soc-triage-agent"
        step_index: 0
        step_type: "run_summary"
        content: "Triage run for alert {{ event.id | default: 'unknown' }} → {% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}disposition={{ _pt.disposition | default: 'INCONCLUSIVE' }} confidence={{ _pt.confidence | default: 0 }}"
        run_summary:
          total_steps: 1
          tool_call_count: 0
          total_duration_ms: null
          final_status: "completed"
          final_output_ref: "{{ steps.write_triage_result.output._id | default: null }}"

  - name: log_result
    type: console
    with:
      message: "SOC Triage complete → {% assign _pt = steps.triage.output.message | json_parse %}disposition={{ _pt.disposition | default: 'INCONCLUSIVE' }} confidence={{ _pt.confidence | default: 0 }} run_id={{ consts.run_id }}"

results.name: SOC Shift Handover
results.description: Every 8 hours, synthesize a narrative summary of autonomous SOC activity for the previous shift and write it to .soc-shift-handover. The narrative is produced by the soc-meta-agent from deterministic counters aggregated against .soc-evolution-log, .soc-audit-trail, and .soc-outcomes. This is the operator's "what happened while I was away" inbox.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Shift Handover
description: >
  Every 8 hours, synthesize a narrative summary of autonomous SOC activity
  for the previous shift and write it to .soc-shift-handover. The narrative
  is produced by the soc-meta-agent from deterministic counters aggregated
  against .soc-evolution-log, .soc-audit-trail, and .soc-outcomes. This is
  the operator's "what happened while I was away" inbox.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 8h
  - type: manual

consts:
  window_hours: 8

steps:
  # ─── Deterministic counters from the last 8h ────────────────────────
  - name: evolution_counters
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-evolution-log"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-{{ consts.window_hours }}h"
      aggs:
        by_result:
          terms:
            field: "result"
            size: 20
        by_source:
          terms:
            field: "source"
            size: 20

  - name: cases_opened_count
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-outcomes"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-{{ consts.window_hours }}h"
            - term: {disposition: "case_created"}

  - name: cases_closed_count
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-forensic-summary"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - range:
                closed_at:
                  gte: "now-{{ consts.window_hours }}h"

  - name: kill_switch_events_count
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-audit-trail"
      size: 0
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-{{ consts.window_hours }}h"
            - term: {event_type: "autonomous_applier_abort"}

  # ─── Top highlights for the narrative ──────────────────────────────
  - name: top_mutations
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-evolution-log"
      size: 10
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term: {source: "soc-autonomous-applier"}
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-{{ consts.window_hours }}h"
            - terms:
                result: ["applied", "blocked_canonical", "blocked_loop", "blocked_cooldown", "blocked_budget", "validation_failed", "failure"]
  - name: compose_narrative
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-meta-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        Produce a SHIFT HANDOVER narrative (<= 6 short paragraphs, Markdown)
        for the SOC analyst taking over. Tone: concise, human, no corporate
        filler. Every concrete claim must be anchored to one of the counters
        or highlights below. Prefer numbers over adjectives.

        Counters (deterministic, already aggregated):
          evolution_by_result    = {{ steps.evolution_counters.output.aggregations.by_result.buckets | json }}
          evolution_by_source    = {{ steps.evolution_counters.output.aggregations.by_source.buckets | json }}
          cases_opened           = {{ steps.cases_opened_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}
          cases_closed           = {{ steps.cases_closed_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}
          kill_switch_events     = {{ steps.kill_switch_events_count.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}

        Highlights (most recent applier decisions, oldest to newest):

results.description:
Closes the self-learning loop. Compares what the backtester PREDICTED against what the observer OBSERVED, and writes regression-test rows to `.soc-regression-dataset`, `.soc-regression-runs`, and `.soc-metrics`.
The dataset accumulates (prediction, reality) pairs that can be used to:
  1. Calibrate backtester verdict thresholds (are we too optimistic?)
  2. Flag agents whose proposals consistently regress (feeds trust scorer)
  3. Surface "prediction accuracy" as a first-class KPI in the dashboard

  * .soc-regression-dataset  - one row per (recommendation, backtest, observation)
    with the prediction, actual outcome, and residual. This is the training
    corpus for future self-improvement.
  * .soc-regression-runs     - one row per tick summarizing accuracy metrics.
  * .soc-metrics             - aggregated KPIs the dashboard and watchdog
    poll: backtest_accuracy_pct, avg_fp_reduction_realized,
    avg_fp_reduction_predicted, residual_mean_abs.

This workflow runs every 10m so the feedback arrives fast enough to influence the next difficulty-controller + trust-scorer pass.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Self-Learning Loop
description: >
  Closes the self-learning loop. Compares what the backtester PREDICTED
  against what the observer OBSERVED, and writes regression-test rows
  to `.soc-regression-dataset`, `.soc-regression-runs`, and `.soc-metrics`.

  The dataset accumulates (prediction, reality) pairs that can be used to:
    1. Calibrate backtester verdict thresholds (are we too optimistic?)
    2. Flag agents whose proposals consistently regress (feeds trust scorer)
    3. Surface "prediction accuracy" as a first-class KPI in the dashboard

  Three outputs per tick:
    * .soc-regression-dataset  - one row per (recommendation, backtest, observation)
      with the prediction, actual outcome, and residual. This is the training
      corpus for future self-improvement.
    * .soc-regression-runs     - one row per tick summarizing accuracy metrics.
    * .soc-metrics             - aggregated KPIs the dashboard and watchdog
      poll: backtest_accuracy_pct, avg_fp_reduction_realized,
      avg_fp_reduction_predicted, residual_mean_abs.

  This workflow runs every 10m so the feedback arrives fast enough to
  influence the next difficulty-controller + trust-scorer pass.

enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 10m
  - type: manual

consts:
  lookback: "now-24h"

steps:
  # ── 1. Backtests + their final decisions ─────────────────────────────
  # NOTE: uses elasticsearch.request (not .search) because the workflow engine's
  # zod schema for top-level `sort` only accepts strings or the reserved keys
  # (_score/_doc/_geo_distance/_script). Sorting @timestamp desc requires an
  # object form that the raw request API passes through unchanged.
  - name: recent_backtests
    type: elasticsearch.request
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /.soc-backtests/_search
      body:
        size: 100
        query:
          range:
            "@timestamp":
              gte: "{{ consts.lookback }}"
        sort:
          - "@timestamp":
              order: desc
  # ── 2. Autonomy decisions for the same window ────────────────────────
  # NOTE: uses elasticsearch.request — see recent_backtests above for rationale.
  - name: recent_decisions
    type: elasticsearch.request
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /.soc-autonomy-decisions/_search
      body:
        size: 500
        query:
          bool:
            filter:
              - range:
                  "@timestamp":
                    gte: "{{ consts.lookback }}"
              - terms:
                  source_workflow: ["soc-autonomous-applier", "soc-post-apply-observer"]
        sort:
          - "@timestamp":
              order: desc
  # ── 3. Recommendations final status ─────────────────────────────────
  - name: recent_recs
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      size: 200
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term: { type: "mutation_intent" }
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "{{ consts.lookback }}"

  # ── 4. One regression-dataset row per backtest ──────────────────────
  - name: write_dataset
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.recent_backtests.output.hits.hits }}"
    steps:
      - name: write_row
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-regression-dataset
          refresh: "wait_for"
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            sample_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id }}"
            rule_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rule_id }}"
            action: "{{ foreach.item._source.action }}"
            predicted:
              verdict: "{{ foreach.item._source.verdict }}"
              fp_reduction_pct: "{{ foreach.item._source.metrics.delta.alert_reduction_pct | default: 0 }}"
              alerts_per_day_before: "{{ foreach.item._source.metrics.before.alerts_per_day | default: 0 }}"
              alerts_per_day_after: "{{ foreach.item._source.metrics.after.alert_count | default: 0 }}"
              simulator: "{{ foreach.item._source.simulator_used | default: 'deterministic_v1' }}"
            observed:
              applied: "{% assign _applied = false %}{% for d in steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.hits %}{% if d._source.rec_id == foreach.item._source.rec_id and d._source.op == 'apply' and d._source.final_status == 'applied' %}{% assign _applied = true %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _applied }}"
              rolled_back: "{% assign _rb = false %}{% for d in steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.hits %}{% if d._source.rec_id == foreach.item._source.rec_id and d._source.final_status == 'regression_detected' %}{% assign _rb = true %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _rb }}"
              final_rec_status: "{% assign _st = 'unknown' %}{% for r in steps.recent_recs.output.hits.hits %}{% if r._source.rec_id == foreach.item._source.rec_id %}{% assign _st = r._source.status %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _st }}"
            residual:
              prediction_matched_reality: "{% assign _predicted_safe = false %}{% if foreach.item._source.verdict == 'projection_safe' %}{% assign _predicted_safe = true %}{% endif %}{% assign _was_clean = true %}{% for d in steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.hits %}{% if d._source.rec_id == foreach.item._source.rec_id and d._source.final_status == 'regression_detected' %}{% assign _was_clean = false %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% if _predicted_safe == _was_clean %}true{% else %}false{% endif %}"
            source: "soc-self-learning-loop"
            dataset_version: "v1"

  # ── 5. One regression-runs row per tick ──────────────────────────────
  - name: write_run_summary
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-regression-runs
      refresh: "wait_for"
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        window: "{{ consts.lookback }}"
        backtests_total: "{{ steps.recent_backtests.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
        decisions_total: "{{ steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
        recs_total: "{{ steps.recent_recs.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
        safe_predictions: "{% assign _n = 0 %}{% for b in steps.recent_backtests.output.hits.hits %}{% if b._source.verdict == 'projection_safe' %}{% assign _n = _n | plus: 1 %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _n }}"
        concerning_predictions: "{% assign _n = 0 %}{% for b in steps.recent_backtests.output.hits.hits %}{% if b._source.verdict == 'projection_concerning' %}{% assign _n = _n | plus: 1 %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _n }}"
        observed_regressions: "{% assign _n = 0 %}{% for d in steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.hits %}{% if d._source.final_status == 'regression_detected' %}{% assign _n = _n | plus: 1 %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _n }}"
        observed_applies: "{% assign _n = 0 %}{% for d in steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.hits %}{% if d._source.op == 'apply' and d._source.final_status == 'applied' %}{% assign _n = _n | plus: 1 %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _n }}"
        source: "soc-self-learning-loop"

  # ── 6. One KPI row in .soc-metrics ──────────────────────────────────
  - name: write_kpi
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-metrics
      refresh: "wait_for"
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
        metric_family: "self_learning"
        window: "{{ consts.lookback }}"
        values:
          backtests_total: "{{ steps.recent_backtests.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
          decisions_total: "{{ steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
          avg_fp_reduction_predicted_pct: "{% assign _sum = 0 %}{% assign _n = 0 %}{% for b in steps.recent_backtests.output.hits.hits %}{% assign _v = b._source.metrics.delta.alert_reduction_pct | default: 0 %}{% assign _sum = _sum | plus: _v %}{% assign _n = _n | plus: 1 %}{% endfor %}{% if _n == 0 %}0{% else %}{{ _sum | divided_by: _n }}{% endif %}"
          regression_rate_pct: "{% assign _r = 0 %}{% assign _t = 0 %}{% for d in steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.hits %}{% if d._source.source_workflow == 'soc-post-apply-observer' %}{% assign _t = _t | plus: 1 %}{% if d._source.final_status == 'regression_detected' %}{% assign _r = _r | plus: 1 %}{% endif %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% if _t == 0 %}0{% else %}{% assign _x = _r | times: 100 %}{{ _x | divided_by: _t }}{% endif %}"
          auto_apply_rate_pct: "{% assign _aa = 0 %}{% assign _t = 0 %}{% for d in steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.hits %}{% assign _t = _t | plus: 1 %}{% if d._source.auto_applied == true %}{% assign _aa = _aa | plus: 1 %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% if _t == 0 %}0{% else %}{% assign _x = _aa | times: 100 %}{{ _x | divided_by: _t }}{% endif %}"
        source: "soc-self-learning-loop"

  - name: heartbeat
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: self_learning_heartbeat
        source: "soc-self-learning-loop"
        backtests: "{{ steps.recent_backtests.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
        decisions: "{{ steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Self-learning loop tick complete: {{ steps.recent_backtests.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }} backtests x {{ steps.recent_decisions.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }} decisions"

results.name: SOC Rule Backtester
results.description:
Projects the likely effect of a proposed rule mutation BEFORE the applier touches the rule. Scheduled every 1m. Reads `pending_backtest` mutation_intents, pulls 30-day historical metrics for the target rule, cross-references `.soc-outcomes` for true-positive impact, writes a row to `.soc-backtests`, and flips the mutation_intent status to one of:

  auto_apply_ready    -> backtest projects safely; applier will auto-land
  pending_review      -> projection concerning or unknown; exception queue
  rejected_backtest   -> projection unsafe (too much reduction or tp misses)

The applier's gate cascade then reads `verdict` directly — the backtester is the ONLY producer of backtest records. Without this workflow, rule-update intents never reach the applier (the gate refuses to apply without a verdict).
Verdict rules (best-effort deterministic projection):
  - action=raise_threshold: projection_safe by default. If any TP alert in the
    last 30d fired with `threshold_result.count < new_threshold`, downgrade
    to projection_concerning (the raise would have muted a real case).
  - action=lower_threshold: projection_concerning (increases volume).
  - action=tighten_query: projection_concerning (may miss TPs; needs review).
  - action=broaden_query: projection_concerning (increases volume).
  - action=disable: projection_concerning if ANY TP in 30d; else projection_safe.
  - action=change_severity / change_risk_score / add_note: projection_safe
    (doesn't change matches).

This is intentionally conservative — the applier's default-path (auto_apply_ready) is restricted to actions where the projection is deterministic and safe. Query shape changes always route to the exception queue so an operator can eyeball the diff.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Rule Backtester
description: >
  Projects the likely effect of a proposed rule mutation BEFORE the applier touches
  the rule. Scheduled every 1m. Reads `pending_backtest` mutation_intents, pulls
  30-day historical metrics for the target rule, cross-references `.soc-outcomes`
  for true-positive impact, writes a row to `.soc-backtests`, and flips the
  mutation_intent status to one of:

    auto_apply_ready    -> backtest projects safely; applier will auto-land
    pending_review      -> projection concerning or unknown; exception queue
    rejected_backtest   -> projection unsafe (too much reduction or tp misses)

  The applier's gate cascade then reads `verdict` directly — the backtester is
  the ONLY producer of backtest records. Without this workflow, rule-update
  intents never reach the applier (the gate refuses to apply without a verdict).

  Verdict rules (best-effort deterministic projection):
    - action=raise_threshold: projection_safe by default. If any TP alert in the
      last 30d fired with `threshold_result.count < new_threshold`, downgrade
      to projection_concerning (the raise would have muted a real case).
    - action=lower_threshold: projection_concerning (increases volume).
    - action=tighten_query: projection_concerning (may miss TPs; needs review).
    - action=broaden_query: projection_concerning (increases volume).
    - action=disable: projection_concerning if ANY TP in 30d; else projection_safe.
    - action=change_severity / change_risk_score / add_note: projection_safe
      (doesn't change matches).

  This is intentionally conservative — the applier's default-path (auto_apply_ready)
  is restricted to actions where the projection is deterministic and safe. Query
  shape changes always route to the exception queue so an operator can eyeball
  the diff.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 1m
  - type: manual

consts:
  window_days: 30
  max_per_tick: 10
  aggressive_actions: ["raise_threshold", "tighten_query", "disable"]

steps:
  # ── 1. Pull pending backtests ─────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: pending_backtests
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      size: 10
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term: {type: "mutation_intent"}
            - terms: {status: ["pending_backtest", "pending"]}
            - term: {"details.artifact_type": "rule"}
            - term: {"details.op": "update"}
  - name: process_intents
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.pending_backtests.output.hits.hits }}"
    steps:
      # -- Pull historical alert count for this rule over window_days --
      - name: historical_alerts
        type: elasticsearch.search
        with:
          index: ".alerts-security.alerts-*"
          size: 0
          query:
            bool:
              filter:
                - term: {"kibana.alert.rule.rule_id": "{{ foreach.item._source.details.patch.rule_id }}"}
                - range:
                    "@timestamp":
                      gte: "now-{{ consts.window_days }}d"
          aggs:
            distinct_hosts:
              cardinality:
                field: "host.name"
            distinct_users:
              cardinality:
                field: "user.name"
            max_threshold_count:
              max:
                field: "kibana.alert.threshold_result.count"

      # -- Pull TP outcomes for this rule (via correlation_id -> alerts) --
      - name: tp_correlations
        type: elasticsearch.search
        with:
          index: ".soc-outcomes"
          size: 100
          query:
            bool:
              filter:
                - term: {disposition: "true_positive"}
                - range:
                    "@timestamp":
                      gte: "now-{{ consts.window_days }}d"
      - name: tp_alert_for_rule
        type: elasticsearch.search
        with:
          index: ".alerts-security.alerts-*"
          size: 50
          query:
            bool:
              filter:
                - term: {"kibana.alert.rule.rule_id": "{{ foreach.item._source.details.patch.rule_id }}"}
                - range:
                    "@timestamp":
                      gte: "now-{{ consts.window_days }}d"
                - terms:
                    "kibana.alert.uuid": "{{ steps.tp_correlations.output.hits.hits | map: '_source' | map: 'correlation_id' | json }}"

      # -- Compute the backtest record deterministically -------------
      - name: write_backtest
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-backtests
          refresh: "wait_for"
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id }}"
            rule_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.patch.rule_id }}"
            action: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.patch.action }}"
            op: "update"
            window_start: "now-{{ consts.window_days | default: 30 }}d"
            window_end: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            window_days: "{{ consts.window_days }}"
            current_rule_snapshot: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.patch.current_values | json }}"
            proposed_rule_snapshot: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.patch.patch_fields | json }}"
            metrics:
              before:
                alert_count: "{{ steps.historical_alerts.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
                distinct_hosts: "{{ steps.historical_alerts.output.aggregations.distinct_hosts.value | default: 0 }}"
                distinct_users: "{{ steps.historical_alerts.output.aggregations.distinct_users.value | default: 0 }}"
                alerts_per_day: "{% assign _cnt = steps.historical_alerts.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% assign _days = consts.window_days %}{{ _cnt | divided_by: _days }}"
              after:
                alert_count: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% assign _c = steps.historical_alerts.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% if _a == 'disable' %}0{% elsif _a == 'raise_threshold' %}{{ _c | divided_by: 2 }}{% elsif _a == 'tighten_query' %}{{ _c | divided_by: 3 }}{% elsif _a == 'lower_threshold' %}{{ _c | times: 2 }}{% elsif _a == 'broaden_query' %}{{ _c | times: 2 }}{% else %}{{ _c }}{% endif %}"
              delta:
                alert_reduction_pct: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% if _a == 'disable' %}100{% elsif _a == 'raise_threshold' %}50{% elsif _a == 'tighten_query' %}66{% elsif _a == 'lower_threshold' %}-100{% elsif _a == 'broaden_query' %}-100{% else %}0{% endif %}"
                net_alert_volume: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% assign _c = steps.historical_alerts.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% if _a == 'disable' %}-{{ _c }}{% elsif _a == 'raise_threshold' %}-{{ _c | divided_by: 2 }}{% else %}0{% endif %}"
            tp_misses: "{{ steps.tp_alert_for_rule.output.hits.hits | map: '_source' | json }}"
            verdict: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% assign _tp = steps.tp_alert_for_rule.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% if _a == 'change_severity' or _a == 'change_risk_score' or _a == 'add_note' %}projection_safe{% elsif _a == 'disable' and _tp == 0 %}projection_safe{% elsif _a == 'disable' and _tp > 0 %}projection_concerning{% elsif _a == 'raise_threshold' and _tp == 0 %}projection_safe{% elsif _a == 'raise_threshold' and _tp > 0 %}projection_concerning{% elsif _a == 'tighten_query' %}projection_concerning{% elsif _a == 'lower_threshold' %}projection_concerning{% elsif _a == 'broaden_query' %}projection_concerning{% elsif _a == 'enable' %}projection_unknown{% else %}projection_unknown{% endif %}"
            verdict_reason: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% assign _tp = steps.tp_alert_for_rule.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% assign _c = steps.historical_alerts.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}Deterministic projection for action={{ _a }}. Observed {{ _c }} historical alerts over {{ consts.window_days }}d, {{ _tp }} confirmed TP correlations. {% if _a == 'change_severity' or _a == 'change_risk_score' or _a == 'add_note' %}Action does not affect query matching.{% elsif _a == 'disable' and _tp == 0 %}No confirmed TPs in window — safe to disable.{% elsif _tp > 0 %}Cannot safely apply; {{ _tp }} TP correlation(s) may be suppressed.{% else %}Query-shape change requires human eyeball.{% endif %}"
            computed_at: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            computed_by: "soc-rule-backtester"
            simulator_used: "deterministic_v1"

      # -- Flip intent status based on verdict -----------------------
      - name: update_intent_status
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: .soc-recommendations
          id: "{{ foreach.item._id }}"
          refresh: "wait_for"
          doc:
            status: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% assign _tp = steps.tp_alert_for_rule.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% if _a == 'change_severity' or _a == 'change_risk_score' or _a == 'add_note' %}auto_apply_ready{% elsif _a == 'disable' and _tp == 0 %}auto_apply_ready{% elsif _a == 'raise_threshold' and _tp == 0 %}auto_apply_ready{% else %}pending_review{% endif %}"
            backtest_ref: "{{ steps.write_backtest.output._id | default: 'unknown' }}"
            backtest_verdict: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% assign _tp = steps.tp_alert_for_rule.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% if _a == 'change_severity' or _a == 'change_risk_score' or _a == 'add_note' %}projection_safe{% elsif _a == 'disable' and _tp == 0 %}projection_safe{% elsif _a == 'raise_threshold' and _tp == 0 %}projection_safe{% elsif _a == 'enable' %}projection_unknown{% else %}projection_concerning{% endif %}"

      # -- Log the decision to .soc-autonomy-decisions ---------------
      - name: log_decision
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-autonomy-decisions
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id }}"
            artifact_type: "rule"
            artifact_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.patch.rule_id }}"
            op: "update"
            action: "{{ foreach.item._source.details.patch.action }}"
            source_agent: "{{ foreach.item._source.source | default: 'unknown' }}"
            source_workflow: "soc-rule-backtester"
            gates_evaluated: ["backtest_projection"]
            gates_passed: ["backtest_projection"]
            final_status: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% assign _tp = steps.tp_alert_for_rule.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% if _a == 'change_severity' or _a == 'change_risk_score' or _a == 'add_note' %}auto_apply_ready{% elsif _a == 'disable' and _tp == 0 %}auto_apply_ready{% elsif _a == 'raise_threshold' and _tp == 0 %}auto_apply_ready{% else %}pending_review{% endif %}"
            auto_applied: false
            required_human: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% assign _tp = steps.tp_alert_for_rule.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% if _a == 'change_severity' or _a == 'change_risk_score' or _a == 'add_note' %}false{% elsif _a == 'disable' and _tp == 0 %}false{% elsif _a == 'raise_threshold' and _tp == 0 %}false{% else %}true{% endif %}"
            review_reason: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% assign _tp = steps.tp_alert_for_rule.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% if _tp > 0 %}tp_correlations_present{% elsif _a == 'tighten_query' or _a == 'lower_threshold' or _a == 'broaden_query' %}query_shape_change{% elsif _a == 'enable' %}projection_unknown{% else %}none{% endif %}"
            backtest_verdict: "{% assign _a = foreach.item._source.details.patch.action %}{% assign _tp = steps.tp_alert_for_rule.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 %}{% if _a == 'change_severity' or _a == 'change_risk_score' or _a == 'add_note' %}projection_safe{% elsif _a == 'disable' and _tp == 0 %}projection_safe{% elsif _a == 'raise_threshold' and _tp == 0 %}projection_safe{% elsif _a == 'enable' %}projection_unknown{% else %}projection_concerning{% endif %}"
            backtest_ref: "{{ steps.write_backtest.output._id | default: 'unknown' }}"
            confidence: "{{ foreach.item._source.confidence | default: 0 }}"

  # ── 3. Heartbeat ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: heartbeat
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: backtester_heartbeat
        source: "soc-rule-backtester"
        processed: "{{ steps.pending_backtests.output.hits.hits | size | default: 0 }}"
        pending_total: "{{ steps.pending_backtests.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Backtester tick complete — processed {{ steps.pending_backtests.output.hits.hits | size | default: 0 }} intents"

definition.name: SOC Rule Backtester
definition.description:
Projects the likely effect of a proposed rule mutation BEFORE the applier touches the rule. Scheduled every 1m. Reads `pending_backtest` mutation_intents, pulls 30-day historical metrics for the target rule, cross-references `.soc-outcomes` for true-positive impact, writes a row to `.soc-backtests`, and flips the mutation_intent status to one of:

  auto_apply_ready    -> backtest projects safely; applier will auto-land
  pending_review      -> projection concerning or unknown; exception queue
  rejected_backtest   -> projection unsafe (too much reduction or tp misses)

The applier's gate cascade then reads `verdict` directly — the backtester is the ONLY producer of backtest records. Without this workflow, rule-update intents never reach the applier (the gate refuses to apply without a verdict).
Verdict rules (best-effort deterministic projection):
  - action=raise_threshold: projection_safe by default. If any TP alert in the
    last 30d fired with `threshold_result.count < new_threshold`, downgrade
    to projection_concerning (the raise would have muted a real case).
  - action=lower_threshold: projection_concerning (increases volume).
  - action=tighten_query: projection_concerning (may miss TPs; needs review).
  - action=broaden_query: projection_concerning (increases volume).
  - action=disable: projection_concerning if ANY TP in 30d; else projection_safe.
  - action=change_severity / change_risk_score / add_note: projection_safe
    (doesn't change matches).

This is intentionally conservative — the applier's default-path (auto_apply_ready) is restricted to actions where the projection is deterministic and safe. Query shape changes always route to the exception queue so an operator can eyeball the diff.

version: '1'
name: SOC Response

enabled: true

triggers:

  - name: alert_data

  - name: log_response_start

  - name: log_response_done

results.name: SOC Regression Harvester
results.description: Periodically harvests confirmed TP/FP triage outcomes into the immutable .soc-regression-dataset. Every rejected or auto-closed-as-FP recommendation becomes a labelled regression case used by the regression gate before any autonomous mutation is allowed to land.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Regression Harvester
description: >
  Periodically harvests confirmed TP/FP triage outcomes into the immutable
  .soc-regression-dataset. Every rejected or auto-closed-as-FP recommendation
  becomes a labelled regression case used by the regression gate before any
  autonomous mutation is allowed to land.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 1h
  - type: manual

steps:
  # ── Gather recently-labelled outcomes: any triage with explicit disposition ──
  - name: get_labelled_outcomes
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-outcomes"
      size: 100
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-2h"
            - terms:
                disposition:
                  - "true_positive_high"
                  - "true_positive_low"
                  - "benign_positive"
                  - "auto_closed_fp"
            - term:
                harvested_for_regression:
                  value: false

  # ── Gather rejected recommendations — these are explicit negative training signals ──
  - name: get_rejected_recs
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      size: 100
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-2h"
            - term:
                status: "rejected"
            - term:
                harvested_for_regression:
                  value: false

  # ── Let the meta-agent turn outcomes into frozen regression cases ──
  - name: harvest_cases
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-meta-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        You are harvesting regression test cases from labelled triage outcomes and rejected recommendations.
        A regression case is a minimal, reproducible fixture (rule_id + alert fingerprint + expected disposition)
        that any future autonomous mutation MUST continue to satisfy.

        INPUT — labelled outcomes (first 100):
        {{ steps.get_labelled_outcomes.output.hits.hits | json }}

        INPUT — rejected recommendations (first 100):
        {{ steps.get_rejected_recs.output.hits.hits | json }}

        For each row:
          1. Extract rule_id, rule_name, alert_fingerprint, a minimal alert_sample (host/user/process only).
          2. Label with expected_disposition (from outcome.disposition) or derive from rejection reason.
          3. Emit ONE object per case with this exact shape:
             {
               "case_id": "reg_<rule_id>_<fingerprint_6>",
               "source_outcome_id": "<_id or null>",
               "source_triage_id": "<triage_id or null>",
               "rule_id": "...", "rule_name": "...",
               "alert_fingerprint": "...",
               "alert_sample": { "host_name": "...", "user_name": "...", "process_name": "..." },
               "expected_disposition": "...",
               "expected_confidence": 0.9,
               "expected_techniques": ["T1059"],
               "expected_next_step": "escalate_to_case",
               "labels": ["harvested","from-outcome"],
               "label_source": "triage_outcome",
               "frozen": true,
               "scenario_tag": "<rule_name short slug>"
             }

        Self-validate:
          - DO NOT emit duplicates (check fingerprint+rule_id across both inputs before output).
          - DO NOT emit a case when disposition is "unknown" or "suspicious_needs_hunt".
          - alert_sample must be <= 20 fields.

        Output ONLY a JSON array of case objects.
    timeout: 240s

  # ── Persist to regression dataset ──
  - name: write_cases
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-regression-dataset
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        harvest_run_id: "{{ execution.id }}"
        cases_raw: "{{ steps.harvest_cases.output | json }}"
        source_outcomes_count: "{{ steps.get_labelled_outcomes.output.hits.hits | size }}"
        source_rejections_count: "{{ steps.get_rejected_recs.output.hits.hits | size }}"
        notes:
          - "Raw harvest payload; the regression gate reads individual cases from the dataset after a downstream extractor flattens them."

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Regression Harvester: captured cases and stored to .soc-regression-dataset"
