results.name: SOC Regression Gate
results.description: The final gate every autonomous mutation passes through. Runs the proposed change against every frozen regression case and writes a pass/fail verdict to .soc-regression-runs. The soc-autonomous-applier blocks any mutation whose gate_result != 'pass'. Fully deterministic — no LLM involved in the gate decision itself; the agent only produces the per-case replay summary.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Regression Gate
description: >
  The final gate every autonomous mutation passes through. Runs the proposed
  change against every frozen regression case and writes a pass/fail verdict to
  .soc-regression-runs. The soc-autonomous-applier blocks any mutation whose
  gate_result != 'pass'. Fully deterministic — no LLM involved in the gate
  decision itself; the agent only produces the per-case replay summary.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: manual

inputs:
  - name: candidate_artifact_ref
    type: string
    required: true
  - name: candidate_definition_hash
    type: string
    required: true
  - name: baseline_artifact_ref
    type: string
    required: false
  - name: baseline_definition_hash
    type: string
    required: false
  - name: trigger
    type: string
    required: true

steps:
  # ── Fetch frozen dataset ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: get_cases
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-regression-dataset"
      size: 500
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term:
                frozen:
                  value: true

  # ── Replay: per case, have the candidate rule/agent produce a verdict,
  #     compare to expected_disposition and collect pass/fail counts. The
  #     agent is asked ONLY to simulate/predict; it does not mutate anything. ──
  - name: replay_candidate
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-meta-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        You are a DETERMINISTIC regression gate. Do NOT improvise or fix cases;
        score them.

        candidate_artifact_ref: {{ inputs.candidate_artifact_ref }}
        candidate_definition_hash: {{ inputs.candidate_definition_hash }}
        baseline_artifact_ref: {{ inputs.baseline_artifact_ref | default: 'n/a' }}
        trigger: {{ inputs.trigger }}

        Frozen regression cases (up to 500):
        {{ steps.get_cases.output.hits.hits | json }}

        For each case:
          1. Determine whether the candidate change would (a) still triage the case
             to its expected_disposition, and (b) still produce expected_next_step.
          2. Emit {"case_id","passed":true|false,"reason":"..."}.

        Then compute:
          passed_total, failed_total, regressions (failed that baseline previously passed).

        Gate rule:
          gate_result = "fail" if regressions > 0
          gate_result = "pass" otherwise

        Output ONLY:
          { "per_case": [...], "passed": N, "failed": N, "regressions": N,
            "regression_delta": 0.0, "gate_result": "pass"|"fail",
            "gate_reason": "<short>" }
    timeout: 420s

  # ── Persist gate outcome ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: write_run
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-regression-runs
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        run_id: "{{ execution.id }}"
        trigger: "{{ inputs.trigger }}"
        candidate_artifact_ref: "{{ inputs.candidate_artifact_ref }}"
        candidate_definition_hash: "{{ inputs.candidate_definition_hash }}"
        baseline_artifact_ref: "{{ inputs.baseline_artifact_ref | default: '' }}"
        baseline_definition_hash: "{{ inputs.baseline_definition_hash | default: '' }}"
        dataset_size: "{{ steps.get_cases.output.hits.hits | size }}"
        passed: "{{ steps.replay_candidate.output.passed | default: 0 }}"
        failed: "{{ steps.replay_candidate.output.failed | default: 0 }}"
        regressions: "{{ steps.replay_candidate.output.regressions | default: 0 }}"
        regression_delta: "{{ steps.replay_candidate.output.regression_delta | default: 0.0 }}"
        gate_result: "{{ steps.replay_candidate.output.gate_result | default: 'skipped' }}"
        gate_reason: "{{ steps.replay_candidate.output.gate_reason | default: 'replay returned no verdict' }}"
        per_case: "{{ steps.replay_candidate.output.per_case | default: [] }}"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Regression Gate: {{ steps.replay_candidate.output.gate_result | default: 'skipped' }} for {{ inputs.candidate_artifact_ref }}"

results.name: SOC Proactive Hunter
results.description: Scheduled proactive threat hunting workflow. Runs every 2 hours to: 1. Gather recent triage results and identify observed MITRE techniques 2. Run hypothesis-driven hunts for expected next-stage techniques 3. Run anomaly detection queries for behavioral deviations 4. Write findings to .soc-hunt-findings for dashboard and case creation
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Proactive Hunter
description: >
  Scheduled proactive threat hunting workflow. Runs every 2 hours to:
  1. Gather recent triage results and identify observed MITRE techniques
  2. Run hypothesis-driven hunts for expected next-stage techniques
  3. Run anomaly detection queries for behavioral deviations
  4. Write findings to .soc-hunt-findings for dashboard and case creation
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 2h
  - type: manual

steps:
  # ── Gather context for hunt planning ─────────────────────────────
  - name: get_recent_triage
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-triage-results"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-24h"
      size: 30
  - name: get_recent_alerts
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".alerts-security.alerts-*"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-24h"
      size: 0
      aggs:
        techniques:
          terms:
            field: "kibana.alert.rule.threat.technique.id"
            size: 30
        by_host:
          terms:
            field: "host.name"
            size: 20
          aggs:
            techniques:
              terms:
                field: "kibana.alert.rule.threat.technique.id"
                size: 10
        by_severity:
          terms:
            field: "kibana.alert.severity"
            size: 5

  - name: get_previous_hunts
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-hunt-findings"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-48h"
      size: 10
  - name: log_start
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Proactive Hunter: starting hunt cycle with {{ steps.get_recent_alerts.output.aggregations.techniques.buckets | size }} observed techniques"

  # Branch: full hypothesis+anomaly hunt when alerts exist, anomaly-only when not.
  - name: check_has_alerts
    type: if
    condition: "steps.get_recent_alerts.output.hits.total.value > 0"
    steps:
      - name: run_hunt
        type: ai.agent
        agent-id: soc-triage-agent
        connector-id: opus
        with:
          message: >
            You are conducting a proactive threat hunt using your proactive-hunt skill.
            This is NOT alert triage — you are hunting for threats that have NOT triggered alerts.

            CONTEXT:

            Observed MITRE techniques in last 24h (by host):
            {{ steps.get_recent_alerts.output.aggregations.by_host.buckets | json }}

            Alert severity distribution:
            {{ steps.get_recent_alerts.output.aggregations.by_severity.buckets | json }}

            Recent triage results count: {{ steps.get_recent_triage.output.hits.total.value }}
            (Use your search tools to query specific triage details as needed.)

            Previous hunts count: {{ steps.get_previous_hunts.output.hits.total.value }}
            (Use your search tools to check .soc-hunt-findings for recent hunts to avoid repeating.)

            INSTRUCTIONS:

            1. HYPOTHESIS-DRIVEN HUNTS:
               For each observed technique, identify the expected next-stage techniques using the
               ATT&CK chaining templates. Build ES|QL queries scoped to the same hosts/users
               where the original technique was observed.

            2. ANOMALY DETECTION:
               Run the standard anomaly queries:
               - New login sources (country/IP not seen in 30 days)
               - First-time process-parent relationships
               - Unusual outbound connections to new destinations
               - Data staging indicators (large files in temp directories)
               - Service account interactive logins

            3. SELF-VALIDATE:
               - Every hypothesis must have a query and result
               - Negative results are valuable — report them
               - Findings must reference specific entities and timeframes

            Respond with JSON:
            {"hunt_id": "hunt-<timestamp>", "hunt_type": "combined",
             "hypotheses": [{"technique_observed": "Txxxx", "technique_hunted": "Tyyyy",
               "host": "...", "query": "...", "result": "positive|negative", "evidence": "..."}],
             "anomaly_findings": [{"query_name": "...", "result_count": N, "findings": "..."}],
             "findings": [{"severity": "CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|INFO",
               "finding": "...", "entities_involved": [], "recommended_action": "..."}],
             "coverage_update": {"techniques_hunted": ["Txxxx"], "data_sources_used": []}}
        timeout: 600s
    else:
      - name: run_anomaly_only
        type: ai.agent
        agent-id: soc-triage-agent
        connector-id: opus
        with:
          message: >
            You are conducting a proactive anomaly detection hunt using your proactive-hunt skill.
            There are no recent alerts, so focus on data-driven anomaly detection:

            1. New login sources (country/IP not seen in 30 days)
            2. First-time process-parent relationships on production hosts
            3. Unusual outbound connections to never-seen destinations
            4. Data staging indicators (large files in temp directories)
            5. Service account interactive logins

            Previous hunts (avoid repeating):
            {{ steps.get_previous_hunts.output.hits.hits | json }}

            Self-validate: every query must produce a result (even if zero findings).

            Respond with JSON:
            {"hunt_id": "hunt-<timestamp>", "hunt_type": "anomaly_detection",
             "anomaly_findings": [{"query_name": "...", "result_count": N, "findings": "..."}],
             "findings": [{"severity": "CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|INFO",
               "finding": "...", "entities_involved": [], "recommended_action": "..."}],
             "coverage_update": {"data_sources_used": []}}
        timeout: 300s

  # ── Write findings ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Only one of run_hunt / run_anomaly_only runs; the other is undefined.
  # Liquid `| default:` falls through to the populated branch.
  - name: write_findings
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-hunt-findings
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        source: "soc-proactive-hunter"
        hunt_output: "{{ steps.run_hunt.output.message | default: steps.run_anomaly_only.output.message }}"
        status: "completed"

  - name: write_audit
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: "proactive_hunt"
        source: "soc-proactive-hunter"
        details: "Proactive threat hunt completed"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Proactive Hunter: hunt cycle complete, findings written to .soc-hunt-findings"

results.name: SOC Pipeline Run Telemetry Indexer (Event Log -> .soc-pipeline-runs)
results.description: Deterministically materialize SOC pipeline run telemetry into .soc-pipeline-runs from .kibana-event-log-* so watchdog can compute pipeline_runs_1h and pipeline_by_status_1h.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Pipeline Run Telemetry Indexer (Event Log -> .soc-pipeline-runs)
description: Deterministically materialize SOC pipeline run telemetry into .soc-pipeline-runs from .kibana-event-log-* so watchdog can compute pipeline_runs_1h and pipeline_by_status_1h.
enabled: true
triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 15m
  - type: manual
steps:
  - name: count_soc_exec_events_last_15m
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".kibana-event-log-*"
      size: 0
      track_total_hits: 1000000
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - range:
                "@timestamp":
                  gte: "now-15m"
            - query_string:
                query: "event.provider:alerting AND event.action:execute AND rule.name:SOC*"
      aggregations:
        by_outcome:
          terms:
            field: "event.outcome"
            size: 10
  - name: write_pipeline_run_telemetry
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-pipeline-runs
      id: "soc_pipeline_runs_{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M' }}"
      refresh: "wait_for"
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: soc_pipeline_runs_materialized
        window: "now-15m"
        pipeline:
          runs_total: "{{ steps.count_soc_exec_events_last_15m.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
          by_outcome: "{{ steps.count_soc_exec_events_last_15m.output.aggregations.by_outcome.buckets | json | default: '[]' }}"
          success_count: "{% assign _s = 0 %}{% for b in steps.count_soc_exec_events_last_15m.output.aggregations.by_outcome.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'success' %}{% assign _s = b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _s }}"
          failure_count: "{% assign _f = 0 %}{% for b in steps.count_soc_exec_events_last_15m.output.aggregations.by_outcome.buckets %}{% if b.key == 'failure' %}{% assign _f = b.doc_count %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ _f }}"
        source: "soc-pipeline-run-telemetry"

results.name: SOC Envelope Validator
results.description:
Post-write sweep for .soc-recommendations. Catches any mutation_intent doc that slipped past the soc-mutation-intent-envelope-validator ingest pipeline — e.g. bulk writes that explicitly disabled pipelines, docs indexed before the pipeline was deployed, or producer writes that bypassed the default_pipeline via `?pipeline=_none`. Belt-and-suspenders validation: the ingest pipeline is the primary gate at write time; this workflow is the periodic audit that guarantees the queue only ever contains valid mutation_intents in `pending` state.
Behavior per tick:
  1. Query .soc-recommendations for `type=mutation_intent AND status=pending`
     docs missing ANY required envelope field, or with `type != mutation_intent`.
     (The query uses pure Elasticsearch bool/should/must_not so validation logic
     lives in the query itself — no fragile Liquid-as-KQL conditions.)
  2. For each violating doc:
     a. Write a structured row to .soc-dead-letter (producer debuggability).
     b. Update the doc to status=rejected with rejection_reason=envelope_invalid
        so the applier skips it.
  3. Emit a heartbeat row to .soc-audit-trail with the invalid count so the
     System Health panel can surface it.

This workflow does NOT duplicate the applier's ownership / budget / cooldown / loop gates. Envelope validity is strictly a shape concern; the applier's gates are policy concerns.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Envelope Validator
description: >
  Post-write sweep for .soc-recommendations. Catches any mutation_intent doc that
  slipped past the soc-mutation-intent-envelope-validator ingest pipeline — e.g.
  bulk writes that explicitly disabled pipelines, docs indexed before the pipeline
  was deployed, or producer writes that bypassed the default_pipeline via
  `?pipeline=_none`. Belt-and-suspenders validation: the ingest pipeline is the
  primary gate at write time; this workflow is the periodic audit that guarantees
  the queue only ever contains valid mutation_intents in `pending` state.

  Behavior per tick:
    1. Query .soc-recommendations for `type=mutation_intent AND status=pending`
       docs missing ANY required envelope field, or with `type != mutation_intent`.
       (The query uses pure Elasticsearch bool/should/must_not so validation logic
       lives in the query itself — no fragile Liquid-as-KQL conditions.)
    2. For each violating doc:
       a. Write a structured row to .soc-dead-letter (producer debuggability).
       b. Update the doc to status=rejected with rejection_reason=envelope_invalid
          so the applier skips it.
    3. Emit a heartbeat row to .soc-audit-trail with the invalid count so the
       System Health panel can surface it.

  This workflow does NOT duplicate the applier's ownership / budget / cooldown /
  loop gates. Envelope validity is strictly a shape concern; the applier's gates
  are policy concerns.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 1m
  - type: manual

consts:
  max_per_tick: 50

steps:
  # ── 1. Find envelope-invalid docs via pure ES query ─────────────────
  # The `should` clauses enumerate every way a doc can be invalid. `minimum_should_match: 1`
  # turns the list into OR semantics. We intentionally do NOT encode enum-value checks
  # here (track ∈ {deterministic, agentic}, confidence ∈ [0,100], etc.) because enum
  # violations mean the ingest pipeline was bypassed entirely — catching "missing field"
  # is a superset check that catches the common producer bugs. The ingest pipeline
  # remains the authoritative enum validator.
  - name: invalid_docs
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      size: 50
      query:
        bool:
          filter:
            - term: { status: "pending" }
            - term: { type: "mutation_intent" }
          should:
            - bool: { must_not: [ { exists: { field: "rec_id" } } ] }
            - bool: { must_not: [ { exists: { field: "schema_version" } } ] }
            - bool: { must_not: [ { exists: { field: "source" } } ] }
            - bool: { must_not: [ { exists: { field: "title" } } ] }
            - bool: { must_not: [ { exists: { field: "summary" } } ] }
            - bool: { must_not: [ { exists: { field: "confidence" } } ] }
            - bool: { must_not: [ { exists: { field: "track" } } ] }
            - bool: { must_not: [ { exists: { field: "details" } } ] }
          minimum_should_match: 1

  # ── 2. Per-doc DLQ write + reject ────────────────────────────────────
  - name: dispatch_invalid
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.invalid_docs.output.hits.hits }}"
    steps:
      - name: dlq_write
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-dead-letter
          refresh: "wait_for"
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            source: "soc-envelope-validator"
            rec_id: "{{ foreach.item._source.rec_id | default: foreach.item._id }}"
            original_type: "{{ foreach.item._source.type | default: 'unknown' }}"
            error: "envelope_validation_failed_post_write_sweep: this doc bypassed the soc-mutation-intent-envelope-validator ingest pipeline. Check the producer for missing `?pipeline` param or explicit `?pipeline=_none`."
            validation_errors: ["post_write_sweep_detected_invalid_envelope"]
            original_doc: "{{ foreach.item._source | json }}"

      - name: mark_rejected
        type: elasticsearch.update
        with:
          index: .soc-recommendations
          id: "{{ foreach.item._id }}"
          refresh: "wait_for"
          doc:
            status: rejected
            applied_by: "soc-envelope-validator"
            applied_at: "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
            rejection_reason: "envelope_invalid_post_write_sweep"

  # ── 3. Heartbeat ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: heartbeat
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: envelope_validator_heartbeat
        source: "soc-envelope-validator"
        invalid_count: "{{ steps.invalid_docs.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"
        message: "Post-write envelope sweep complete. Invalid docs rerouted to .soc-dead-letter and marked rejected."

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Envelope-validator tick complete — invalid={{ steps.invalid_docs.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"

definition.name: SOC Envelope Validator
definition.description:
Post-write sweep for .soc-recommendations. Catches any mutation_intent doc that slipped past the soc-mutation-intent-envelope-validator ingest pipeline — e.g. bulk writes that explicitly disabled pipelines, docs indexed before the pipeline was deployed, or producer writes that bypassed the default_pipeline via `?pipeline=_none`. Belt-and-suspenders validation: the ingest pipeline is the primary gate at write time; this workflow is the periodic audit that guarantees the queue only ever contains valid mutation_intents in `pending` state.
Behavior per tick:
  1. Query .soc-recommendations for `type=mutation_intent AND status=pending`
     docs missing ANY required envelope field, or with `type != mutation_intent`.
     (The query uses pure Elasticsearch bool/should/must_not so validation logic
     lives in the query itself — no fragile Liquid-as-KQL conditions.)
  2. For each violating doc:
     a. Write a structured row to .soc-dead-letter (producer debuggability).
     b. Update the doc to status=rejected with rejection_reason=envelope_invalid
        so the applier skips it.
  3. Emit a heartbeat row to .soc-audit-trail with the invalid count so the
     System Health panel can surface it.

This workflow does NOT duplicate the applier's ownership / budget / cooldown / loop gates. Envelope validity is strictly a shape concern; the applier's gates are policy concerns.

document.error: envelope_validation_failed_post_write_sweep: this doc bypassed the soc-mutation-intent-envelope-validator ingest pipeline. Check the producer for missing `?pipeline` param or explicit `?pipeline=_none`.

document.message: Post-write envelope sweep complete. Invalid docs rerouted to .soc-dead-letter and marked rejected.

with.message: Envelope-validator tick complete — invalid={{ steps.invalid_docs.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}

results.name: SOC Case Creation
results.description: Creates Kibana security cases with structured evidence from the full triage pipeline.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Case Creation
description: Creates Kibana security cases with structured evidence from the full triage pipeline.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: manual

inputs:
  - name: investigation_result
    type: string
  - name: alert_data
    type: string

steps:
  - name: create_case
    type: kibana.request
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /api/cases
      body:
        title: "[SOC-AUTO] Security Incident - {{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        description: "## Autonomous SOC Case\n\n### Investigation Results\n{{ inputs.investigation_result }}\n\n### Alert Data\n{{ inputs.alert_data }}"
        tags:
          - soc-simulation
          - auto-generated
        severity: medium
        connector:
          id: none
          name: none
          type: ".none"
          fields: null
        settings:
          syncAlerts: true
        owner: securitySolution

  - name: write_case_outcome
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-outcomes
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        correlation_id: "case-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        disposition: "case_created"
        agents_involved: "soc-triage-agent,soc-entity-agent,soc-hunt-agent"

  - name: log_case
    type: console
    with:
      message: "SOC Case Creation complete: {{ steps.create_case.output | json }}"

results.name: SOC Architecture Reviewer
results.description: Scheduled architectural review of the AutoSOC mesh. Inventories all agents, skills, and workflows, gathers metrics, and uses the meta-agent with the architecture-review skill to identify consolidation opportunities and anti-patterns. Writes recommendations to .soc-recommendations for human review.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Architecture Reviewer
description: >
  Scheduled architectural review of the AutoSOC mesh. Inventories all agents, skills,
  and workflows, gathers metrics, and uses the meta-agent with the architecture-review
  skill to identify consolidation opportunities and anti-patterns. Writes recommendations
  to .soc-recommendations for human review.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 6h
  - type: manual

steps:
  # ── Inventory current components ─────────────────────────────────
  - name: get_agents
    type: kibana.request
    with:
      method: GET
      path: /api/agent_builder/agents

  - name: get_skills
    type: kibana.request
    with:
      method: GET
      path: /api/agent_builder/skills

  - name: get_evolution_log
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-evolution-log"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-7d"
      size: 50
  - name: get_metrics
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-metrics"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-7d"
      size: 100
  - name: get_recommendations
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-recommendations"
      query:
        range:
          "@timestamp":
            gte: "now-7d"
      size: 0
      aggs:
        by_source:
          terms:
            field: "source"
            size: 20
          aggs:
            statuses:
              terms:
                field: "status"
                size: 10

  - name: log_start
    type: console
    with:
      message: "Architecture Reviewer: starting periodic review"

  # ── Run architectural analysis ───────────────────────────────────
  - name: review
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-meta-agent
    connector-id: opus
    with:
      message: >
        Perform an architectural review of the AutoSOC mesh using your architecture-review skill.

        Analyze the current inventory for consolidation opportunities, anti-patterns,
        and structural improvements.

        INVENTORY:
        Agents: {{ steps.get_agents.output | json }}
        Skills: {{ steps.get_skills.output | json }}

        METRICS (7 days):
        Evolution log: {{ steps.get_evolution_log.output.hits.hits | json }}
        Pipeline metrics: {{ steps.get_metrics.output.hits.hits | json }}
        Recommendation stats: {{ steps.get_recommendations.output.aggregations | json }}

        IDEAL ARCHITECTURE:
        - soc-triage-agent: Unified classification + enrichment + investigation
        - soc-deteng-agent: Principal Detection Engineer — strategic rule authoring + coverage-gap closure + redesign of irredeemable rules
        - soc-signal-quality-agent: Tactical FP/TP tuning (exceptions, thresholds, last-resort disables)
        - soc-meta-agent: System evolution brain (skills for health-check, difficulty, arch-review)
        - soc-autonomous-applier-agent: Governance-gated applier for autosoc-owned mutations
        - soc-rec-applier-agent: Recommendation execution
        - Everything else: Deterministic workflows

        Evaluate all components against this ideal. Identify any meta-agent-created agents
        that should be converted to skills or workflows.

        Self-validate: every finding must include metrics-based justification.

        Respond with JSON:
        {
          "findings": [ { "area": "agents|skills|workflows|registries", "issue": "...", "severity": "low|med|high", "evidence": [...] } ],
          "summary":  "...",
          "intents":  [ /* ZERO or more mutation_intent objects — SAME envelope as soc-meta (title, summary, reasoning, confidence, track, housekeeping, expected_impact, evidence, details{artifact_type, artifact_id (auto-*), op, expected_ownership, reason, new_definition?, patch?, dependencies:[]}) */ ]
        }
    timeout: 600s

  # ── Write results ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: write_evolution_log
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-evolution-log
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        source: "soc-arch-reviewer"
        event_type: "architecture_review"
        review_output: "{{ steps.review.output | json }}"

  - name: write_recommendation
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-recommendations
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        rec_id: "arch-review-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M%S' }}"
        type: "architecture_review"
        source: "soc-arch-reviewer"
        source_doc_id: "{{ steps.write_evolution_log.output._id }}"
        status: "pending"
        title: "Architecture Review - {{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M' }}"
        summary: "{{ steps.review.output.message }}"
        details: "{{ steps.review.output | json }}"
        reasoning: "Periodic architectural review for consolidation opportunities"
        confidence: 70
        track: "agentic"
        expected_impact: "{{ steps.review.output.expected_impact }}"
        evidence: "{{ steps.review.output.evidence | default: [] }}"

  # ── Fan out concrete mutation intents (if any) ───────────────────
  - name: write_mutation_intents
    type: foreach
    foreach: "{{ steps.review.output.intents }}"
    steps:
      - name: write_intent
        type: elasticsearch.index
        with:
          index: .soc-recommendations
          document:
            "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ' }}"
            rec_id: "arch-mi-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y%m%d%H%M%S' }}-{{ foreach.index }}"
            schema_version: 2
            type: "mutation_intent"
            source: "soc-arch-reviewer"
            source_doc_id: "{{ steps.write_evolution_log.output._id }}"
            status: "pending"
            title: "{{ foreach.item.title }}"
            summary: "{{ foreach.item.summary }}"
            reasoning: "{{ foreach.item.reasoning | default: 'Architectural consolidation' }}"
            confidence: "{{ foreach.item.confidence | default: 70 }}"
            track: "{{ foreach.item.track | default: 'agentic' }}"
            housekeeping: "{{ foreach.item.housekeeping | default: false }}"
            expected_impact: "{{ foreach.item.expected_impact | default: empty }}"
            evidence: "{{ foreach.item.evidence | default: empty }}"
            details: "{{ foreach.item.details }}"

  - name: log_done
    type: console
    with:
      message: >-
        Architecture Reviewer: review complete; findings written and
        {{ steps.review.output.intents | size | default: 0 }} mutation intent(s) dispatched.

name: Test Foreach

  - type: manual

  - name: make_array

item index={{ foreach.index }}

results.name: SOC Watchdog Health Report Extractor
results.description: Snapshot the latest soc-watchdog health_report into .soc-audit-trail.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Watchdog Health Report Extractor
description: Snapshot the latest soc-watchdog health_report into .soc-audit-trail.
enabled: true
triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 1h
steps:
  - name: get_latest_watchdog
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: ".soc-coverage-gaps*"
      body:
        size: 1
        sort:
          - "@timestamp": "desc"
        _source:
          - "@timestamp"
          - "source"
          - "health_report"
          - "message"
        query:
          bool:
            filter:
              - term:
                  source: "soc-watchdog"
              - range:
                  "@timestamp":
                    gte: "now-24h"
  - name: write_watchdog_snapshot
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: soc_watchdog_health_report_snapshot
        watchdog:
          total_matches_24h: "{{ steps.get_latest_watchdog.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"

results.description: Deterministically verify the SOC dead-letter data stream exists and write a heartbeat to .soc-audit-trail.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Dead-letter Existence & Heartbeat
description: Deterministically verify the SOC dead-letter data stream exists and write a heartbeat to .soc-audit-trail.

triggers:
  - type: scheduled

      every: 1h

  - name: check_dead_letter

      body:
        size: 0
        track_total_hits: true

        event_type: soc_dead_letter_heartbeat
        dead_letter:
          exists_and_queryable: true
          total_hits_24h: "{{ steps.check_dead_letter.output.hits.total.value | default: 0 }}"

results.name: SOC Agent Health Telemetry Probe
results.description: Deterministically verify whether .soc-agent-health* is receiving any documents and log the result to .soc-audit-trail for watchdog/ops follow-up.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Agent Health Telemetry Probe
description: Deterministically verify whether .soc-agent-health* is receiving any documents and log the result to .soc-audit-trail for watchdog/ops follow-up.
enabled: true
triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 1h
  - type: manual
steps:
  - name: agent_health_last_30m
    type: elasticsearch.search
    with:
      index: .soc-agent-health*
      body:
        size: 0
        query:
          range:
            "@timestamp":
              gte: "now-30m"
              lt: "now"
        aggs:
          total_docs:
            value_count:
              field: "@timestamp"
          has_throughput:
            filter:
              exists:
                field: throughput
          has_latency_p50:
            filter:
              exists:
                field: latency_p50
          has_latency_p95:
            filter:
              exists:
                field: latency_p95
          has_error_rate:
            filter:
              exists:
                field: error_rate
  - name: write_probe_result
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: agent_health_telemetry_probe
        source: soc-meta-agent
        time_window:
          from: now-30m
          to: now
        agent_health_index_pattern: .soc-agent-health*
        result:
          aggregations: "{{ steps.agent_health_last_30m.aggregations | json }}"
        notes:
          - "Watchdog reports .soc-agent-health telemetry is missing, preventing deterministic STALLED/DEGRADED/FAILING evaluation via throughput/latency/error thresholds."
          - "This probe produces a trendable signal (docs present vs absent; key fields present vs absent) without LLM reasoning."

          total:
            value_count:
              field: "@timestamp"
          has_triage_output:
            filter:
              exists:
                field: triage_output
          triage_output_contains_object_object:
            filter:
              match_phrase:
                triage_output: "[object Object]"
          triage_output_contains_false_positive:
            filter:
              match_phrase:
                triage_output: "FALSE_POSITIVE"
          triage_output_contains_true_positive:
            filter:
              match_phrase:
                triage_output: "TRUE_POSITIVE"
          triage_output_contains_t1033:
            filter:
              match_phrase:
                triage_output: "T1033"
          has_structured_classification:
            filter:
              exists:
                field: classification
          has_structured_confidence:
            filter:
              exists:
                field: confidence
          has_structured_alert_id:
            filter:
              exists:
                field: alert_id
  - name: write_snapshot
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-audit-trail
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        event_type: triage_output_normalization_snapshot
        source: soc-meta-agent
        time_window:
          from: now-24h
          to: now
        triage_results_index_pattern: .soc-triage-results*
        aggregations: "{{ steps.triage_results_schema_snapshot.aggregations | json }}"
        notes:
          - "Watchdog reports KPI/coverage blind spots because triage classifications/confidence/techniques are often embedded in triage_output JSON strings rather than structured fields."
          - "This workflow produces a trendable, deterministic signal to drive ingest parsing/normalization work (no LLM required)."

definition.name: SOC Triage Output Normalization Snapshot
definition.description: Deterministically measure how much triage data is embedded in triage_output (unqueryable JSON strings) vs available as structured fields, and log the result for KPI/coverage remediation.

notes: Watchdog reports KPI/coverage blind spots because triage classifications/confidence/techniques are often embedded in triage_output JSON strings rather than structured fields.
This workflow produces a trendable, deterministic signal to drive ingest parsing/normalization work (no LLM required).

results.name: SOC Enrichment
results.description: Entity enrichment pipeline. Enriches triage results with entity context, writes outcome, and routes to investigation.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Enrichment
description: Entity enrichment pipeline. Enriches triage results with entity context, writes outcome, and routes to investigation.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: manual

inputs:
  - name: triage_result
    type: string
  - name: alert_data
    type: string

steps:
  - name: enrich
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-entity-agent
    connector-id: gpt
    with:
      message: >
        Enrich this triage result with deep entity context.
        Use ES|QL to fetch risk scores, 7-day behavioral baselines, and entity relationships.
        Check SML for cached baselines. Write updated baselines to SML via sml_attach.
        After adjusting the confidence, determine next_step:
        - confidence >= 70 → "response" (confirmed TP, ready for containment)
        - confidence 40-69 → "investigation" (ambiguous, needs deep hunt)
        - confidence < 40 → "close" (likely FP after enrichment)

        Triage result:
        {{ inputs.triage_result }}

        Original alert data:
        {{ inputs.alert_data }}
    timeout: 300s

  - name: write_enrichment
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-entity-enrichment
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        source: "soc-enrichment"
        hop_count: "2"
        enrichment_output: "{{ steps.enrich.output | json }}"

  - name: write_outcome
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-outcomes
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        correlation_id: "enrich-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        disposition: "enriched"
        agents_involved: "soc-triage-agent,soc-entity-agent"

  - name: log_result
    type: console
    with:
      message: "SOC Enrichment complete: {{ steps.enrich.output | json }}"

definition.name: SOC Enrichment
definition.description: Entity enrichment pipeline. Enriches triage results with entity context, writes outcome, and routes to investigation.

with.message: SOC Enrichment complete: {{ steps.enrich.output | json }}

results.name: SOC Investigation
results.description: Deep threat hunting for ambiguous alerts (confidence 40-69). Uses Hunt Agent for deep analysis.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Investigation
description: Deep threat hunting for ambiguous alerts (confidence 40-69). Uses Hunt Agent for deep analysis.
enabled: true

triggers:
  - type: manual

inputs:
  - name: enriched_data
    type: string
  - name: alert_data
    type: string

steps:
  - name: hunt
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-hunt-agent
    connector-id: gpt
    with:
      message: >
        Deep investigation for an ambiguous alert (confidence 40-69 after enrichment).
        1) Run broad ES|QL scans for the involved hosts, users, IPs over the past 24 hours
        2) Look for lateral movement, C2 beaconing, data staging, or privilege escalation patterns
        3) Check SML for similar past investigations and known TTPs
        4) Correlate with any recent triage results or entity enrichments
        5) Determine final confidence and next_step:
           - confidence >= 70 → "response" (confirmed threat)
           - confidence 40-69 → "case" (still uncertain but should be tracked)
           - confidence < 40 → "close" (cleared after deep investigation)

        Enriched data:
        {{ inputs.enriched_data }}

        Original alert:
        {{ inputs.alert_data }}
    timeout: 300s

  - name: write_investigation
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-investigation-findings
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        source: "soc-investigation"
        hop_count: "3"
        investigation_output: "{{ steps.hunt.output | json }}"

  - name: write_outcome
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-outcomes
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        correlation_id: "hunt-{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        disposition: "investigated"
        agents_involved: "soc-triage-agent,soc-entity-agent,soc-hunt-agent"

  - name: log_result
    type: console
    with:
      message: "SOC Investigation complete: {{ steps.hunt.output | json }}"

definition.name: SOC Investigation
definition.description: Deep threat hunting for ambiguous alerts (confidence 40-69). Uses Hunt Agent for deep analysis.

with.message: SOC Investigation complete: {{ steps.hunt.output | json }}

results.name: SOC Preflight
results.description: Preflight checks for SOC monitoring prerequisites (index access, dead-letter presence, and common ES blockers) and logs structured blockers.
results.yaml:
version: '1'
name: SOC Preflight
description: Preflight checks for SOC monitoring prerequisites (index access, dead-letter presence, and common ES blockers) and logs structured blockers.
enabled: true
triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 15m
  - type: manual
steps:
  - name: invoke
    type: ai.agent
    agent-id: soc-preflight-agent
    connector-id: gpt
    with:
      message: "Run SOC preflight checks now. Probe required SOC indices/patterns for existence and accessibility. If any blocker is found (security_exception indices:admin/resolve/index, remote_cluster_client missing, dead-letter missing, alerts index missing), write a structured health_report document to .soc-coverage-gaps. Return your JSON output."
    timeout: 300s
  - name: log
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: .soc-agent-outputs
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ 'now' | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        agent_id: soc-preflight-agent
        output: "{{ steps.invoke.output | json }}"

definition.name: SOC Preflight
definition.description: Preflight checks for SOC monitoring prerequisites (index access, dead-letter presence, and common ES blockers) and logs structured blockers.

with.message: Run SOC preflight checks now. Probe required SOC indices/patterns for existence and accessibility. If any blocker is found (security_exception indices:admin/resolve/index, remote_cluster_client missing, dead-letter missing, alerts index missing), write a structured health_report document to .soc-coverage-gaps.
